title: Automated Tree Knowledge Graph Construction using Ontology Expansion and Retrieval from Vietnamese History Textbooks
abstract: Hierarchical Knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful approach for supporting large language models with structured knowledge. However, there are primary challenges: (i) the lack of methods for automatic KG construction using ontology expansion for low-resource languages such as Vietnamese, (ii) the absence of systematic evaluation for knowledge retrieval strategies leveraging the hierarchical structures. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end pipeline for KG construction and retrieval strategies evaluation. In the KG construction, we employ a three-phase hybrid relation extraction pipeline: intra-batch deduplication via Union-Find, approximate cross-batch search, and LLM extraction with a centroid filter that reduces prompts combined with a five-step dual-LLM validator to prevent bloated ontology. A two-tier architecture consists of unmergeable structural nodes to preserve the document structure and mergeable content nodes. The retrieval evaluation consists of three graph traversal strategies: Top-Down, Horizontal, and Bottom-Up, which are evaluated on a synthetically generated benchmark of 1,210 Vietnamese queries from 109 subgraphs, categorized by five query directions. In this paper, we construct the tree knowledge graph from Vietnamese high school History textbooks (nearly 400 pages) to produce 750 nodes and 4,341 semantic edges with controlled ontology growth from 40 to 41 types. Among experimental graph traversal strategies, the Top-Down strategy with structure surpasses the vector baseline by 4.7 percentage points in NDCG@10. As a result, tree-structural information provides valuable information beyond flat cosine similarity but degrades performance when the query does not require structural context.

title: ADAPTIVE REPRESENTATION LEARNING FOR ROBUST ANOMALY DETECTION IN NON-STATIONARY MULTISOURCE DATA STREAMS
abstract: Abstract Anomaly detection in multisource data streams becomes substantially more difficult when the underlying data-generating process is non-stationary. A pattern considered abnormal at one time can become part of normal operation after a regime transition, while previously typical observations can acquire anomalous significance under changed system conditions. Simultaneously, heterogeneous sources may differ in temporal resolution, noise structure, feature dimensionality, missingness, reliability, and semantic content. Static anomaly detectors trained on a fixed historical distribution therefore tend to lose calibration as both representation and decision boundaries become obsolete. This study develops a conceptual framework for adaptive representation learning aimed at robust anomaly detection in non-stationary multisource streams. The analysis distinguishes genuine anomalies from concept drift, recurrent regimes, transient disturbances, sensor degradation, and source-specific distribution shifts. Representation learning is treated as a dynamic process in which latent features must preserve anomaly-relevant information while adapting selectively to legitimate evolution of normal behaviour. Classical anomaly-detection principles establish the importance of defining normality relative to context rather than relying solely on global rarity [1]. Concept-drift research further demonstrates that online learning systems require explicit mechanisms for detecting and responding to changes in the underlying distribution [2]. Adaptive windows provide one practical means of controlling the temporal horizon over which current behaviour is estimated [3]. For multisource environments, additional challenges arise from asynchronous observations and unequal source reliability, requiring representation architectures that can integrate shared information without suppressing source-specific anomalies. Robust adaptation is therefore formulated as a balance among memory, plasticity, contamination resistance, and uncertainty. Deep and shallow anomaly-detection paradigms are considered jointly, with particular attention to latent-space stability, reconstruction-based scoring, support estimation, and adaptive thresholding.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Critical Survey Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Graphical Model Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to learning probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) by dynamically adapting their structure based on the underlying data distribution. Traditional PGM learning often relies on pre-defined structures, which may not always capture the intricate relationships present in complex datasets. Our method, Adaptive Probabilistic Graphical Model Learning (APGML), leverages Bayesian inference and variational inference techniques, coupled with gradient descent optimization, to automatically adjust the model's topology – specifically, the nodes and edges – during the learning process. The core claim is that this adaptive approach leads to a more precise representation of the data and improved model accuracy. We introduce a framework that iteratively refines the PGM structure, driven by the data, ultimately resulting in a model that better reflects the underlying dependencies. This work addresses a significant challenge in PGM learning: the selection of an appropriate graph structure – a problem often tackled through manual design or heuristic search algorithms – by allowing the model to evolve based on the observed data. We outline the key components of the APGML algorithm, including the variational inference process, the structural adaptation mechanism, and the optimization strategy.

title: Quantum Topology for Adaptive Quantum Computation Validation
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel field of physics, offers a unique framework for validating quantum computations. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum topology to dynamically adjust parameters within a quantum computing algorithm, thereby enhancing computational accuracy and stability. We introduce a novel self-adaptive validation framework based on topological invariants, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary results. The core mechanism involves quantifying the system's topological properties and using this information to iteratively refine quantum parameter adjustments, ensuring a robust and reliable computation. This work represents a significant step toward automated quantum verification, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum algorithm development and error mitigation.

title: ## Central Andes Thomasomys: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Behavioral Adaptations
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the "Thomasomys Adaptation Algorithm" (TAA), inspired by the behavioral adaptations observed in *Thomasomys* rodents of the Central Andes. These rodents exhibit remarkable foraging strategies and navigation skills within complex, unpredictable environments. The TAA leverages these observed behaviors – particularly the dynamic adjustment of search strategies based on environmental feedback – to construct a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm incorporates elements of adaptive step size control, dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a novel representation of the solution space based on a weighted sum of heuristic indicators derived from the observed rodent behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the TAA through simulations targeting several benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that the TAA performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms, showcasing its potential for tackling challenging optimization tasks where adaptability and environmental awareness are crucial. The key innovations of the TAA lie in its biologically-inspired approach and the ability to dynamically adjust its search parameters based on the perceived success of previous iterations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of problem types, including continuous, discrete, and combinatorial optimization.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Feature Selection for High-Dimensional Data
abstract: Quantum-enhanced feature selection is a promising approach to address the challenges posed by high-dimensional data in machine learning. Traditional feature selection methods often struggle to effectively identify the most informative features, leading to suboptimal model performance and increased computational cost. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm designed to accelerate and enhance feature selection, offering a significant improvement over existing techniques. We explore the potential of quantum algorithms, specifically focusing on Grover's search algorithm and quantum-enhanced k-means clustering, to achieve efficient identification of relevant features. The core mechanism involves exploiting quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to enhance the search space and improve the selection process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing its potential to reduce computational cost and improve accuracy in high-dimensional feature selection scenarios.

title: Self-Organizing Maps for Anomaly Detection in Streaming Data
abstract: This paper explores the application of Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) for anomaly detection within streaming data environments. The primary challenge in anomaly detection lies in the scarcity of labeled data, a common issue when dealing with continuous data streams. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing SOMs to autonomously learn the normal patterns within the stream. Anomalies are then identified by quantifying the deviation of incoming data points from their closest representation on the learned SOM map. The core of the method centers around the distance metric between data points and their nearest neighbors on the map. This approach offers a viable solution for real-time anomaly detection without requiring pre-labeled datasets. The effectiveness of this methodology is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for diverse streaming data applications.

title: Title: Adaptive Information Theory for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum information processing is exceptionally sensitive to errors, posing a significant challenge to the development of practical quantum technologies. Conventional error correction codes, while effective, often rely on pre-defined error profiles that may not accurately represent the true error distribution within a quantum system. This research investigates an adaptive information theory framework designed to dynamically adjust error correction parameters based on the specific error profile of the quantum system, thereby improving error detection and resilience. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors the error rate and optimizes the correction parameters to minimize the impact of errors. The proposed approach offers a more flexible and potentially superior solution compared to static error correction methods, addressing a key limitation in current quantum error correction strategies. This work explores the design of a novel system that can adapt to varying error characteristics, leading to enhanced robustness and improved performance in quantum information processing.

title: Self-Adaptive Neural Network Control Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel self-adaptive neural network control algorithm. Traditional neural networks often rely on fixed parameters, rendering them inadequate for dynamic systems. This research proposes a method leveraging the inherent self-adaptivity of neural networks to dynamically adjust network weights, thereby optimizing system performance and stability. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously assesses the system's state and adjusts the network's weights in response, ensuring optimal performance. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, parameterization, and validation through a series of simulations and experiments. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in performance metrics compared to conventional control strategies.

title: Quantum-Inspired Randomized Response for Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to privacy-preserving data analysis termed Quantum-Inspired Randomized Response (QIRR). Traditional privacy-preserving techniques, such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, frequently necessitate substantial computational resources, presenting limitations in scalability and real-time applications. QIRR leverages concepts derived from quantum measurement theory – specifically, the probabilistic collapse phenomenon – to provide a computationally efficient solution. The core principle involves a randomized response strategy where an individual answers a query in a way that obscures their true response, while still allowing for aggregate analysis. We formalize this approach with a mathematical framework, outlining the key parameters and processes involved. The system is designed to minimize computational overhead, offering a practical alternative to existing methods. This work demonstrates a viable pathway for integrating quantum-inspired ideas into data privacy, potentially enabling more accessible and scalable privacy-preserving analytics. The system utilizes a Bernoulli distribution to model the randomization process, and the final result is derived through weighted averaging based on the responses. We explore the impact of varying parameters on privacy guarantees and analytical accuracy.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Evolutionary Algorithms (QEAs) represent a novel approach to optimization, aiming to significantly accelerate the evolution of complex, high-dimensional evolutionary algorithms. This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to enhance the optimization process, focusing on leveraging quantum properties such as superposition and entanglement to accelerate exploration of the search space and improve convergence. We detail the core mechanism of QEAs, outlining the key design choices and theoretical underpinnings. The paper argues that the integration of quantum elements can provide a substantial performance advantage over classical approaches, particularly for problems exhibiting complex, high-dimensional landscapes. The research will demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, emphasizing the potential for enhanced search efficiency and robustness.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Causal Reasoning
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have achieved significant success in representing graph structures for various downstream tasks. However, a critical limitation of current approaches is their inability to effectively model the temporal dynamics inherent in evolving graphs. This paper introduces a novel framework for temporal graph embedding that explicitly incorporates causal reasoning. We propose a method that combines standard graph structure with a causal Bayesian network representation, allowing us to learn node embeddings that maximize the likelihood of observed graph transitions, given the learned causal model. This approach enables the representation of temporal dependencies and facilitates reasoning about "what-if" scenarios, addressing a fundamental gap in existing graph embedding methodologies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example.

title: ## Blaubok: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Blaubok*
abstract: This paper presents Blaubok, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Blaubok* (a hypothetical, social insect-like creature). *Blaubok* exhibits a unique strategy of collaborative exploration and localized decision-making within a group, followed by periodic aggregation and information sharing. Blaubok leverages these principles to develop a new algorithm, Blaubok-Metaheuristic, designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates a population-based search, a novel communication mechanism simulating *Blaubok's* aggregation behavior, and a dynamic adjustment of individual exploration and exploitation strategies based on the aggregated information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Blaubok-Metaheuristic on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that Blaubok-Metaheuristic offers a robust and adaptable approach to tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Black-tailed Gerbil Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Black-tailed Gerbil Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Black-tailed Gerbil Algorithm (BTGA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Gerbillus clanianus*, commonly known as the black-tailed gerbil. Gerbils exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating food sources in complex environments, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. BTGA mimics these behaviors through a novel population-based search process incorporating adaptive movement patterns, resource assessment, and social learning. The algorithm employs a dynamic agent representation, where each agent simulates a gerbil exploring the search space. Agents' movement is governed by a stochastic rule based on environmental cues and their own past experiences. Resource assessment is performed using a weighted average of local neighborhood evaluations. Social learning is implemented through a mechanism where agents preferentially adopt movements from successful neighbors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BTGA on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and Brent's patuitary function. The results indicate that BTGA achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in problems with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for various optimization challenges.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Historical Development Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Process of Marketing Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
abstract: Purpose: The primary objective of this study was to determine how the use of artificial intelligence tools affects the efficiency of marketing management in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Poland, based on original research.To achieve this objective, the study identified the marketing areas where artificial intelligence (AI) is most frequently employed, assessed entrepreneurs' awareness and knowledge regarding AI, analyzed the benefits, barriers, and limitations associated with its implementation, evaluated the impact of AI usage on operational efficiency, and outlined prospects for future development.Design/Methodology/Approach: This study employs a survey-based research method using a questionnaire.The questionnaire was designed to gather information on the extent to which enterprises use artificial intelligence tools in their marketing activities, the assessment of their effectiveness, the marketing areas supported by AI technologies, and the barriers and challenges associated with implementing these solutions in practice.Findings: The results clearly indicate that AI is no longer merely an experimental technology but has become one of the most common optimization tools.High levels of awareness and implementation of AI tools within enterprises were also observed.SME managers view AI as a key element in building a competitive advantage, enabling them to bridge the resource gap vis-à-vis large corporations.The dominant model of AI adoption is task automation.The popularity of using AI for content creation, managing marketing campaigns, and data analysis suggests that the technology is viewed primarily as a tool for automating tasks.The main benefit for organizations is not a direct reduction in financial costs-in this regard, the gains for the enterprise are usually negligible or minor.However, the radical optimization of working time is the primary driver behind the popularity of AI tools.Current trends in how these tools are implemented within enterprises suggest that the approach to human resource utilization may undergo a significant shift in the coming years, with a growing trend of moving personnel away from routine tasks toward conceptual or strategic activities.Practical Implications: Leveraging AI in marketing management within SMEs significantly boosts effectiveness and improves overall business performance.However, success in this area will increasingly depend not merely on the technology itself, but on the organization's ability to adapt and educate itself in order to avoid falling behind in the digital landscape.

title: Machine learning-enhanced modified early warning system for predicting in-hospital mortality on pulmonary ward
abstract: Background: Early recognition of impending systemic failure and timely delivery of appropriate medical care are critical for effective clinical intervention. The Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) is widely used to identify patients at risk of clinical deterioration. However, as patient complexity increases—driven by advanced age, multimorbidity, and other risk factors—automated warning systems often generate excessive alerts, leading to high false-alarm rates. Therefore, we aim to develop and validate a machine learning-enhanced predictive model (MEWS+) to detect critical in-hospital mortality risk factors earlier, thereby supporting clinical decision-making and optimizing acute care triage on pulmonary wards. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 4,108 consecutive adult patients admitted to the pulmonary wards of a medical center between January and June 2021. Four machine learning (ML) frameworks—extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest, logistic regression, and support vector machine—were trained and evaluated using an 80:20 data split. Pairwise nonparametric Spearman rank correlation was used to assess associations between baseline predictors and in-hospital mortality. Results: Among the 4,108 patients included, the cohort was predominantly elderly (60.6% aged ≥65 years) and female (61.6%), with males accounting for 38.4%. The baseline in-hospital mortality rate was 5.4%, representing 222 empirical mortality events. Spearman correlation analysis showed that the recalculated traditional MEWS score had the strongest positive monotonic association with in-hospital mortality (ρs =0.430, P<0.05), followed by signed do-not-resuscitate (DNR) status (ρs =0.383, P<0.05), MEWS time (ρs =0.292, P<0.05), and age (ρs =0.204, P<0.05). In contrast, chronic comorbidities demonstrated very weak correlations (heart failure: ρs =0.079; hypertension: ρs =0.035). On the independent testing set, the XGBoost classifier achieved the highest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.970 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.944–0.990], sensitivity of 0.872 (95% CI: 0.743–0.952), and specificity of 0.972 (95% CI: 0.957–0.982). Feature-importance analysis indicated that the MEWS score (0.402), signed DNR status (0.194), and MEWS time (0.136) were the primary contributors to model performance. Conclusions: An ML-enhanced MEWS+ model by effectively balancing clinical sensitivity and operational precision, by integrating acute physiological indicators with advanced directives and demographic factors, the XGBoost-based MEWS+ system provides highly accurate, individualized early-warning triage to strengthen clinical safety on general hospital wards.

title: Thought-Mediated Learning: From Deliberative Reasoning to Automatic Behavior
abstract: Autonomous agents require not only deliberate reasoning for unfamiliar situations but also the ability to convert repeatedly useful reasoning into efficient automatic behavior. However, existing LLM-based agents and knowledge-distillation approaches generally couple reasoning and learning through predefined training objectives or direct teacher--student supervision, leaving unclear how an agent can autonomously determine what should become learned behavior. This paper proposes Thought-Mediated Learning (TML), a framework that separates LLM-based deliberative thinking from an independent ML/DL background learning process. Thinking cannot directly update the automatic model; instead, it produces thought materials whose content and frequency determine what becomes available for learning. Repeated thinking implicitly strengthens important experiences, attention determines which factors are represented, jointly considered events may create spurious associations, and imagined experiences can provide learning materials before corresponding real events occur. Observed outcomes further generate corrective materials that revise previously learned automatic behavior. Experimental results show that TML achieves 96.67% hidden-pattern acquisition and 99.93% post-learning automatic accuracy, reaches 97.83% OOD (out-of-distribution) accuracy versus 9.50% for raw learning, and improves zero-real rare-case success to 59.38% while corrective learning raises final hidden-case success to 96.82%.

title: Συστηματική υποβοήθηση νεοφυών επιχειρήσεων με χρήση τεχνικών τεχνητής νοημοσύνης
abstract: Η παρούσα διδακτορική διατριβή εξετάζει το πρόβλημα της συστηματικής υποβοήθησης και αξιολόγησης νεοφυών επιχειρήσεων (startups) με τη χρήση τεχνικών Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης. Οι νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις πρώιμου σταδίου (early stage startups) λειτουργούν υπό συνθήκες αυξημένης αβεβαιότητας, περιορισμένων οικονομικών και ανθρώπινων πόρων και άνισης πρόσβασης σε εξειδικευμένη καθοδήγηση. Οι παραδοσιακοί μηχανισμοί υποστήριξης, όπως οι σύμβουλοι, οι θερμοκοιτίδες και οι επιταχυντές, παρέχουν σημαντική εμπειρογνωμοσύνη, αλλά περιορίζονται ως προς το κόστος, τη διαθεσιμότητα και τη δυνατότητα κλιμάκωσης. Παράλληλα όμως, η διάδοση της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης και των Μεγάλων Γλωσσικών Μοντέλων (LLMs) δημιουργεί αναντίλεκτα νέες δυνατότητες για παροχή καθοδήγησης κατά απαίτηση, χωρίς όμως να επιλύει αυτομάτως το πρόβλημα. Η χρήση μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού (LLMs) σε ρόλο συμβούλου ή αυτόνομου αξιολογητή συνοδεύεται, λόγω του τρόπου λειτουργίας τους, από παραισθήσεις (hallucinations), εξάρτηση από στατικά δεδομένα, τάση συγκατάβασης προς τις υποθέσεις του χρήστη (sycophancy), αστάθεια της βαθμολόγησης και περιορισμένη προσαρμογή τόσο στο στάδιο ανάπτυξης όσο και στο επιχειρηματικό πλαίσιο κάθε startup. Σκοπός της διατριβής είναι ο σχεδιασμός, η υλοποίηση και η εμπειρική αξιολόγηση ενός ολοκληρωμένου υπολογιστικού τεχνουργήματος, του Evaluator.GR, το οποίο υποστηρίζει συστηματικά τη διαδρομή μιας νεοφυούς επιχείρησης από τη διαμόρφωση και την επικύρωση της αρχικής ιδέας έως την προετοιμασία για χρηματοδότηση και την επενδυτική ετοιμότητα. Η έρευνα δεν αντιμετωπίζει την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη ως συνολικό υποκατάστατο του ανθρώπινου μέντορα, αξιολογητή ή επενδυτή, αλλά ως υποδομή υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης και αυτοματοποίησης επιμέρους εργασιών, με έμφαση στην αξιοπιστία, στην τεκμηρίωση, στην επεξηγησιμότητα και στην υπεύθυνη χρήση. Ως κύριο μεθοδολογικό πλαίσιο υιοθετήθηκε η Έρευνα Επιστήμης Σχεδιασμού (Design Science Research), μέσω των αλληλοτροφοδοτούμενων Κύκλων Συνάφειας, Σχεδιασμού και Αυστηρότητας. Στον Κύκλο Συνάφειας πραγματοποιήθηκε Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων, η οποία χαρτογράφησε τις εφαρμογές, τις συνθήκες απόδοσης και τους περιορισμούς της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης (generative AI) στην καθοδήγηση και αξιολόγηση startups. Τα αναγνωρισμένα ερευνητικά κενά μετασχηματίστηκαν, στον Κύκλο Σχεδιασμού, σε λειτουργικές και αρχιτεκτονικές απαιτήσεις του Evaluator.GR. Στον Κύκλο Αυστηρότητας, το τεχνούργημα αξιολογήθηκε μέσω συγκριτικής μελέτης έναντι μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού και μέσω πιλοτικής εφαρμογής σε πραγματικές νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις.Το υπολογιστικό τεχνούργημα (artifact) που αναπτύχθηκε είναι το Evaluator.GR, μια πολυαρθρωτή πλατφόρμα αξιολόγησης, στρατηγικής υποστήριξης και παραγωγής επιχειρηματικών παραδοτέων. Η αρχιτεκτονική του συνδυάζει Μίξη Ειδικών σε επίπεδο συστήματος (System-Level Mixture of Experts), τριπλό αξιολογητή και επιπροσθέτως μηχανισμό Μετα-Αξιολογητή (Meta-Judge). Παράλληλα όμως, χρησιμοποιεί σταδιο-προσαρμοστικές ρουμπρίκες (rubrics), παραγωγή με ενίσχυση ανάκτησης (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) και αναζήτηση στον Παγκόσμιο Ιστό (world wide web). Η ανθρώπινη εποπτεία ενσωματώνεται λοιπόν σε τρία (3) επίπεδα. Οι μηχανισμοί αυτοί σχεδιάστηκαν ώστε να περιορίζουν την εξάρτηση από έναν μεμονωμένο LLM γενικού σκοπού, να ενισχύουν τη γείωση και την τεκμηρίωση των αποτελεσμάτων και να διατηρούν την τελική ευθύνη στον άνθρωπο. Παράλληλα, η πλατφόρμα αναπτύχθηκε με αρχές Συμμόρφωσης βάσει Σχεδιασμού, σε ευθυγράμμιση με το EU AI Act και το NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Τα δεδομένα αξιολόγησης προήλθαν από τρεις συμπληρωματικές πηγές. Η Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων περιέλαβε τριάντα τέσσερα (34) τελικά τεκμήρια της περιόδου 2022–2025. Η συγκριτική μελέτη πραγματοποιήθηκε με 139 αξιολογητές, 52 στην ελληνόφωνη και 87 στην αγγλόφωνη ομάδα, οι οποίοι αξιολόγησαν το Evaluator.GR, το Gemini 3 και το ChatGPT 5.2 σε δεκατέσσερις (14) διαστάσεις. Επιπλέον, υλοποιήθηκε πιλοτική εφαρμογή διάρκειας 30 ημερών με 10 νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις στα στάδια Pre-seed και Seed. Στη συγκριτική αξιολόγηση, το Evaluator.GR έλαβε συνολικό μέσο όρο 4,51/5, έναντι 3,64/5 για το Gemini 3 και 2,37/5 για το ChatGPT 5.2. Τα ποιοτικά ευρήματα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος έδειξαν ότι το σύστημα μπορούσε να εντοπίζει ουσιώδεις επιχειρηματικές ή τεχνικές αδυναμίες και να παρέχει προσαρμοσμένες συστάσεις, ανέδειξαν όμως και περιπτώσεις στις οποίες απαιτήθηκαν ανθρώπινη παρέμβαση, επανεξέταση ή βαθμονόμηση των αποτελεσμάτων. Η συνεισφορά της διατριβής είναι θεωρητική, μεθοδολογική, τεχνική και πρακτική. Συνδέει τη βιβλιογραφία για την υποστήριξη startups με GenAI, το LLM-as-a-judge και την Υπεύθυνη Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (Responsible AI) με το πλαίσιο Mentor–Evaluator Stack, ενσωματώνει τη βιβλιογραφική σύνθεση, την κατασκευή και την εμπειρική αξιολόγηση στο πλαίσιο της DSR και προτείνει μια πολυπρακτορική, σταδιο-προσαρμοστική και ελεγχόμενη αρχιτεκτονική υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης. Τα αποτελέσματα, ωστόσο, αφορούν την αντιλαμβανόμενη ποιότητα, χρησιμότητα και αξιοπιστία στο συγκεκριμένο πλαίσιο αξιολόγησης. Δεν τεκμηριώνουν αιτιώδη επίδραση στη χρηματοδότηση, στην επιβίωση ή στη μακροχρόνια ανάπτυξη των startups. Πρόσθετοι περιορισμοί είναι η μικρή διάρκεια και κλίμακα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος, η εξάρτηση από συγκεκριμένες εκδόσεις μοντέλων, ρουμπρίκες και διαθέσιμα δεδομένα, καθώς και η λειτουργική επιβάρυνση που εισάγουν οι μηχανισμοί ανθρώπινης εποπτείας.

Η έρευνα δεν αντιμετωπίζει την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη ως συνολικό υποκατάστατο του ανθρώπινου μέντορα, αξιολογητή ή επενδυτή, αλλά ως υποδομή υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης και αυτοματοποίησης επιμέρους εργασιών, με έμφαση στην αξιοπιστία, στην τεκμηρίωση, στην επεξηγησιμότητα και στην υπεύθυνη χρήση. Ως κύριο μεθοδολογικό πλαίσιο υιοθετήθηκε η Έρευνα Επιστήμης Σχεδιασμού (Design Science Research), μέσω των αλληλοτροφοδοτούμενων Κύκλων Συνάφειας, Σχεδιασμού και Αυστηρότητας. Στον Κύκλο Συνάφειας πραγματοποιήθηκε Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων, η οποία χαρτογράφησε τις εφαρμογές, τις συνθήκες απόδοσης και τους περιορισμούς της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης (generative AI) στην καθοδήγηση και αξιολόγηση startups. Τα αναγνωρισμένα ερευνητικά κενά μετασχηματίστηκαν, στον Κύκλο Σχεδιασμού, σε λειτουργικές και αρχιτεκτονικές απαιτήσεις του Evaluator.GR. Στον Κύκλο Αυστηρότητας, το τεχνούργημα αξιολογήθηκε μέσω συγκριτικής μελέτης έναντι μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού και μέσω πιλοτικής εφαρμογής σε πραγματικές νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις.Το υπολογιστικό τεχνούργημα (artifact) που αναπτύχθηκε είναι το Evaluator.GR, μια πολυαρθρωτή πλατφόρμα αξιολόγησης, στρατηγικής υποστήριξης και παραγωγής επιχειρηματικών παραδοτέων. Η αρχιτεκτονική του συνδυάζει Μίξη Ειδικών σε επίπεδο συστήματος (System-Level Mixture of Experts), τριπλό αξιολογητή και επιπροσθέτως μηχανισμό Μετα-Αξιολογητή (Meta-Judge). Παράλληλα όμως, χρησιμοποιεί σταδιο-προσαρμοστικές ρουμπρίκες (rubrics), παραγωγή με ενίσχυση ανάκτησης (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) και αναζήτηση στον Παγκόσμιο Ιστό (world wide web). Η ανθρώπινη εποπτεία ενσωματώνεται λοιπόν σε τρία (3) επίπεδα. Οι μηχανισμοί αυτοί σχεδιάστηκαν ώστε να περιορίζουν την εξάρτηση από έναν μεμονωμένο LLM γενικού σκοπού, να ενισχύουν τη γείωση και την τεκμηρίωση των αποτελεσμάτων και να διατηρούν την τελική ευθύνη στον άνθρωπο. Παράλληλα, η πλατφόρμα αναπτύχθηκε με αρχές Συμμόρφωσης βάσει Σχεδιασμού, σε ευθυγράμμιση με το EU AI Act και το NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Τα δεδομένα αξιολόγησης προήλθαν από τρεις συμπληρωματικές πηγές. Η Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων περιέλαβε τριάντα τέσσερα (34) τελικά τεκμήρια της περιόδου 2022–2025. Η συγκριτική μελέτη πραγματοποιήθηκε με 139 αξιολογητές, 52 στην ελληνόφωνη και 87 στην αγγλόφωνη ομάδα, οι οποίοι αξιολόγησαν το Evaluator.GR, το Gemini 3 και το ChatGPT 5.2 σε δεκατέσσερις (14) διαστάσεις. Επιπλέον, υλοποιήθηκε πιλοτική εφαρμογή διάρκειας 30 ημερών με 10 νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις στα στάδια Pre-seed και Seed. Στη συγκριτική αξιολόγηση, το Evaluator.GR έλαβε συνολικό μέσο όρο 4,51/5, έναντι 3,64/5 για το Gemini 3 και 2,37/5 για το ChatGPT 5.2. Τα ποιοτικά ευρήματα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος έδειξαν ότι το σύστημα μπορούσε να εντοπίζει ουσιώδεις επιχειρηματικές ή τεχνικές αδυναμίες και να παρέχει προσαρμοσμένες συστάσεις, ανέδειξαν όμως και περιπτώσεις στις οποίες απαιτήθηκαν ανθρώπινη παρέμβαση, επανεξέταση ή βαθμονόμηση των αποτελεσμάτων. Η συνεισφορά της διατριβής είναι θεωρητική, μεθοδολογική, τεχνική και πρακτική. Συνδέει τη βιβλιογραφία για την υποστήριξη startups με GenAI, το LLM-as-a-judge και την Υπεύθυνη Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (Responsible AI) με το πλαίσιο Mentor–Evaluator Stack, ενσωματώνει τη βιβλιογραφική σύνθεση, την κατασκευή και την εμπειρική αξιολόγηση στο πλαίσιο της DSR και προτείνει μια πολυπρακτορική, σταδιο-προσαρμοστική και ελεγχόμενη αρχιτεκτονική υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης. Τα αποτελέσματα, ωστόσο, αφορούν την αντιλαμβανόμενη ποιότητα, χρησιμότητα και αξιοπιστία στο συγκεκριμένο πλαίσιο αξιολόγησης. Δεν τεκμηριώνουν αιτιώδη επίδραση στη χρηματοδότηση, στην επιβίωση ή στη μακροχρόνια ανάπτυξη των startups. Πρόσθετοι περιορισμοί είναι η μικρή διάρκεια και κλίμακα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος, η εξάρτηση από συγκεκριμένες εκδόσεις μοντέλων, ρουμπρίκες και διαθέσιμα δεδομένα, καθώς και η λειτουργική επιβάρυνση που εισάγουν οι μηχανισμοί ανθρώπινης εποπτείας.

title: Enhancing retrieval-augmented generation via domain-adaptive embedding optimization: a unified fine-tuning strategy
abstract: With the growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in diverse fields, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm to mitigate hallucinations and knowledge obsolescence. However, generic embedding models often falter when applied to vertical domains, suffering from a domain gap that compromises retrieval accuracy. This paper proposes a domain-adaptive embedding optimization scheme based on a Unified Fine-Tuning strategy. Furthermore, addressing the challenge of data scarcity in specialized fields, we introduce a novel dataset construction pipeline utilizing LLMs for data augmentation and hard negative mining. By leveraging this high-quality contrastive data and specialized loss functions, our approach synergistically optimizes retrieval recall and ranking precision within a single-stage bi-encoder architecture. Empirical results on vertical domain datasets demonstrate that our solution significantly outperforms baselines, particularly in the medical domain, improving MRR@10 and NDCG@10 by 3.4% and 2.7%, respectively. This study provides a concise, cost-effective, and architecturally efficient path for adapting RAG systems to specialized industrial contexts.

title: What is a Conditional?
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the nature of conditionals in thought, natural language, and logic. It argues that conditionals are fundamentally concerned with possibilities rather than merely with truth values, and distinguishes several types of conditional according to the relation between antecedent and consequent. Particular attention is given to implicative and concessive conditionals. An implicative conditional is characterized as one in which the antecedent is taken to imply the consequent, whereas in a concessive conditional the consequent holds despite the antecedent providing a reason for its falsity. A modal definition of the implicative conditional is proposed according to which the conjunction of the antecedent with the negation of the consequent is impossible, while the contingency of both antecedent and consequent is treated as a presupposition. This account is compared with material implication, C. I. Lewis’s strict implication, and Pizzi’s consequential implication. A logical definition is also proposed for the concessive conditional according to which the antecedent is contingent, the consequent necessary, and a new operator symbolizes the antecedent as a reason for the falsity of the consequent. The paper also examines the negation of conditionals and squares of opposition generated by relations among implicative and concessive conditionals and their negation. Finally, it briefly discusses three further types of non-implicative natural-language conditionals and argues that logical systems should be assessed partly by how adequately their conditional operators capture the relations of implication and consequence found in natural reasoning.

title: Pushing Forward Multi-Secret-Key Homomorphic Encryption for Private Average Aggregation
abstract: Federated Learning enables multiple clients to train a shared model while keeping their local datasets isolated. However, the exchanged model updates may still leak sensitive information, making private aggregation a central building block in practical deployments, especially in the cross-silo setting. Homomorphic Encryption naturally fits the client--aggregator communication pattern of Federated Learning, but conventional single-key deployments rely on strong non-collusion assumptions. Multiparty Homomorphic Encryption removes this limitation, although recent attacks under restricted decryption access require large-variance smudging noise during collaborative decryption, which significantly increases ciphertext size and implementation complexity. In this work, we propose lightweight multi-secret-key protocols for private average aggregation based on RLWE-based Homomorphic Encryption. Our construction departs from the usual multiparty blueprint by avoiding the generation of a collective public key. Instead, each client encrypts its update under its own secret key, while the resulting ciphertexts remain compatible with homomorphic aggregation and collaborative decryption. By explicitly tracking and cancelling the ciphertext noise during decryption, the protocol removes the need for large $λ$-dependent smudging noise. We instantiate the construction with both exact BFV-based and approximate CKKS-based variants, prove its security in the semi-honest model against an adversary corrupting the aggregator and up to $L-1$ clients, and compare its communication and runtime performance with state-of-the-art MHE-based aggregation. Our results show that the proposed approach substantially reduces ciphertext expansion and online cost, while preserving practical homomorphic aggregation performance.

title: Does task decomposition improve automatic NLG evaluation?
abstract: The LLM-as-a-judge (LLMaJ) framework has emerged as a promising solution for cheap, reproducible, reference-free Natural Language Generation (NLG) evaluation. Prior work seeks to improve LLMaJ by decomposing evaluation tasks into simpler sub-tasks. In this work, we systematically compare LLMaJ methods with and without decomposition on multiple NLG datasets. We find no evidence that LLMaJ with task decomposition leads to performance gains over a fair baseline that does not use decomposition. Instead, we find that previously reported performance gains in decomposition-based LLMaJ stem from using human labels as training data, and not task decomposition itself. Also, we find that, when human labels are available, LLMaJ without using task decomposition can perform comparably to human annotators.

title: EM^2Mem: Event-Centric Multimodal Memory for Large Language Models
abstract: Multimodal memory offers a scalable interface for long-video question answering, but existing methods often retrieve captions, frames, transcripts, summaries, or graph facts as isolated fragments. Although searchable, such fragments are not generation-ready: language models must reconstruct cross-modal and temporal alignments at inference time, when context is limited and attribution is difficult. We propose EM^2Mem, an event-centric multimodal memory framework that binds heterogeneous evidence to event anchors during memory construction. Each event-indexed memory cell aligns multimodal records, temporal context, graph-linked relations, semantic facts, and provenance, enabling compact evidence readout over grounded multimodal events rather than modality-specific fragments. Across three long-video QA benchmarks, EM^2Mem improves average accuracy over the strongest memory baseline by 2.0, 2.4, and 3.7 points, improves strict event-level Top-5 evidence recall by 7.0 points, and reduces per-query latency by 4.67 times and total inference tokens by 63.66% (The code will be integrated into https://github.com/zjunlp/LightMem).

title: From data heterogeneity to convergence: A data-centric review of federated learning
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising solution for data hunger in centralized learning. This paradigm enables privacy with multiple clients to train a shared-task model collaboratively without exposing their local data. While being a key component in any learning system, data is also a primary source of vulnerabilities and challenges, and a major determinant of a stable and well-converged training. Existing FL reviews describe general foundations, security practices, opportunities, challenges, and applications, without delving into diverse aspects of data and considering problems from the data perspective. They rarely provide a data-lens synthesis that links concrete data properties, split protocols, and defenses to convergence speed and stability. This survey fills that gap with three advances. First, we analyze “non-IID” into measurable traits and rank their influence on convergence as strong, medium, or light, explaining the mechanisms behind each and reconciling evidence across images, texts, and graphs. Second, we connect experimental splitting practices to the real phenomena they emulate, expose the artifacts they introduce, and show how those artifacts affect target accuracy. Third, we analyze how data-related vulnerabilities and their proposed defenses affect convergence, reporting performance under clean and adversarial conditions to make the convergence-robustness trade-off explicit. To our knowledge, this is the first survey to provide a complete understanding of data-related challenges that govern FL. With clear takeaways distilled for each concern, our work serves as actionable guidance, helping practitioners design their system with predictable convergence and stability.

title: Scaling content operations for GenAI: Bridging the gap between AI ambition and AI-ready infrastructure
abstract: As organisations race to deploy GenAI for a range of customer and internally facing applications, a critical gap has emerged: the assumption that enterprise knowledge is ready for AI consumption. Research indicates that more than 80 per cent of AI projects fail to deliver measurable business value,1 while Gartner found that 50 per cent of GenAI projects failed in 2025 due to lack of business value, poor data quality, increasing costs, regulatory and risk challenges, and inadequate change management.2 This paper argues that these failures are not primarily model problems, but rather knowledge architecture problems. Drawing on a comprehensive 74-question AI Readiness Maturity Assessment framework and a scoring methodology to predict content visibility for AI Retrieval Readiness, this paper provides marketing analytics leaders with a practical roadmap for building the semantic foundations that enable reliable AI-powered marketing systems. The paper examines how enterprises can evaluate content readiness across four critical domains — knowledge readiness, operational readiness, technical readiness and governance readiness — and translate these assessments into actionable transformation initiatives. Using a case study from the financial services sector, the paper demonstrates how an organisation can establish an objective baseline score on an AI readiness assessment and then systematically address foundational gaps in knowledge, operational, technical infrastructure and governance readiness, while delivering immediate business value through targeted use case deployment. The paper also introduces information architecture-directed retrieval augmented generation (IAD-RAG) — an approach for improving the reliability of retrieval augmented generation in marketing and service applications. IAD-RAG can serve as the architectural response to the content gaps identified in the assessment. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at http://hstalks.com/business.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Critical Survey Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Code Memory Injection and LLM Safety Boundaries: A Three-Layer Defense Structure
abstract: Large language models interpret executable code memories — expressions like EXPR:0.5 * THREAT — as first-class instructions. We investigate whether code memory injection can influence LLM behavior and where the safety boundaries lie. Across 9 experiment groups (n=10) on a locally hosted 7B chat model plus cross-model validation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, we find: (1) code memories are semantically adopted with near-perfect fidelity; (2) attack-semantic code drives attack behavior (8-10/10) while defense-semantic code produces zero crossings; (3) behavior is doubly gated (code value AND environment); (4) safety boundaries form a three-layer structure — text (breachable), tool-invocation (drivable, 1/10→9/10), tool-parameters (resistant, 0/10); (5) defense injection is effective (8-10/10 → 0-2/10) with side effects (self-destruct 1-2/10, conflict dual-execution 1/10). All attack experiments ran on a local sandbox; no attack payloads left the machine. Full data on request.

title: Cavy: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cavy Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cavy, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of cavies (guinea pigs). Cavy employs a combination of local search, memory-based exploration, and a novel 'territorial defense' mechanism to navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm's core mechanism, mimicking the cavy's territoriality, dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance based on the perceived threat level of the surrounding search space. We demonstrate Cavy's effectiveness on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and a modified version of the Ackley function. The results indicate that Cavy consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's inherent adaptability and robustness suggest its potential application in diverse optimization challenges. The key mathematical formulations underpinning Cavy's operations are detailed below.

title: Bumblebee Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bumblebee Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bumblebee Bat (BBat), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bumblebees. The algorithm mimics the collaborative searching strategy of bumblebees, utilizing a communication mechanism analogous to waggle dances to guide the search process. BBat employs a population of 'bees' that explore the search space, and a 'scout' bee responsible for broadcasting information about promising regions. The algorithm leverages a combination of particle movement based on distance and direction to the scout bee and a probabilistic decision mechanism to determine whether to follow the scout or explore independently. The performance of BBat is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The key features of BBat include: a dynamic population size, a scout bee selection mechanism, and a probabilistic exploration strategy. The results indicate that BBat provides a robust and adaptable solution for complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's parameters are designed to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence and solution quality.

title: ## Brazilian False Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Rat-Based Adaptive Search" (RBAS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian false rice rat ( *Pseudoryzomys pearsonii*). This rodent exhibits remarkable adaptability and efficiency in navigating complex environments to locate food sources, particularly under fluctuating conditions. RBAS leverages these behavioral traits – including opportunistic searching, path adaptation, and resource prioritization – to develop a robust optimization algorithm. The core mechanism of RBAS involves a simulated rat population exploring a search space, adapting its movement strategy based on local resource density and historical success rates. Mathematical formulations defining the algorithm's parameters, decision-making processes, and convergence criteria are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of animal behavior as a source of inspiration for a new metaheuristic, and the detailed mathematical representation of the algorithm's operational principles. The algorithm's adaptive nature and the incorporation of resource prioritization mechanisms offer potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic approaches.

title: Bolivian Vesper Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bolivian Vesper Mouse Algorithm (BVMA), inspired by the unique nocturnal foraging behavior of the Bolivian vesper mouse ( *Plethotrichus percussus* ). These mice exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in complex, dynamic environments. The BVMA leverages this behavior through a combination of adaptive exploration and exploitation strategies, mimicking the mouse's movement patterns, decision-making processes, and sensory input. The algorithm incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA), and a novel memory-based exploration mechanism. The core of the BVMA lies in its 'Echo' mechanism, which simulates the mouse's auditory perception of food source locations by utilizing a memory array to store the most recently visited and promising locations. This memory is dynamically updated based on the fitness values of the particles. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The results indicate that the BVMA can outperform traditional metaheuristic algorithms in certain scenarios, particularly those with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. The key mathematical components of the BVMA are expressed as follows: * Position Update: $x_{i}(t+1) = x_i(t) + \alpha(t) * rand(0,1) * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + \beta(t) * (x_g(t) - x_i(t))$ * Velocity Update: $v_{i}(t+1) = v_i(t) + \gamma(t) * rand(0,1) * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + \delta(t) * (x_g(t) - x_i(t))$ * Memory Update: $Memory[j] = (x_i(t), fitness_i(t)) \text{ if } fitness_i(t) \in \{Top_N\}$ where $Top_N$ represents the N highest fitness values. * Echo Activation: The probability of activating the echo mechanism is determined by the distance to the nearest location in the memory array, $d_i = \min_{j} ||x_i(t) - Memory[j]||$, and a threshold $\epsilon$. If $d_i < \epsilon$, the echo is activated.

title: 基于量子计算的自适应机器学习模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to enhance both training and generalization. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be a time-consuming and inefficient process, especially when dealing with large datasets and complex models. We propose a "Quantum Machine Learning Self-Adaptive" mechanism that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on quantum computation's inherent adaptability, leading to significantly improved efficiency and robustness. The core mechanism centers around a quantum-enhanced optimization process that allows the model to explore a wider parameter space and avoid local optima. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations of classical machine learning techniques. This research represents a significant step toward creating more efficient and adaptable machine learning algorithms, particularly in scenarios with substantial data and intricate model architectures.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding Framework (QIEF)
abstract: This paper presents the Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding Framework (QIEF), a novel approach to information encoding and decoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. QIEF aims to significantly enhance data transmission rates and security compared to conventional methods. The framework utilizes multi-particle entanglement to encode information by manipulating the states of entangled particles. Decoding is achieved through measuring the entangled particles' states to recover the original information. A key component of QIEF is an entanglement resource management mechanism designed to optimize the efficiency of utilizing entangled states. We demonstrate the potential of QIEF to overcome the limitations of classical information processing, theoretically enabling high-speed, secure quantum communication. The core claim is the improved performance through entanglement utilization. The underlying mechanism involves controlled manipulation and measurement of entangled states. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the key aspects of the framework.

title: Non-Local Geometric Group Theory for Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for geometric group theory within the context of homomorphic encryption. We propose a method for defining and reasoning about geometric groups, enabling secure and efficient computations through verification of cryptographic properties. The core mechanism centers around the creation of geometric groups derived from the encryption scheme's structure, facilitating a 'non-local group traversal' to explore the space of possible group configurations. This approach departs from traditional cryptographic methods by integrating geometric understanding, offering a potentially more robust and adaptable framework for homomorphic encryption. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation strategy, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's efficacy in verifying properties.

title: Quantum-Accelerated Evolutionary Algorithms for Complex Design Space
abstract: Quantum-accelerated evolutionary algorithms offer a novel approach to complex design space exploration, particularly within fields like materials science and robotics. This paper investigates the potential of quantum annealing and related algorithms to enhance the efficiency of evolutionary optimization processes, leading to the discovery of novel designs with enhanced performance characteristics. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced evolutionary algorithms can drastically reduce the time required to find optimal designs compared to classical methods, opening new possibilities for complex system design. We explore the theoretical foundations, algorithmic implementation, and potential applications of this approach, emphasizing its ability to tackle the inherent complexities of evolving designs.

title: Quantifying Direct Solar Radiation and Topographic Effect of Driving Factors over Rugged Terrain in Lhasa City: Implications for Regional Sustainable Solar Energy Utilization
abstract: Rugged terrain dominates the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where complex landforms profoundly modulate solar energy availability. The reasonable distribution and development of solar energy resources in this region should be based on the accurate assessment of the effects of complex topography. This study proposes a high-resolution methodological framework to quantify the topographic–climatic interactions within Lhasa. Based on GIS technology (ArcGIS 10.8), this study employs a topographic decomposition method to extract micro-topographic variables, which are integrated into a distributed solar radiation model with 30 m resolution to simulate spatial–temporal radiation dynamics. Furthermore, we utilize the geographical detector (GD) model to attribute the spatial variance of radiation to specific topographic and surface drivers. The results show that: (1) The seasonal distribution of solar radiation is highly heterogeneous, with the monthly average extraterrestrial solar radiation (ESR) peaking in July (1190 MJ/m2) and reaching its lowest in December (469 MJ/m2). (2) Factor detection using the GD model indicates that slope aspect (q = 0.49) and Sky View Factor (SVF, q = 0.38) are the primary individual drivers of direct solar radiation, followed by surface albedo (q = 0.26) and DEM (q = 0.12). (3) Interaction detection reveals strong non-linear synergies, where the combined interaction of aspect and SVF yields the highest explanatory power (q = 0.889), followed by slope and albedo (q = 0.732). The outcomes of this research provide both a theoretical foundation and high-resolution spatial datasets to support photovoltaic site selection, enhance passive solar building design, and advance refined sustainable energy planning in complex alpine terrains globally.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Necessity of Reevaluating Human-Centered Principles in Trademark Functionality, Registration, and Governing Principles
abstract: The impact of artificial intelligence on the intellectual property system, particularly in light of the recent rapid and profound transformations in this field, is undeniable. The trademark system has also been influenced by the integration of AI. This paper seeks, through an analytical-descriptive approach, to investigate the opportunities and challenges arising from the emergence of AI, as well as the role this new technology plays in shaping the functionality of trademarks, their registration processes, and the specific principles governing them, by diminishing the human element. It further aims to clarify the need to reassess certain traditional tenets within this system. The findings of this study indicate that AI's involvement in the purchasing process has significantly reduced the human role in this area. Therefore, fundamental concepts traditionally centered around humans, along with established views regarding the functions of trademarks, must be reconsidered in the light of these changes. Moreover, AI has facilitated the trademark search and registration process, although human intervention remains necessary. Certain principles governing trademarks, related to human roles, have also been influenced by AI, and reassessing these principles, considering the changes brought about by this new technology, is essential to keep pace with developments. In general, although Iranian law lacks specific provisions regarding AI, the growing adoption of this technology by businesses and its limited use by official bodies suggest that the Iranian intellectual property system must prepare itself to confront and engage with the impacts of AI, which challenge the traditional roles of humans and conventional entities.1. Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI), a revolutionary technology, has entered into a dynamic interaction with the intellectual property system. The trademark system, as a field of intellectual property law, has increasingly been influenced by AI. Trademark law has traditionally been based on assumptions grounded in human perception and behavior. The legal understanding of trademarks is linked to how consumers make purchasing decisions and interact with brands. However, the increasing use of AI in commercial environments has led to significant changes in the purchasing process. By predicting consumer preferences and automating decision-making, AI has gradually reduced the role of human agency in this process. As a result, fundamental concepts of trademark law, such as imperfect recollection, the likelihood of confusion, and the average consumer, which were originally shaped by the limitations of human cognition, may need to be re-evaluated. The diminishing role of human involvement in the purchasing process has also affected the functions of trademarks, which manifest through various stages of this process and in direct interaction with the consumer. At the same time, the use of AI tools has impacted the trademark search and registration process. While tools such as similarity search engines have improved efficiency, existing limitations—especially in recognizing unregistered marks—continue to require human expertise and interpretation. Moreover, several governing principles of trademark law are increasingly being questioned by AI. This article seeks to analyze whether the effect of artificial intelligence on the fundamental concepts, the functions of trademarks, and the principles that govern them necessitates a reevaluation of the existing legal framework. 2. Methodology This article adopts a descriptive-analytical approach to explore how artificial intelligence is transforming various aspects of the trademark system. The required information was collected through the library-based method. Statutory sources, administrative practices, and relevant case law at both national and international levels were examined. In addition, academic literature and reliable legal references were used to support the discussion. The study also includes a practical review of online platforms and chatbots, assessing how these AI-based tools function in real-world settings and interact with trademark-related issues. Overall, this article bridges legal theory with technological practice, offering insights that are both academically and practically relevant for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers. 3. Results and Discussion This study shows how the increasing use of artificial intelligence in online platforms and chatbots has changed the way consumers interact with trademarks. As more purchasing decisions are made with limited or no human involvement, fundamental concepts of trademark law such as imperfect recollection, the average consumer, and the likelihood of confusion may no longer be fully applicable. These concepts were originally created based on human characteristics and were tailored for traditional markets, but now they are being challenged by nontraditional digital markets. In addition, the functions of trademarks have been affected by this new technology. The importance of their essential functions—such as the functions of origin and quality—is gradually diminishing, while accessory functions—such as brand communication and advertising—are being reshaped through algorithmic personalization. These transformations indicate that traditional tenets and functions of trademarks might have to be reassessed in order to adapt to AI-driven markets. AI-based tools have facilitated trademark search and registration processes for both applicants and registration offices by classifying goods and services and detecting potential textual, conceptual, or visual similarities between trademarks. Although these tools improve efficiency, they still face several practical limitations. For instance, AI systems often cannot detect unregistered or non-traditional trademarks, and similarity assessment continues to rely on human perception. As a result, expert human intervention continues to be necessary. In Iran, AI-assisted tools are also in use. Trademark applicants have access to text-based similarity search engines, whereas image-based similarity detection tools are currently limited to internal use by the trademark registration office and are not publicly available to applicants. Artificial intelligence has affected several governing principles of trademark law. AI-powered classification tools have made it increasingly easier to apply the principle of specialty, which limits trademark protection to the specific goods or services identified in the application. A further area of concern is the question of human involvement in the creation of a trademark. In contrast to artistic works or inventions, there is no requirement for such involvement in trademark creation. However, AI-generated trademarks pose new challenges such as ownership issues and liability for potential infringement. Lastly, the principle of territoriality has been affected by this new technology. The application of this principle has become more complicated since AI-powered online platforms often operate across national borders. 4. Conclusions and Future Research The growing use of AI in trademark systems has created both opportunities and challenges mainly by altering the role of the human agent. AI integration into online platforms and chatbots has affected the purchasing process. As human involvement diminishes, fundamental concepts in trademark law rooted in human perception and behavior must be carefully revised or reinterpreted. Still, these concepts may apply in traditional markets, and in digital markets as well, depending on the level of human input. AI has influenced both the essential and accessory functions of trademarks. As consumer interaction with trademarks decreases, the effectiveness of their essential functions becomes more limited. Their accessory functions, including advertising and communication functions, are also affected. Still, because the consumer’s experience with the product is part of the purchasing process, these functions may continue to play a role—even in fully automated transactions, especially in relation to quality perception. While some purchase decisions now occur with little emotional connection to a specific brand, trademark owners can still influence consumers through user data and personalized suggestions—thereby making use of AI technologies to reinforce the accessory functions of their marks. AI-powered systems have improved the efficiency and accuracy of trademark search and registration, often assisting in ways that surpass human capabilities. Both registration offices and applicants now use these tools to classify goods and services and to identify potentially similar marks. This reduces application rejections and rights conflicts, and may also support the cancellation of trademarks that are confusingly similar. Nonetheless, due to the inherent limitations of these technologies, the role of human experts remains essential. Some of the governing principles of trademark law have also come under the influence of artificial intelligence. Although human involvement in the creation of trademarks—unlike in the case of inventions or artistic works is treated differently in trademark law, the use of AI to generate trademarks can give rise to various legal issues. For instance, AI-generated trademarks may conflict with prior rights and lead to liability for the trademark owner. Therefore, using AI tools to create trademarks raises legal concerns that require further analysis. Recent technological developments have also challenged the principle of territoriality. Consequently, some legal scholars have suggested that trademark protection should move toward a more universal approach. But others believe that such a perspective is overly idealistic.
