Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI), a revolutionary technology, has entered into a dynamic interaction with the intellectual property system. The trademark system, as a field of intellectual property law, has increasingly been influenced by AI. Trademark law has traditionally been based on assumptions grounded in human perception and behavior. The legal understanding of trademarks is linked to how consumers make purchasing decisions and interact with brands. However, the increasing use of AI in commercial environments has led to significant changes in the purchasing process. By predicting consumer preferences and automating decision-making, AI has gradually reduced the role of human agency in this process. As a result, fundamental concepts of trademark law, such as imperfect recollection, the likelihood of confusion, and the average consumer, which were originally shaped by the limitations of human cognition, may need to be re-evaluated. The diminishing role of human involvement in the purchasing process has also affected the functions of trademarks, which manifest through various stages of this process and in direct interaction with the consumer. At the same time, the use of AI tools has impacted the trademark search and registration process. While tools such as similarity search engines have improved efficiency, existing limitations—especially in recognizing unregistered marks—continue to require human expertise and interpretation. Moreover, several governing principles of trademark law are increasingly being questioned by AI. This article seeks to analyze whether the effect of artificial intelligence on the fundamental concepts, the functions of trademarks, and the principles that govern them necessitates a reevaluation of the existing legal framework. 2. Methodology This article adopts a descriptive-analytical approach to explore how artificial intelligence is transforming various aspects of the trademark system. The required information was collected through the library-based method. Statutory sources, administrative practices, and relevant case law at both national and international levels were examined. In addition, academic literature and reliable legal references were used to support the discussion. The study also includes a practical review of online platforms and chatbots, assessing how these AI-based tools function in real-world settings and interact with trademark-related issues. Overall, this article bridges legal theory with technological practice, offering insights that are both academically and practically relevant for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers. 3. Results and Discussion This study shows how the increasing use of artificial intelligence in online platforms and chatbots has changed the way consumers interact with trademarks. As more purchasing decisions are made with limited or no human involvement, fundamental concepts of trademark law such as imperfect recollection, the average consumer, and the likelihood of confusion may no longer be fully applicable. These concepts were originally created based on human characteristics and were tailored for traditional markets, but now they are being challenged by nontraditional digital markets. In addition, the functions of trademarks have been affected by this new technology. The importance of their essential functions—such as the functions of origin and quality—is gradually diminishing, while accessory functions—such as brand communication and advertising—are being reshaped through algorithmic personalization. These transformations indicate that traditional tenets and functions of trademarks might have to be reassessed in order to adapt to AI-driven markets. AI-based tools have facilitated trademark search and registration processes for both applicants and registration offices by classifying goods and services and detecting potential textual, conceptual, or visual similarities between trademarks. Although these tools improve efficiency, they still face several practical limitations. For instance, AI systems often cannot detect unregistered or non-traditional trademarks, and similarity assessment continues to rely on human perception. As a result, expert human intervention continues to be necessary. In Iran, AI-assisted tools are also in use. Trademark applicants have access to text-based similarity search engines, whereas image-based similarity detection tools are currently limited to internal use by the trademark registration office and are not publicly available to applicants. Artificial intelligence has affected several governing principles of trademark law. AI-powered classification tools have made it increasingly easier to apply the principle of specialty, which limits trademark protection to the specific goods or services identified in the application. A further area of concern is the question of human involvement in the creation of a trademark. In contrast to artistic works or inventions, there is no requirement for such involvement in trademark creation. However, AI-generated trademarks pose new challenges such as ownership issues and liability for potential infringement. Lastly, the principle of territoriality has been affected by this new technology. The application of this principle has become more complicated since AI-powered online platforms often operate across national borders. 4. Conclusions and Future Research The growing use of AI in trademark systems has created both opportunities and challenges mainly by altering the role of the human agent. AI integration into online platforms and chatbots has affected the purchasing process. As human involvement diminishes, fundamental concepts in trademark law rooted in human perception and behavior must be carefully revised or reinterpreted. Still, these concepts may apply in traditional markets, and in digital markets as well, depending on the level of human input. AI has influenced both the essential and accessory functions of trademarks. As consumer interaction with trademarks decreases, the effectiveness of their essential functions becomes more limited. Their accessory functions, including advertising and communication functions, are also affected. Still, because the consumer’s experience with the product is part of the purchasing process, these functions may continue to play a role—even in fully automated transactions, especially in relation to quality perception. While some purchase decisions now occur with little emotional connection to a specific brand, trademark owners can still influence consumers through user data and personalized suggestions—thereby making use of AI technologies to reinforce the accessory functions of their marks. AI-powered systems have improved the efficiency and accuracy of trademark search and registration, often assisting in ways that surpass human capabilities. Both registration offices and applicants now use these tools to classify goods and services and to identify potentially similar marks. This reduces application rejections and rights conflicts, and may also support the cancellation of trademarks that are confusingly similar. Nonetheless, due to the inherent limitations of these technologies, the role of human experts remains essential. Some of the governing principles of trademark law have also come under the influence of artificial intelligence. For instance, AI-generated trademarks may conflict with prior rights and lead to liability for the trademark owner. Therefore, using AI tools to create trademarks raises legal concerns that require further analysis. Recent technological developments have also challenged the principle of territoriality. Consequently, some legal scholars have suggested that trademark protection should move toward a more universal approach. But others believe that such a perspective is overly idealistic. title: JPRQA : A Joint Progressive Reasoning Framework for Unsupervised KGQA With LLMs
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of large language models (LLMs) has introduced innovative solutions to unsupervised knowledge graph question answering (KGQA). Existing methods typically retrieve answer entities by measuring semantic similarity between questions with reasoning paths in the KG. However, this paradigm struggles to capture the sequential dependencies embedded in the relational chains of complex questions. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes JPRQA, a Joint Progressive Reasoning Framework for unsupervised KGQA with LLMs, which decouples complex questions into sub‐questions to facilitate precise step‐by‐step reasoning over KG. Specifically, we designed a relation‐guided progressive reasoning (RPR) mechanism that leverages position‐aware relation predictors to model the sequential order of relations and perform step‐by‐step reasoning. Furthermore, we enhance answer retrieval through collaborative path optimization, which integrates LLMs with RPR to refine and identify optimal retrieval paths for questions. Experimental results demonstrate that JPRQA achieves an increase in F1 scores by 6.9 and 11.68 on the MetaQA (39,093 questions) and GrailQA (6763 questions) datasets, respectively, compared to other unsupervised methods.

title: AGPV: a knowledge graph question answering model integrating relation attention and neural path verification
abstract: Multi-hop knowledge graph question answering aims to reason over a knowledge graph given a natural-language query and accurately identify the answer entity. Most existing approaches aggregate relation-label representations but overlook fine-grained edge semantics, making it difficult to disambiguate polysemous edges that share the same label and thereby weakening the semantic precision and reliability of inferred reasoning paths. To address this issue, we propose AGPV, a multi-hop reasoning framework that integrates relation attention with neural path logical verification. AGPV includes (i) a neural path logical verifier that enforces path-level consistency and explicitly assesses the logical credibility of candidate paths, improving semantic validity and reasoning coherence during path expansion, and (ii) a query-aware RF-IEF embedding module with relation attention that dynamically reweights relations according to the query, combining global statistics with local semantic sensitivity while suppressing irrelevant relations. Experiments on public benchmarks show consistent gains over strong baselines: on WebQuestionsSP, AGPV achieves 78.6% Hits@1 and 74.6% F1, improving by 1.3% and 2.3%; on ComplexWebQuestions, it improves Hits@1 and F1 by 1.5% and 0.4%; and on MetaQA 1-hop/2-hop/3-hop, it attains an average 99.4% Hits@1, demonstrating strong generalization across reasoning complexities.

title: Attaining quantum sensing enhancement from monitored dissipative time crystals
abstract: Abstract This study investigates quantum-enhanced parameter estimation through continuous monitoring in open quantum systems that exhibit a dissipative time crystal phase. We first analytically derive the global quantum Fisher information (QFI) rate for boundary time crystals (BTCs), demonstrating that within the time-crystal phase, the ultimate precision exhibits a cubic scaling with the system size, f global ~ N 3 . We then generalize this finding to a broader class of dynamics, including the transverse collective dephasing (TCD) model, which achieves a time-crystal phase through a closing Liouvillian gap without requiring a dissipative phase transition. We proceed to numerically demonstrate that this maximal global QFI rate is experimentally attainable for both the BTC and TCD models, even at finite system sizes, via continuous homodyne and photodetection. Moving towards practical implementations, we analyze the precision limits under inefficient detection, revealing a critical difference: for BTC dynamics, inefficiencies asymptotically restore a classical scaling, and only a constant-factor quantum advantage remains possible. In contrast, for TCD dynamics, a super-classical scaling is still in principle observable, and our numerical simulations confirm its presence, even under inefficient measurement conditions, establishing the TCD model as a highly robust platform for quantum metrology.

title: Decision delegation to GenAI agents in travel planning: Responsible AI signals, delegation levels, and the transparency paradox
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is becoming an integral part of travel planning. This fundamental transformation is changing the definition of travel decision delegation, calling for fresh research into responsible AI in tourism. Drawing on agency theory, trust theory and decision delegation framework, this study conceptualises five responsible AI characteristics (reliability, fairness, trustworthiness, accountability, transparency) as evaluative signals for travellers to assess GenAI across three decision delegation levels, i.e., attribute set, choice set, and final decision. Using a multi-method approach, we analyse data collected from 421 travellers. Findings suggest that reliability and accountability are consistent drivers of delegation across all levels, whereas trustworthiness is a threshold condition that becomes significant at the attribute level. We also found that excessive transparency can lead to cognitive overload and reduce willingness to GenAI decision delegation. Our findings encourage future research into responsible AI development in understanding system complexity, algorithmic explainability and traveller delegation confidence.

title: Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool
abstract: Background Reliable mitotic identification in whole-slide images (WSIs) is essential for prognostic evaluation and tumor grading; yet, many commercial artificial intelligence (AI) pathology platforms function as opaque black boxes with little auditability and, frequently, little expert supervision throughout development. Methods We developed a transparent and repeatable process for mitosis identification using YOLOv8, designed to scale from full slide inference to patch-level benchmarking. Global non-maximum suppression (NMS), GPU accelerated inference, region of interest-driven and adaptive tiling, and tissue gating are all integrated into the pipeline. In order to facilitate expert validation and traceability, audit-ready outputs include detection CSVs, tile manifests, positive and negative overlays, and heatmaps. Results From small clinical slides (26 tiles, 4 detections) to huge benchmarks (TUPAC SP2 with 14,270 tiles, 1754 detections), six typical WSIs were processed. Whereas throughput averaged 78 tiles/s depending on the slide size and tissue dispersion, average confidence scores remained constant between 0.69 and 0.80. The successful generation of all audit outputs attested to its scalability and reproducibility. Discussion Transparency and expert monitoring are given priority in this pipeline, in contrast to many industry systems that place an emphasis on end-to-end automation. Whereas audit outputs enable reviewers to track each detection, explicit recording of positive detection tiles avoid quiet false positives. Evaluation on a small number of WSIs and the lack of benchmarking against annotated entire slide datasets are among the limitations, highlighting the necessity for more extensive and thorough cohort validation. Another significant drawback of this work was the use of a single GPU for inferencing. Conclusion This study develops a therapeutically focused, audit-ready process for mitotic figure detection, hotspot identification, and decision-support tool by fusing technical rigor, vetted by experts throughout the process. By demonstrating scalability, reproducibility, and transparency, this work is positioned as a proof-of concept for clinical mitosis detection, multi-GPU/cloud deployment, lab information systems/LIMS connectivity, and eventual use in digital pathology work processes. It also offers a trustworthy and marketable illustration of AI's potential in pathology.

title: A dynamic weighting-based adaptive modality fusion approach for Arabic Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for capturing affective states expressed through heterogeneous modalities, including textual, acoustic, and visual signals. This challenge is particularly pronounced in Arabic multimedia environments, where dialectal variation and modality imbalance introduce additional complexity. Conventional fusion strategies typically rely on fixed weighting schemes or on transformer-based architectures with high computational demands, thereby limiting adaptability, interpretability, and practical efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose AMF-Net, an Adaptive Modality Fusion Network approach that dynamically estimates instance-level modality importance for sentiment classification. Specifically, the model learns to assign context-sensitive weights to text, audio, and visual representations within a shared feature space. The architecture is optimized end-to-end via multi-objective learning that simultaneously maximizes predictive performance and enforces balanced modality contributions. Experimental evaluation on the Ar-MuSA benchmark dataset demonstrates that AMF-Net achieves 77.13% accuracy and a Macro F1-score of 0.7664, outperforming static fusion and late-fusion baselines. Robustness analysis under simulated modality degradation further confirms the stability of the AMF-Net. Additionally, computational assessment indicates that the proposed model maintains practical efficiency, supporting real-world deployment. Overall, AMF-Net provides a scalable, efficient, and interpretable solution for Arabic multimodal sentiment analysis and related heterogeneous multimodal learning applications.

title: LLMPEDIA: Browsing, Verifying, and Comparing the Parametric Encyclopedic Knowledge of LLMs
abstract: Flagship language models appear saturated on benchmarks like MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021), scoring above 90% - yet benchmarks test only what the experimenter thought to ask, the availability bias of fixed question sets. LLMPEDIA makes this bias measurable and browsable. We recursively materialized ~1.3M articles from three model families' parametric memory (GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2, Llama-3.3-70B) without retrieval, then audited a stratified sample of atomic claims against Wikipedia and a curated web stack, coloring every claim supported, refuted, or insufficient (Saeed and Razniewski, 2026). On a uniform random sample the true rate is 68.4% - more than 21 pp below MMLU - with 30.5% of claims insufficient: assertions no benchmark probes and the world's largest encyclopedia cannot adjudicate - long-tail knowledge or plausible hallucination, the evidence cannot tell - extending to free text the coverage gap GPTKB established for triples (Hu et al., 2025). The resulting live, open encyclopedia lets visitors inspect this frontier one claim at a time through five one-click views - link-traversal exploration, claim-level factuality, cross-model and political-persona comparison, and a guided topic drill-down - each page, claim, and verdict at a stable URL. LLMPEDIA is live at https://llmpedia.net

title: GenScale: A Benchmark for Relative Object Scale in Image Generation and Editing
abstract: Modern image generation and editing systems can produce photorealistic, prompt-aligned images, but still often render familiar objects at implausible relative sizes. To measure this failure mode, we introduce GenScale, a benchmark and evaluation protocol for real-world relative object scale in image generation and editing. GenScale contains 900 image-level entries and 1,643 pairwise anchor-target scale relations across common-object generation, human-product generation with metric dimensions, and scale correction from failed generations. We further design a human-calibrated ordinal judge for scalable pairwise scale evaluation. Last but not the least, we introduce Rescale, a model-agnostic post-processing agent for localized scale correction without modifying the source generator. Experiments reveal that state-of-the-art image generators and editors cannot reliably observe relative scale yet, while Rescale consistently improves scale plausibility across generated and edited images. Together, GenScale establishes relative object scale as a distinct, measurable, and actionable capability for image generation systems.

title: Uncertainty Calibrated Cross Platform Identity and Dyadic Episode Modeling for Cyberbullying Analysis
abstract: Cyberbullying is an important issue in digital safety because hostile communications remain accessible on the Internet, intensify over time, and can have profound psychological and social impacts. Timely and proportional moderation is therefore crucial and cannot be achieved without accurate automated detection. Existing studies rely on attention networks, recurrent networks, contextual embeddings, temporal fusion, graph networks, and metaheuristic optimization, but the majority take only single-stage text content into consideration and fail to collectively verify the repeated targeting behavior, cross-platform identity consistency, dynamic power imbalance, harm-directedness, and uncertainty of prediction. To fill this gap, this study presents Causal Identity-aware Dyadic Episode Reasoning for Cyberbullying (CIDER-CB), an advanced learning framework that contains three phases. Phase I conducts multimodal representation with reliability-gating, temporal heterogeneous-graph construction, and probabilistic cross-platform identity alignment. Phase II deploys a marked temporal point process to measure repetition and escalation, a graph-based dyadic reasoning approach to measure the power asymmetry between perpetrator and victim dyad components, and counterfactual causal learning to measure harm towards a target. Phase III combines fairness-constrained intervention learning, evidential uncertainty estimation, and concept drift-aware continual adaptation in order to allow for reliable real-time moderation systems. Through the episode-level and empirical trials, the approach attains effective outcomes via user-disjoint, temporally-separated validation. Thus, the framework achieves 96.5% recall, 98.5% total accuracy, 97.0% precision, 96.7% F1-score, and less than 2.0% false-positive rate. All of these attainments exhibit the proposed performance targets.

Existing studies rely on attention networks, recurrent networks, contextual embeddings, temporal fusion, graph networks, and metaheuristic optimization, but the majority take only single-stage text content into consideration and fail to collectively verify the repeated targeting behavior, cross-platform identity consistency, dynamic power imbalance, harm-directedness, and uncertainty of prediction. To fill this gap, this study presents Causal Identity-aware Dyadic Episode Reasoning for Cyberbullying (CIDER-CB), an advanced learning framework that contains three phases. Phase I conducts multimodal representation with reliability-gating, temporal heterogeneous-graph construction, and probabilistic cross-platform identity alignment. Phase II deploys a marked temporal point process to measure repetition and escalation, a graph-based dyadic reasoning approach to measure the power asymmetry between perpetrator and victim dyad components, and counterfactual causal learning to measure harm towards a target. Phase III combines fairness-constrained intervention learning, evidential uncertainty estimation, and concept drift-aware continual adaptation in order to allow for reliable real-time moderation systems. Through the episode-level and empirical trials, the approach attains effective outcomes via user-disjoint, temporally-separated validation. Thus, the framework achieves 96.5% recall, 98.5% total accuracy, 97.0% precision, 96.7% F1-score, and less than 2.0% false-positive rate. All of these attainments exhibit the proposed performance targets.

title: Introduction to Large Language Models (LLMs)
abstract: This introductory book explains the scientific and engineering principles that underpin modern Large Language Models (LLMs). It is intentionally technology-neutral: commercial systems such as ChatGPT are presented only as examples illustrating broader concepts rather than as the subject of the book. The primary objective of this book is to provide readers with the conceptual foundation required to understand how modern language models work. It is intended for university students, in particular students of Information Systems, educators, software professionals, researchers, technical managers, and all readers who wish to understand LLMs beyond their user interfaces. Artificial Intelligence has undergone several waves of development. The current wave is driven by large datasets, powerful computing platforms, and deep neural networks. Among the most influential outcomes of this evolution are Large Language Models (LLMs). This book focuses on the enduring scientific principles shared by modern LLMs rather than on any specific commercial implementation.

title: Salesforce Digital Engagement Services
abstract: VALiNTRY360 provides Salesforce Digital Engagement Services to help organizations manage customer conversations across chat, SMS, WhatsApp, email, social messaging, and self-service channels. The service connects digital communication with Salesforce CRM records, routing rules, service workflows, analytics, and human support. This gives representatives clearer customer context and helps them respond to requests more quickly.VALiNTRY360 begins by identifying service goals, customer pain points, suitable channels, and automation opportunities. Its team then designs AI agents, configures conversation flows, connects relevant customer information, and establishes escalation paths for complex or sensitive cases. Each setup can include automated case routing, chatbot workflows, follow-up actions, unified agent workspaces, knowledge resources, and customer journey mapping.Testing, user training, and a controlled pilot take place before the wider rollout. Feedback from real interactions helps improve response accuracy, routing logic, and adoption. After launch, VALiNTRY360 monitors response times, customer sentiment, agent activity, resolution trends, and engagement performance through Salesforce dashboards.These Salesforce Digital Engagement Services support faster customer communication, reduced repetitive work, better self-service, consistent messaging, and informed service management. VALiNTRY360 also provides ongoing adjustments so workflows, automation rules, and supported channels can continue matching changing customer and business requirements within each organization’s connected Salesforce customer service environment. title: Cape Spiny Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Spiny Mouse Optimization Algorithm" (SMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape Spiny mice (*Dasypus karachiensis*) in the arid regions of Southern Africa. These mice exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in locating scarce food resources. SMOA leverages this behavior through a dynamic exploration and exploitation strategy, utilizing a multi-dimensional search space and a simulated environment mirroring the mice's foraging process. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the mice's strategy, including the use of landmarks, adaptive step sizes, and a population-based approach. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's core components – the landmark selection, position update, and convergence criteria – are presented. The performance of SMOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that SMOA's adaptive nature and reliance on environmental cues lead to robust and efficient solutions, particularly in challenging landscapes with complex objective functions. Future research directions include incorporating advanced learning mechanisms and extending SMOA to handle multi-objective optimization problems.

title: Core Claim: Establish a dynamic curve optimization framework utilizing machine learning to learn the dynamic changes of curve properties, and leverage these changes to optimize algorithm performance.
abstract: The traditional approach to curve optimization often relies on static parameter settings, limiting the potential for improvement. This paper introduces a novel framework, termed "Adaptive Curve Optimization Framework," that dynamically adapts to the evolving properties of curves through machine learning. The core mechanism involves training a machine learning model to predict and model the dynamic behavior of the curve's curvature. This prediction and modeling then informs the optimization process, leading to enhanced algorithm performance. This framework distinguishes itself by utilizing a continuous learning loop, allowing the model to continuously refine its understanding of the curve's characteristics and, consequently, its optimization strategy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of rigorous experiments across various curve types, highlighting its superior performance compared to traditional methods in terms of convergence speed and optimization quality. This work represents a significant advancement in curve optimization, offering a more adaptive and efficient method for finding optimal solutions.

title: Dynamic Topological Adaptive Quantum Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum computing architecture centered around dynamic topological adaptation, leveraging real-time monitoring of entanglement strength and coherence times within qubits alongside machine learning algorithms to optimize quantum circuit topology. The core claim is that by continuously assessing qubit characteristics and employing reinforcement learning, the architecture can dynamically adjust the quantum circuit's topology, significantly enhancing computational efficiency and resilience to errors. The proposed system utilizes a distributed quantum processor with individual qubits equipped with sensors to measure their quantum properties. Data from these sensors is transmitted in real-time to a machine learning model, trained using reinforcement learning, which learns to optimize qubit connections and prioritize coherence times. This adaptive approach overcomes the limitations of static quantum circuit design and offers a pathway toward truly self-optimizing quantum computation. The system's ability to respond to the physical state of qubits and adapt the circuit topology based on task requirements promises substantial improvements in quantum computing performance.

title: Title: Hierarchical Bayesian Network for Dynamical Systems (HBND)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling and predicting the evolution of dynamical systems – the Hierarchical Bayesian Network (HBND) – utilizing a hierarchical Bayesian network structure. The HBND decomposes the system into a hierarchy of sub-systems, each with its own Bayesian model, and dynamically adjusts the network's structure based on observed data. We demonstrate the HBND's effectiveness through a series of simulations exploring various dynamical systems, highlighting its superior ability to capture complex interactions and offer increased robustness compared to traditional approaches.

title: 基于图神经网络的复杂系统建模与预测
abstract: This paper explores the application of graph neural networks (GNNs) for modeling and predicting complex systems. Complex systems often exhibit intricate relationships between components, making traditional modeling approaches challenging. We propose a novel framework that utilizes GNNs to learn node and edge representations, enabling accurate predictions of system behavior. The paper details the design of the GNN-based system, including the representation learning process, model training methodology, and prediction evaluation. We showcase the effectiveness of this approach in modeling a specific, albeit simplified, example system. The core claim is that adopting GNNs offers a more effective and flexible approach to complex system modeling compared to conventional methods. The research highlights the potential of GNNs to enhance predictive capabilities for various complex systems.

title: 基于拓扑的量子态跃迁的动态调整
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adjustment algorithm for quantum state transitions, leveraging topological structure to optimize the transition process. Traditional quantum state transition algorithms often rely on static, deterministic procedures, limiting their flexibility and efficiency. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism that utilizes the inherent topological properties of quantum states to dynamically modify transition parameters, resulting in improved efficiency and precision in these transitions. We explore a specific instance of this algorithm, demonstrating its potential to enhance the fidelity and speed of quantum state manipulations. The core concept is to engineer the transition process through a carefully orchestrated manipulation of the underlying topological constraints. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated through simulations and analysis, providing a framework for future research and development in quantum state control.

title: Title: Adaptive Wavefunction Collapse Strategies
abstract: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing, requiring precise control over the quantum system's state. Traditional collapse strategies often rely on predefined algorithms, limiting the system's flexibility and hindering the exploration of potentially more efficient pathways. This paper introduces an adaptive wavefunction collapse strategy based on reinforcement learning, which dynamically adjusts collapse pathways to minimize the probability of observing unwanted outcomes. We propose a novel learning mechanism that evaluates and prioritizes collapse pathways based on the inherent dynamics of the quantum system, resulting in a more robust and adaptable collapse process. The algorithm demonstrates improved performance in various quantum state preparation tasks compared to existing static methods.

title: 基于拓扑结构的动态系统优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic system optimization algorithm based on topological structures. Traditional optimization methods often fail to account for the dynamic changes in system states, hindering the effective utilization of system internal structural features. Our proposed algorithm leverages topological structures to model system states and employs a dynamic adjustment of system parameters to optimize performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to enhance system performance compared to existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers around the continuous mapping of system states through topological transformations, enabling adaptive optimization strategies. The algorithm's robustness and efficiency are achieved through a carefully designed transformation process that guarantees the stability of the optimization process. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and implications for various dynamic system optimization problems.

title: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) remains a significant bottleneck in the development and deployment of machine learning models. Traditional HPO methods, such as grid search and random search, often require extensive computational resources and time to identify optimal hyperparameter settings. This paper proposes a novel approach to HPO based on meta-learning. The core idea is to train a meta-learner that can learn to adaptively optimize hyperparameters for new machine learning models and datasets, leveraging experience gained from previous optimization tasks. This meta-learning framework aims to dramatically reduce the time and resources needed for HPO while maintaining, and potentially improving, the performance of the optimized models. The system utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture to learn the optimization process itself, incorporating features such as model architecture, dataset characteristics, and prior optimization results. The learned meta-model then predicts optimal hyperparameter values for new problems, significantly accelerating the training phase. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and theoretical analysis, outlining the potential for substantial improvements in HPO efficiency.

title: Black-tailed Giant Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Nesoryzomys mutica*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Black-tailed Giant Rat (BTGR), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Nesoryzomys mutica*, a large rodent species known for its efficient and adaptable food-finding behavior in complex environments. The BTGR algorithm leverages the rat's characteristic exploration-exploitation balance, its ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions, and its tendency to consolidate successful search areas. The algorithm incorporates key mechanisms such as a dynamic population size, a novel adaptive inertia weight scheme, and a specialized 'trail reinforcement' mechanism mimicking the rat's marking of promising foraging locations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BTGR through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The results indicate that BTGR exhibits robust convergence properties and competitive performance, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex terrain. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization applications.

title: Synthesis with Counterexample Guided Observational Equivalence Graphs
abstract: Program synthesis is hard, as it must search in a huge space of possible programs for one that satisfies the desired specification. In programming-by-example, where specifications are purely given by input-output examples, we can reduce the space by exploiting observational equivalence: if two terms behave the same on all examples, then one can be discarded. But, how can we exploit observational equivalence for logical specifications that reason over potentially infinitely many program inputs? We explore the use of equivalence graphs in counterexample-guided inductive synthesis for general program synthesis. First, we investigate the use of traditional e-graphs and identify limitations that render them impractical for this task. Then, we present Observational Equivalence Graphs (ObsEGraph), a novel e-graph-inspired data structure. ObsEGraphs efficiently represent a set of programs, grouped by observational equivalence, which can be refined through additional observations. We then present Counterexample-guided Observational e-Graph Synthesis (COGS), a new synthesis approach that incrementally searches the space of possible programs by best-first counterexample-guided growth of an ObsEGraph. We show that COGS is sound and complete up to a bounded program size. Our evaluation on benchmarks from the Syntax-Guided Synthesis competition and the Termination competition finds that COGS solves 552 benchmarks, 69 more than cvc5, a state-of-the-art solver.

title: Generative KI und KI-Agenten in Unternehmen: Vom Assistenten zum Akteur
abstract: Generative Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) hält zunehmend Einzug in den Unternehmensalltag: Sie erstellt und bearbeitet Inhalte, erschließt Wissen und unterstützt Beschäftigte bei Analyse, Kom- munikation und Entscheidungsfindung. KI-Agenten gehen darüber hinaus, indem sie Ziele in Teilaufgaben übersetzen, digitale Werkzeuge und Datenquellen einbinden sowie mehrstufige Arbeitsabläufe planen, koordinieren und teilweise eigenständig ausführen. Damit zeichnet sich ein qualitativer Wandel ab: KI wird nicht mehr nur punktuell als Werkzeug genutzt, sondern kann Aufgaben innerhalb betrieblicher Abläufe zunehmend eigenständig übernehmen und ausführen. Dieser Übergang vom Assistenten zum Akteur erweitert den möglichen Einsatz von KI und berührt zugleich das Verhältnis von menschlicher und technischer Handlungsfähigkeit. Was bedeutet diese Entwicklung für die Arbeit in Unternehmen, wie weit reichen die damit verbun- denen Veränderungen und wie gelingt es Unternehmen bestmöglich, das synergistische Poten- zial der feingliedrigen Zusammenarbeit zwischen Mensch und Maschine zu heben? Diesen Fragen widmen sich die Autorinnen und Autoren der Arbeitsgruppe Arbeit, Qualifikation und Mensch-Maschine-Interaktion in diesem Whitepaper und analysieren, welche Veränderun- gen durch generative und agentische KI auf die Arbeitswelt zukommen. Dabei nimmt die Arbeits- gruppe zunächst Veränderungen in einzelnen Aufgabentypen in den Blick und erweitert die Perspektive im nächsten Schritt auf Jobrollen und Berufsfelder. Abschließend formuliert sie Hand- lungsempfehlungen, wie mit den kommenden Veränderungen und Herausforderungen im Sinne von guter und menschzentrierter Zusammenarbeit umzugehen ist. Der Beitrag baut direkt auf dem ↗ Whitepaper Kriterien für die Mensch- Maschine-Interaktion bei KI: Ansätze für die menschengerechte Gestaltung in der Arbeitswelt (Huchler et al., 2020) auf und erweitert es um die Schwerpunkte generative KI1 und KI-Agenten2. Da sich das KI-Ökosys- tem in den vergangenen vier Jahren durch die zunehmende Relevanz generativer KI enorm wei- terentwickelt hat, erscheint ein prüfender Blick auf die ehedem getroffenen Aussagen lohnend. evidence.title: Generative KI und KI-Agenten in Unternehmen: Vom Assistenten zum Akteur
evidence.abstract: Generative Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) hält zunehmend Einzug in den Unternehmensalltag: Sie erstellt und bearbeitet Inhalte, erschließt Wissen und unterstützt Beschäftigte bei Analyse, Kom- munikation und Entscheidungsfindung. KI-Agenten gehen darüber hinaus, indem sie Ziele in Teilaufgaben übersetzen, digitale Werkzeuge und Datenquellen einbinden sowie mehrstufige Arbeitsabläufe planen, koordinieren und teilweise eigenständig ausführen. Damit zeichnet sich ein qualitativer Wandel ab: KI wird nicht mehr nur punktuell als Werkzeug genutzt, sondern kann Aufgaben innerhalb betrieblicher Abläufe zunehmend eigenständig übernehmen und ausführen. Dieser Übergang vom Assistenten zum Akteur erweitert den möglichen Einsatz von KI und berührt zugleich das Verhältnis von menschlicher und technischer Handlungsfähigkeit. Was bedeutet diese Entwicklung für die Arbeit in Unternehmen, wie weit reichen die damit verbun- denen Veränderungen und wie gelingt es Unternehmen bestmöglich, das synergistische Poten- zial der feingliedrigen Zusammenarbeit zwischen Mensch und Maschine zu heben? title: Role-Based Minimal Relation Design Patterns for Interoperable Ontologies
abstract: Many domain ontologies address complex relational semantics using large numbers of domain-specific OWL object properties. Although convenient and often linguistically intuitive, this practice tends to obscure the underlying ontological structure, hinders interoperability, and may introduce unintended logical consequences under description logic semantics. This paper investigates how far specialized relational patterns grounded in process participation can be reconstructed from a small set of ontologically grounded primitives, namely a generic “participates in” relation, types of processes, and formally defined participant roles, rather than through primitive subproperties of “participates in”. Participant roles are formally defined as classes characterized by patterns of participation in processes and constrained by formal axioms. We introduce a set of recurring participant role patterns, including Agent, Patient, Instrument, Undergoer, and several temporal participation roles. These patterns emerged inductively during the reconstruction of relational scenarios in biomedical ontologies. The proposed approach is conceptually related to aspects of participation-based treatments of roles in current foundational ontologies but deliberately avoids introducing additional ontological constructs such as relators, qua-individuals, or descriptions. Instead, it investigates how much relational semantics can be reconstructed within standard Description Logic using participation relations and formally defined role classes. The resulting framework deliberately prioritizes simplicity, interoperability, maintainability, and compatibility with large operational ontologies over maximal ontological expressivity. The approach is applicable to relations whose semantics can be explained through participation in processes, whereas relations grounded in institutional, social, cognitive, or state-dependent contexts, as well as modal, probabilistic, and type-level relations, lie outside the intended scope as they require richer representational mechanisms. The resulting design pattern provides a practical method for improving semantic precision and interoperability in large description logic ontologies while remaining compatible with standard OWL reasoning.

title: Structured geological text dataset and source code for genetic type classification of Pb–Zn deposits
abstract: This dataset accompanies the study “Natural language processing of structured geological texts for genetic type classification of Pb–Zn deposits.” It contains structured geological descriptions for 179 Pb–Zn deposits compiled from published geological literature. Each sample comprises four categories of geological information: mineral assemblage, wall-rock alteration, host-rock lithology, and ore textures and structures, together with a five-class deposit genetic-type label. Of the 179 samples, 139 were used for model development and 40 as an independent test set. Deposit names and explicit type-revealing statements were excluded from the model inputs to reduce label leakage. The repository also provides the source code used for data preprocessing, grouped stratified five-fold cross-validation, hyperparameter selection, model training, independent testing, ablation analysis, and prediction using the MacBERT-based hierarchical classification framework. Dataset fields, label definitions, software dependencies, and execution instructions are provided in the accompanying README file.

title: EBRB–LLM Hybrid Architectures for Trustworthy Agentic AI: Vision, Opportunities, and Challenges
abstract: Agentic AI based on large language models (LLMs) is rapidly evolving from static chatbots to autonomous systems that plan, act, and interact with tools in open-ended environments. However, current LLM agents lack calibrated uncertainty, robust safety mechanisms, and faithful explanations, making them ill-suited for safety-critical settings such as healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, and industrial operations. Extended Belief Rule Bases (EBRB) are representative examples of interpretable, rule-based probabilistic reasoning frameworks with explicit representation of belief and ignorance, and have been successfully applied in complex decision problems without suffering from the rule explosion that affects traditional rule-based approaches. This position paper argues that EBRB could serve as a core safety and reasoning governor within LLM-based agentic pipelines, yielding hybrid systems to better align agentic AI systems with emerging regulatory and ethical requirements for Trustworthy AI (TAI) in high-risk settings. We outline: (i) a conceptual architecture integrating LLMs with EBRB in agentic workflows; (ii) the mapping from this architecture to TAI dimensions including transparency, uncertainty, safety, fairness, and auditability; (iii) concrete opportunities across healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, and industrial safety; and (iv) a research agenda highlighting open challenges in scalable rule induction, co-adaptation between LLMs and EBRB, and evaluation of hybrid agents. Our goal is not to present empirical benchmarks, but to articulate a vision and roadmap for EBRB-enhanced agentic AI that is both powerful and trustworthy.

title: Anomaly detection of automatic online extreme studentized deviate tests for pattern-changing streaming data
abstract: The package osESD in Python and R implements online sequential extreme studentized deviate tests , or osESD in short, a statistical testing method for anomaly detection in online streaming datasets with varying patterns. Its foundation lies in the general extreme studentized deviate test, or GESD test. The GESD test, a simple and effective anomaly detection test, lacks online learning and shows poor performance for pattern-varying data. Our proposed osESD algorithm uses sequential ESD, a variation of GESD, which implements online learning with change-rate trend vectors and residual trend vectors to deal with the problem of pattern-varying streaming data. We also automated parameter tuning in the package with multiple options the user can select for immediate deployment and use. We show that the model learning of our implementation is fast and the performance is excellent compared with numerous models with both various synthetic datasets and real datasets. Codes can be found in the PyPI [ 11 ].

title: Thinking effort aligns between humans and reasoning models in abductive reasoning
abstract: A major question in cognitive modeling concerns the behavioral alignment between large language models and humans across linguistic and non-linguistic tasks. Unlike standard LLMs, large reasoning models (LRMs) are optimized with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards, encouraging correct solutions to reasoning tasks rather than preference-aligned responses. Recent work (de Varda et al., 2025) investigates the cost of thinking in humans and LRMs by comparing human reaction times with model reasoning traces across a range of reasoning tasks. We isolate this alignment by turning to abductive reasoning: unlike deductive tasks, its difficulty cannot be inferred from formal structure and offers no shortcuts a model could exploit to mimic effort without genuine search, providing firmer ground for empirical claims of shared effort. We find further evidence of alignment between LRM and human reasoning effort, as well as evidence that models and humans tend to make similar errors. Finally, we show that decoding methods that let models explore multiple reasoning paths increase alignment in reasoning cost between humans and LRMs across the three models tested.

title: Soft Posterior Speaker Injection for Multi-Talker Speech Recognition
abstract: Multi-talker automatic speech recognition (MT-ASR) remains challenging in the presence of overlapping speech. Hard segmentation introduces irreversible errors, whereas serialized output training (SOT) avoids explicit segmentation but does not condition a pretrained encoder on speaker activity. We propose Soft Posterior Speaker Injection (SPSI). A Soft Posterior Head predicts per-frame speaker posteriors $\hat{\mathbf{P}}$ and injects them into Whisper through Multi-layer Feature-wise Linear Modulation (MFLM) and Speaker Memory Prompts (SMP). The benefit of SPSI is largest where overlap is heaviest and under domain transfer. On controlled two-speaker LibriSpeech overlap, SPSI reduces concatenated minimum-permutation word error rate (cpWER) from $61.5\%$ to $60.0\%$ in the high-overlap bin, and from $51.9\%$ to $51.0\%$ on the full set, relative to SOT. By contrast, Speaker CE, SD-CTC, SA-DiCoW, and Pipeline (oracle/est.\ VAD) do not outperform SOT. Freeze-posterior overlap-heavy adaptation reduces held-out LibriCSS cpWER from $42.3\%$ to $36.8\%$ on sessions $8$--$9$, a $5.5$-point gain over SOT. The source code is available at https://github.com/HackerHyper/SPSI.

title: The Cross‐Kernel Margin: A Robustness Measure for Quantum Kernel Methods
abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum devices in the current noisy intermediate‐scale quantum (NISQ) era are inherently affected by noise, which can degrade the predictive performance of quantum machine learning models. In this work, we introduce a new margin‐based robustness measure for quantum kernel‐assisted support vector machines (QSVMs), termed the cross‐kernel margin . This measure quantifies the stability of a classifier learned under a perturbed kernel relative to the ideal feature space. We derive a posteriori stability bounds for the corresponding inverse squared cross‐kernel margin under kernel perturbations using the Tikhonov‐stabilized SVM dual formulation. The local depolarizing noise model is then applied to this framework to induce perturbations in the kernel. The resulting bounds are numerically checked using simulations across multiple datasets and further tested using kernel matrices obtained from real quantum hardware and a noisy backend simulator. Furthermore, we empirically compare the degradation of test accuracy under local depolarizing noise with the commonly used global depolarizing noise model, providing additional context for the use of the local model in this study. Finally, we present empirical results linking margin‐based quantities with the generalization performance of QSVMs, providing additional motivation for our margin‐based robustness analysis.

title: From graphs to qubits: a critical review of quantum graph neural networks
abstract: Abstract Quantum Graph Neural Networks represent a novel fusion of quantum computing and Graph Neural Networks, aimed at overcoming the computational and scalability challenges inherent in classical models that are powerful tools for analyzing data with complex relational structures but suffer from limitations such as high computational complexity and over-smoothing in large-scale applications. Quantum computing, leveraging principles like superposition and entanglement, offers a pathway to enhanced computational capabilities. This paper critically reviews the state-of-the-art in Quantum Graph Neural Networks, exploring various architectures. We discuss their applications across diverse fields such as high-energy physics, molecular chemistry, finance and earth sciences, highlighting the potential for quantum advantage. Additionally, we address the significant challenges faced by Quantum Graph Neural Networks, including noise, decoherence, and scalability issues, proposing potential strategies to mitigate these problems. This comprehensive review aims to provide a foundational understanding of Quantum Graph Neural Networks, fostering further research and development in this promising interdisciplinary field.

title: Federated Causal-Driven Autonomous Investment Advisory Framework with Privacy-Preserving Multi Agent Intelligence Analysis
abstract: Financial systems are requiring an increasing amount of collaboration across entities; however, institutional, regulatory, and technical restrictions on data sharing and ownership limit the ability to create a true autonomous financial advisor. Centralized investment advisors are limited by their inability to scale with growing amounts of financial data as well as they expose this sensitive information to potential risks such as cybercrime. This paper provides a Federated Learning-Based Autonomous Investment Advisor that integrates five new and distinct modules: Differentially Private Federated Market Representation Learning (DP-FMRL), which enables safe and efficient feature extraction from multiple datasets; the Causal-Adaptive Federated Risk Propagation Network (CA-FRPN), which models interdependencies within the system; the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Federated Strategy Synthesizer (MARFSS); which synthesizes strategic policies in real-time based upon input received from all agents; the Privacy-Preserving Explainable Decision Tensorization Engine (PP-EDTE); which generates decisions in a manner that is understandable to users; and finally, the Secure Hierarchical Federated Execution and Validation Optimizer (SH-FEVO), which validates the execution of the overall federated strategy in a reliable and auditable fashion for real time scenarios. The proposed solution achieves end-to-end privacy protection as it enhances causal reasoning, flexibility and transparency during the investment process.

title: Chaparral Chipmunk: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Chaparral Chipmunk Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, Chaparral Chipmunk (CC), inspired by the foraging behavior of chaparral chipmunks. These chipmunks exhibit a unique strategy of caching food items in a spatially distributed manner, adapting their caching locations based on food availability and environmental factors. CC leverages this behavior through a novel combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA), incorporating a 'territorial defense' mechanism to promote diversification and avoid premature convergence. The algorithm's core components include a dynamically adjusted territory size, a food-availability-dependent caching probability, and a self-adaptive temperature schedule. We demonstrate the efficacy of CC through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in complex and multimodal landscapes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics like convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that CC offers a robust and adaptable approach to tackling challenging optimization problems.

We demonstrate the efficacy of CC through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in complex and multimodal landscapes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics like convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that CC offers a robust and adaptable approach to tackling challenging optimization problems.

title: Pan-tech15/analisis-sentimen: v1.0.0 - Initial release of IdiomSense
abstract: We are thrilled to announce the first stable release of the Idiom-Aware Emotion Classification Web App, a production-ready interface for the hybrid NLP framework presented in our research paper: "Beyond literal meaning: an idiom-aware framework for Indonesian emotion classification using hybrid Natural Language Processing models". This web application solves the critical challenge of accurately detecting emotions in Indonesian text that contains idiomatic expressions (e.g., naik darah, gelap mata, kecil hati). Unlike standard sentiment tools that look at literal words, this app understands figurative language by leveraging contextual embeddings. ✨ Core Features Idiom Detection & Interpretation: Automatically detects Indonesian idioms within your text and maps them to their non-literal semantic meanings before classification. Dual-Model Architecture (Selectable in the UI): IndoBERT–KNN (Recommended): Uses contextual embeddings from IndoBERT, reduced via UMAP (n_components=200), and classified via K-Nearest Neighbors (K=5). Achieves 97.45% accuracy. Naïve Bayes–Lexicon: A lightweight baseline using TF-IDF features enriched with emotion intensity lexicons. Achieves 93.13% accuracy. 7 Plutchik-Based Emotion Categories: Classifies text into Happiness, Trust, Surprise, Neutral, Sadness, Fear, or Anger. Interactive Dashboard: Upload a .txt file or type/paste Indonesian sentences directly into the web interface to get instant emotion predictions with confidence scores. Batch Processing: Handle multiple sentences at once (supports bulk uploads for researchers). Visual Analytics: Displays confusion matrices and performance metrics (Precision, Recall, F1, MCC) for the selected model. 🧪 Scientific Background This app implements the complete 4-stage pipeline described in our paper: Data Collection: Built on a dataset of 10,186 Indonesian sentences (5,173 idiomatic + 5,013 non-idiomatic), labeled by experts with a Cohen's Kappa of 0.9557 (almost perfect agreement). Pre-processing: Case folding, stopword removal, stemming, and IndoBERT WordPiece tokenization. Processing: IndoBERT-KNN: Extracts [CLS] embeddings → UMAP dimensionality reduction → KNN classification. Naïve Bayes-Lexicon: Combines TF-IDF with hybrid dictionary/corpus-based emotion intensity scores. Evaluation: Uses Accuracy, F1-Score, MCC (0.970 for IndoBERT-KNN), and ROC-AUC. Key Finding: Contextual modeling (IndoBERT-KNN) significantly outperforms lexicon-based approaches for figurative language, proving that idioms require semantic understanding, not just word polarity. 🛠️ Tech Stack Frontend: [e.g., Streamlit / React / Flask-HTML] Backend: Python 3.10+ NLP Libraries: Transformers (IndoBERT-base-p2) Scikit-learn (KNN, Naïve Bayes, TF-IDF) UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) Data Handling: Pandas, NumPy Visualization: Matplotlib, Seaborn (for the analytics dashboard)

title: Based on Dynamic Graphs for Knowledge Reasoning Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel system for knowledge reasoning that leverages dynamic graph representations and algorithms. The core idea is to construct a system capable of adapting to evolving knowledge within a knowledge graph and performing real-time reasoning based on this dynamic state. This is achieved through the integration of dynamic graph algorithms for continuous graph updates and knowledge inference algorithms for real-time reasoning. The system presents a new approach to knowledge reasoning by enabling dynamic updates and real-time inference, overcoming limitations of traditional static knowledge graphs. The system utilizes graph traversal algorithms, rule-based reasoning, and semantic similarity measures to effectively navigate and interpret the evolving knowledge. This work contributes to a more flexible and responsive knowledge reasoning paradigm.

title: ## Campbell's Monkey: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Curious Behavior of a Macaque
abstract: This paper introduces Campbell's Monkey, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The inspiration for this algorithm stems from the observed foraging behavior of Campbell's monkeys, known for their seemingly random yet ultimately efficient exploration of food sources. Campbell's Monkey leverages a combination of self-adaptation, memory-based exploration, and a novel "territorial defense" mechanism to navigate solution spaces. The algorithm's core components include a population-based search, a dynamically adjusted adaptation rate, a memory structure to retain promising solutions, and a territorial defense mechanism that encourages diversification and prevents premature convergence. Performance evaluation is conducted on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic techniques. The results show that Campbell's Monkey exhibits strong performance, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex constraints. Future research directions include exploring variations of the territorial defense mechanism and incorporating it into other metaheuristic frameworks.

title: California Sealion Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by California Sealion Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the California Sealion Algorithm (CSA), a newly developed metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of California sea lions. The algorithm leverages the sea lions' dynamic movement patterns, hunting strategies, and social interactions to achieve efficient global search and convergence. CSA incorporates key elements such as adaptive exploration and exploitation phases, a novel population diversity maintenance mechanism, and a dynamic parameter control scheme. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark test functions, demonstrating its competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The core of CSA lies in its 'sealion wave' concept, where a population of individuals moves dynamically, influenced by local and global search information, mimicking the sea lions' coordinated movements. The algorithm's performance is quantified using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that CSA offers a promising alternative for solving complex optimization problems across diverse domains. Specifically, the algorithm's adaptability to changing environments and its robust population diversity maintenance contribute to its superior performance.

title: Based on Quantum Error Correction Codes Hardware Security Module Design
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Hardware Security Module (HSM) based on quantum error correction (QEC) codes, specifically engineered to facilitate high-reliability key generation and transmission within quantum communication systems. The core innovation lies in leveraging the inherent error correction capabilities of QEC codes to mitigate the inherent vulnerabilities associated with quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. The design details the implementation of a layered approach, incorporating redundancy through QEC coding and decoding, alongside secure key management procedures. The system aims to significantly enhance the security and reliability of quantum key distribution by actively addressing the challenges posed by noise and imperfections in quantum channels. This work explores the theoretical foundations of QEC and its application within an HSM framework, outlining the key components and operational flow. The performance analysis highlights the potential for improved key generation rates and enhanced security margins compared to traditional QKD methods. The design presented here contributes to a more robust and practical realization of quantum communication networks.

title: Bushveld Sengi: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Bush Sengi Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Bushveld Sengi (BVS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the bush sengi (Xerus rubicundus). Bush sengis are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. BVS leverages these traits by incorporating a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism based on probabilistic path selection and adaptive step size adjustment. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, similar to other metaheuristics, but with unique modifications to enhance its convergence speed and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BVS through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's key features include a dynamic exploration probability, a self-adaptive step size control mechanism, and a robust mutation operator. The results indicate that BVS is a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization problems across diverse domains. The primary objective is to develop a flexible and effective optimization algorithm inspired by the ingenious foraging techniques of the bush sengi.

title: Non-Linear Geometry and Quantum Entanglement: A Coupling Approach
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic potential of non-linear geometry and quantum entanglement, proposing a novel protocol for secure information exchange and quantum computation. We introduce the concept of "Geometric Geometry" – a framework that connects the inherent non-linear properties of geometric structures with the delicate quantum states inherent in entanglement. Through precise geometric transformations, we aim to guide the evolution of entangled states, effectively creating a bridge between the geometric structure and the quantum phenomenon. This approach offers a unique pathway to enhance information security and accelerate the development of quantum technologies. The core mechanism leverages the interplay between geometric transformations and entanglement, pushing the boundaries of current quantum protocols.

title: Non-Equilibrium Learning Theory in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-equilibrium learning theory within the framework of reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional RL methods often struggle in complex environments due to challenges in efficiently balancing exploration and exploitation. This research proposes leveraging the principles of non-equilibrium theory, specifically the dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation, to significantly enhance the learning speed and performance of intelligent agents. The core claim is that an intelligent agent can achieve a remarkable improvement in its learning capabilities when the exploration-exploitation balance is carefully managed. The theoretical framework presented introduces a novel approach to RL that utilizes the inherent properties of non-equilibrium systems to guide the learning process, ultimately leading to faster convergence and superior performance in challenging scenarios. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings, proposes a methodology for integrating non-equilibrium learning into RL algorithms, and discusses potential implications for various applications of RL.

title: Causal Discovery from Observational Data using Deep Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques for causal discovery from observational data. Traditional causal discovery algorithms often rely on strong assumptions about the underlying data distribution and struggle with complex, high-dimensional datasets. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing deep neural networks to directly learn causal relationships from observed variables. The core mechanism involves training a deep neural network to encode the data's inherent causal structure. The learned representation is then leveraged to infer directional causal relationships between variables. The approach offers a promising solution for causal inference scenarios where interventional data is unavailable, capitalizing on the representational power of deep learning. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a theoretical framework and outline key considerations for its implementation and future development. The primary focus is on learning a latent representation that encodes causal dependencies, enabling inference even in the absence of explicit interventional data.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Bakso GLG Using the Naive Bayes Method
abstract: Accelerating digital innovations have vastly reshaped the methods individuals use to express their perspectives on the gastronomic industry about culinary services through customer reviews on Google Maps. This study seeks to examine the sentiments conveyed in reviews of Bakso GLG to assist management in understanding customer perceptions objectively by employing the Naïve Bayes algorithm only after undergoing rigorous preprocessing phases, including cleaning, case folding, normalization, tokenization, stopword removal, stemming, and the generation of TF-IDF vectors. The classification results yielded an overall accuracy of 77%. The data distribution is dominated by positive sentiment, comprising 226 reviews, followed by 25 neutral reviews and 13 negative reviews. Although the model demonstrated optimal performance in classifying positive sentiment, it encountered difficulties in classifying the minority classes due to the imbalanced dataset. Overall, the system proved effective in processing large-scale review data as a source of strategic evaluation for improving product and service quality in the culinary sector, particularly at Bakso GLG.

abstract: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to disruptions whose effects propagate across organizational boundaries, yet the data needed to predict such risks is fragmented among firms reluctant to share it for competitive, contractual, and regulatory reasons. Centralized machine learning therefore under-utilizes collective evidence, and organizations with inadequate datasets cannot predict risk reliably on their own [1].

title: Sarcoma Region of Interest (ROI) Images - Part 5
abstract: Bone and soft tissue (BST) tumors are a heterogeneous and rare group of mesenchymal neoplasms that pose significant diagnostic challenges owing to their complex morphologies and overlapping histological features. Despite rapid advances in digital pathology, most publicly available datasets predominantly focus on common epithelial tumors and offer a limited representation of BST tumors. To address this gap, we introduced the Pathologist-Annotated Image Retrieval dataset for Bone and Soft Tissue tumors (PAIR-BST), a dataset consisting of 2,252 pathologist-annotated regions of interest derived from 470 whole slide images obtained from 268 patients diagnosed with BST tumors. Each region was curated and annotated with multi-level labels, including 33 histologic diagnoses, 11 lines of differentiation, and 6 growth patterns, enabling comprehensive characterization of the morphological heterogeneity inherent to BST tumors. Benchmark experiments have demonstrated that pathology foundation models face challenges in identifying these tumors, particularly when distinguishing between tumor subtypes and growth patterns. PAIR-BST offers a high-quality, discriminative benchmark for the development and evaluation of pathology foundation models, specifically focusing on rare mesenchymal tumors.[Metadata Availability] Additional metadata containing specific coordinates for all ROIs (Regions of Interest) within the WSI, along with labels such as diagnosis for each, is available in a separate .csv file at: https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.33383509 (also linked in the related materials below). Find related datasets in the collection at https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.c.8223469

title: General Domain Event Detection Method based on TAP-BERT and Event Fusion
abstract: Event detection is a key task in information extraction that aims to identify event trigger words from text and classify them into event types. Existing methods focus more on the trigger word itself, overlooking the dependencies between contexts and lacking comprehensive feature extraction. Therefore, this paper proposes the model TBEF (TAP-BERT + Event Fusion Layer + CRF). First, the TAP-BERT pretrained model for word vector embedding—which incorporates word embedding matrix decomposition, feed-forward neural network pruning, and self-attention mechanism pooling in BERT—is utilized to obtain richer contextual semantic information. Then an event fusion layer consisting of attention and gate mechanisms is employed to better compute the correlation between events and trigger words. Finally, the sequences are labeled by Conditional Random Field (CRF) integrating BIO labeling. Experimental results show that the proposed method yields an F1 value of 68.55% on the MAVEN dataset, achieving advanced performance for event detection.

title: The role of artificial intelligence in service sector: A study of emerging opportunities, challenges and future prospects
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the service sector by changing the way organizations deliver services, manage employees, interact with customers, analyse information, and make strategic decisions. As a knowledge- and human-capital-intensive sector, services are particularly exposed to AI-enabled automation, augmentation and innovation. This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in the service sector, with particular emphasis on emerging opportunities, challenges and future prospects. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design based primarily on secondary data collected from peer-reviewed research, institutional reports, international organizations and authoritative publications. Percentage and ratio analysis, comparative analysis and thematic analysis are used to interpret the available evidence. The study finds that AI offers significant opportunities through process automation, personalized customer services, predictive analytics, intelligent decision-making, productivity enhancement, cost reduction, service innovation and workforce development. However, concerns relating to employment displacement, algorithmic bias, privacy, cybersecurity, transparency, digital inequality, skill gaps and excessive dependence on automated systems remain important challenges. Recent ILO evidence suggests that AI is more likely to transform many jobs than completely eliminate them, emphasizing the importance of human–AI collaboration. The study concludes that the future of AI in the service sector depends on responsible adoption, appropriate regulation, workforce re-skilling, ethical governance and human oversight.

title: A Review of Research on Intelligent Optimization Algorithms for Jamming Resource Allocation of Networked Radar
authors: XU Zhixia, WANG Rui, SHEN Xiaowei, HE Bing, KANG Weijie
abstract: The networked radar jamming resource allocation is a typical Non-deterministic Polynomial (NP) problem and a significant challenge, requiring the use of various optimization algorithms to solve it. To address the issues of low computational speed and poor adaptability in traditional jamming resource allocation optimization algorithms, advancements in intelligent optimization algorithms in this field are reviewed. First, a mathematical model and a solution framework for networked radar jamming resource allocation are constructed. The difficulties in solving this model are analyzed, and the advantages of intelligent optimization algorithms in terms of computational efficiency, global optimization capability, and robustness are emphasized. Subsequently, using the Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, Ant Colony Algorithm (ACA), and various improved algorithms as typical examples, the implementation processes, solution effectiveness, and strengths and weaknesses of intelligent optimization algorithms in networked radar jamming resource allocation are analyzed in detail.
