title: Bridging the digital pathology divide: reciprocal learning between high-resource and low-resource settings
abstract: Digital pathology (DP) represents a major advance in global health, integrating digital whole-slide imaging, telepathology and clinical-grade artificial intelligence into cohesive workflows that can improve diagnostic accuracy and educational access. Realising these gains, however, depends on local infrastructure, governance, reimbursement and workforce capacity. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated DP uptake in some settings, but adoption remains highly uneven between high-resource settings (HRS) and low-resource settings (LRS), reflecting unequal infrastructure, workforce, policy and financing. This analysis contends that reciprocal innovation, a model of ongoing two-way learning between HRS and LRS that is distinct from one-way technology transfer, can accelerate DP adoption by leveraging the strengths of each environment. Drawing on examples from HRS and LRS, we examine use cases in education and clinical practice, the adoption barriers that persist and policy mechanisms required for sustainable scaling. While HRS contribute regulatory frameworks, validation standards and mentorship, LRS offer innovations in cost efficiency, workflow resilience and open-source adaptation that can inform more sustainable models globally. Neither HRS nor LRS are homogeneous entities. Resource availability also varies substantially within each category: HRS may contain poorly resourced institutions, while some institutions in LRS may have comparatively greater resources but still face broader system-level infrastructure constraints. Ensuring access to those in LRS requires targeted investment, harmonised standards and mutual learning across resource levels. DP has the potential to foster bidirectional partnerships to democratise access to timely, accurate and patient-centred pathology services across all resource settings.

title: Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Information Science
abstract: Abstract Quantum information science is a new and rapidly developing discipline that studies the general laws governing the transmission, storage, and processing of information in systems that obey the laws of quantum mechanics. It makes extensive use of matrix theory and operator theory on Hilbert spaces to investigate the capabilities of such systems and to develop principles for their rational design. An important consequence of the development of quantum information science is a substantial clarification of the logical structure and foundations of quantum mechanics and of its relation to reality. These lectures are devoted to the foundations of the mathematical theory of quantum systems: states, observables, communication channels, their entropic and information characteristics, and quantum information-processing protocols. The lectures provide a detailed introduction to the statistical structure of quantum theory and the necessary background from classical information theory; hence, knowledge of the basic mathematical subjects—analysis, linear algebra, and probability theory—is sufficient for understanding the material. In the first part of the course, we use the “standard” statistical model of a quantum system, but consider it in comparison with the classical statistical description. A consistent development of this approach leads to a generalized statistical model of quantum mechanics, in which observables (in general, “unsharp”) are described by probability operator-valued measures, while evolutions (in general, irreversible) are described by completely positive maps. Introductory material on these concepts, which underlie mathematical models of quantum information systems in the presence of noise and errors and have numerous applications in quantum information science, is presented in the second part of the course.

title: A domain-specific RAG framework for aviation intelligence: integrating localized LLMs with hybrid reasoning
abstract: Driven by the strict requirements of the "Intelligent APP" project—completely offline local deployment and acceptable performance under constrained hardware resources—this study proposes a localized intelligent question-answering system integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology to address highquality knowledge acquisition and data security risks in aviation R&D. General-purpose models often suffer from domainspecific knowledge gaps and hallucinations. To overcome this within strict hardware limits, we integrate 7B-parameter general and deep-thinking models, along with a lightweight text-embedding model, to efficiently vectorize data into a local database. By employing prompt-tuning strategies, the system dynamically retrieves relevant knowledge fragments via vector similarity matching to guide response generation, thereby effectively suppressing hallucinations. The proposed framework establishes a completely internet-independent, closed-loop workflow encompassing query preprocessing, precision local retrieval, and answer optimization. Quantitative evaluation using the RAGAS framework demonstrates robust system performance. Measured on a scale of 0 to 1, the Vector RAG system achieved a context precision of 0.99, a context recall of 0.81, and a faithfulness score of 0.87. The answer correctness reached up to 0.73, significantly approaching the performance boundary of cloud-based massive models. The results indicate that this fully localized architecture significantly enhances the accuracy and security of knowledge retrieval for aviation professionals, providing a replicable, resource-efficient, and secure technical solution for LLM deployment in specialized vertical industries.

title: Privacy-preserving visualization of brain functional connectivity
abstract: Visualizations are fundamental to neuroimaging research, facilitating tasks ranging from exploratory data analysis to the communication and interpretation of findings. Despite their necessity, visualizations can potentially compromise the confidentiality of individual participants. In this paper, we discuss how visualizations may inadvertently lead to privacy leakage and explore methods to mitigate such risks. Our work investigates ways to securely share visualizations that faithfully preserve the patterns supporting the derived insights from data analysis, rather than deriving conclusions from the visualizations themselves. We address privacy-preserving visualization within a differential privacy (DP) framework, focusing on commonly used visualization methods for functional network connectivity. Various perturbation-based strategies are investigated for protecting correlation-related measures, with analyses of their privacy costs and the effects of pre-processing and/or post-processing. To achieve a better balance between privacy and visual utility, this paper introduces novel workflows tailored for connectogram and seed-based connectivity visualizations that maintain the qualitative patterns observed in non-private results. Overall, this work illustrates how DP can be effectively applied to neuroimaging visualization, demonstrating its efficacy as a robust methodology for securing sensitive biomedical data.

title: Multi-agent collaborative knowledge question answering for mineralogy
abstract: ABSTRACT When large language models are applied to professional geological fields such as mineralogy, they frequently suffer from knowledge obsolescence, factual hallucinations, and invalid complex logical reasoning. Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods mostly adopt a static pipeline architecture, which easily causes logical breaks and semantic fragmentation when processing complex geological queries, and can hardly realize collaborative utilization of structured knowledge and unstructured text. To address the above shortcomings, this paper proposes a Multi-agent Mineral RAG (MaM-RAG) approach for mineralogy-oriented collaborative retrieval-augmented generation. This method constructs a collaborative closed loop of intent recognition-multi-source execution-decision fusion. An intent recognition agent performs non-destructive decoupling of complex queries while completely preserving the internal logical structure. Multi-source retrieval agents acquire knowledge graphs and text corpora in parallel to break information isolation among heterogeneous data. A decision fusion agent conducts semantic consistency verification on multi-source evidence and triggers reflective retrieval in case of evidence inconsistency, completing self-verification and self-correction of the reasoning process. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves significantly higher accuracy than traditional RAG and general large language models on mineralogy professional question answering tasks. It can effectively suppress factual hallucinations and improve answer accuracy and robustness, providing a feasible solution for professional intelligent question answering in the geological domain.

title: The Performance of Quantum State Texture in Noninertial Frames
abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum state texture, an important characteristic of the structure of quantum state space, reflects the intrinsic nature of quantum states. We investigate the influence of the Unruh effect on quantum state texture for multipartite generalized GHZ states, and establish trade‐off relations between physically accessible and inaccessible quantum state texture. Then, we derive quantitative restricting relationships between quantum state texture and genuine multipartite entanglement. Furthermore, we examine the dynamic evolution of quantum state texture under acceleration through an amplitude damping channel. We find that the quantum state texture of the physically accessible state increases monotonically with acceleration, while its physically inaccessible counterpart exhibits the opposite trend. Interestingly, after undergoing amplitude damping channel, the quantum state texture is enhanced and increases monotonically with the damping probability. Our research reveals how quantum state texture changes in noninertial frames, providing theoretical support for the connection between quantum information and relativity.

title: GadIR: A Spatial-Topology Preserving Compiler for Quantum Many-Body Systems Simulation
abstract: Simulating quantum many-body systems has been one of the most important applications of quantum computation. For simulation, the Hamiltonian of a physical system is compiled into quantum programs with native instructions for quantum hardware. In previous works, the Hamiltonian is represented as Pauli strings, then compiled and optimized based on the quantum circuit model. Such representation paradigm neglects the spatial topology of original physical models, which is vital information to reducing the overhead of compiling many-body systems Hamiltonians. To address such neglect, we introduce a spatial-topology preserving compiler for quantum many-body simulation. Using Pauli gadgets as the representations of the Hamiltonian, we introduce our intermediate representation -- GadIR, to preserve the spatial-topology information of original physical models. Our compiler frontend performs the group reduction algorithm based on Pauli gadget model, which is a hardware-independent optimization. Our compiler backend performs trotterization and scheduling on Pauli gadgets, then synthesizes the Pauli gadgets into hardware-native quantum programs. We evaluate our compiler on all the canonical quantum many-body system models, while achieving a significant reduction on compilation overhead regarding four major quantum architectures. Overall, our spatial-topology preserving IR exploits the compilation optimization space for quantum many-body systems Hamiltonian.

title: CATeye: Coupled Attribute-Topology Invariance Learning for Voucher Abuse Detection
abstract: Voucher abuse poses a major challenge in e-commerce, where malicious users exploit promotional vouchers for profit. Unfortunately, fraud patterns evolve rapidly over time and across regions, causing distribution shifts that degrade existing detection models unless retrained frequently. To tackle this, we propose the Coupled Attribute-Topology Invariance Learning framework (CATeye). The key challenge arises from coupled attribute-topology shift, where edges built from attribute proximity cause environment-driven attribute shift to induce shifted topology, thereby amplifying variant signals through GNN message passing. CATeye sees through such coupled shifts with two learnable selectors. First, an Attribute Invariance Selector (AIS) learns node-adaptive masks to filter out non-invariant attributes. Then, conditioned on retained invariant attributes, an Edge Invariance Selector (EIS) samples an invariant subgraph and isolates non-invariant edges. Using the resulting invariant and non-invariant components, CATeye constructs multiple views and applies view-specific objectives to emphasize domain-invariant representations while suppressing domain-specific variations. Experiments on both a proprietary dataset from Lazada, a major Southeast Asian e-commerce platform, and a public benchmark show that CATeye consistently outperforms nine strong domain generalization and graph anomaly detection baselines, achieving up to an 8.61% improvement in average F1 score over the strongest baseline. Source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Tian0426/CATeye.

title: HiLRP: Toward One Trustworthy Explanation for Vision Transformer: Conservation-Valid Attribution via Attention Primitives
abstract: Vision Transformer (ViT) design has become increasingly diverse, with backbones combining convolutional stems, windowed, linear, or multi-axis attention, patch merging, and spatial reduction in various configurations. This diversity poses challenges for existing attribution methods, whose assumptions often do not hold across ViT variants: Grad-CAM requires a terminal spatial feature map, attention rollout assumes global softmax attention, and layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) requires module-specific rules. To the best of our knowledge, no existing method provides a unified attribution framework across this architectural space. We show that this architectural diversity can be captured by a simpler underlying structure. The attention and resolution-reduction operators in current ViTs can be decomposed into four operation types: linear maps, bilinear mixing, normalization or gating, and reindexing. Each operation admits a relevance rule that satisfies conservation. Based on these rules, HiLRP supports new backbones by construction rather than by architecture-specific derivation, and its attribution maps decompose the prediction rather than relying on heuristic assumptions. We prove conservation and conditional equivariance and verify both to machine precision. Across 14 attribution methods and 10 architectures, we find that no prior method remains reliable across ViT families, while Faithfulness Correlation becomes uninformative for backbones robust to spatial masking. HiLRP alone preserves conservation across windowed, spatial-reduction, multi-axis, and linear-attention models, where naive extensions can produce zero or inflated relevance. It also localizes attribution failures in class activation mapping, achieving 0.97 Pointing compared with 0.55 for competing methods on EfficientViT.

title: ViTAL-X: Video-Text Alignment with Cross-Modal Temporal Edits
abstract: Video-text models adapted from image-text architectures (e.g., CLIP) frequently exhibit temporal blindness, the inability to perceive fundamental cues like order, direction, and motion dynamics. Standard datasets mask this limitation by enabling models to exploit static spatial shortcuts. To systematically evaluate this, we introduce XTE-Bench, a diagnostic probe revealing that even large-scale video-language models struggle with basic temporal reasoning, indicating that parameter scaling alone is insufficient to resolve this flaw. To address this, we propose Cross-Modal Temporal Edits (XTE), a self-supervised framework that injects precise temporal supervision. By performing synchronized video-text transformations, XTE generates hard temporal negatives without manual annotation. We instantiate this with ViTAL-X, a lightweight model that equips frozen image-text backbones with temporal awareness while preserving their foundational spatial knowledge. Across six temporal benchmarks, ViTAL-X achieves state-of-the-art performance. Utilizing only 0.4B parameters and 1M training clips, ViTAL-X outperforms 7B-parameter models and surpasses baselines trained on 600x more data. These results demonstrate that targeted, high-quality temporal alignment provides a highly efficient alternative to pure scaling.

title: WHEN AI BECOMES THE STRATEGIST: HUMAN AI COLLABORATION, STRATEGIC CONFORMITY, AND COMPETITIVE DECISION-MAKING
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence and large language models are increasingly used not only to support operational tasks but to generate and evaluate business strategy itself.This conceptual article examines what happens to competitive decision-making when AI moves from an analytical tool to something closer to a strategic collaborator.Drawing on human-AI complementarity theory, institutional theory, and the dynamic capabilities perspective, the article argues that AI-generated strategic advice carries a structural risk: because large language models are trained on shared bodies of business text and respond to similar prompts with similar reasoning patterns, firms that lean heavily on AI for strategic recommendations may converge toward common playbooks rather than differentiate from rivals.This risk echoes long-standing accounts of institutional isomorphism, but with a new mechanism a shared algorithmic advisor rather than shared professional norms or regulatory pressure.At the same time, evidence on human-in-the-loop decision-making suggests that keeping a human's judgment in the final step of a recommendation process need not weaken decision quality and may improve how recommendations are received and acted on.The article synthesizes this literature into a conceptual framework distinguishing condition under which human-AI collaboration is likely to preserve strategic diversity from conditions under which it is likely to produce conformity, and it closes with managerial implications for firms that want to use AI's analytical power without surrendering the strategic distinctiveness that competitive advantage depends on.

title: Dual-Domain Spectral Vision Transformer with Asymmetric Boundary-Guided Diffusion for Ultra-High Resolution Panoptic Histopathology Segmentation
abstract: Precise panoptic and semantic segmentation of microscopic tissue structures, malignant glandular morphologies, and infiltrative tumor boundaries in gigapixel Whole Slide Images (WSIs) represents an indispensable prerequisite for computational oncology, digital pathology grading, and personalized therapeutic stratification. While deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) have advanced automated histological analysis, current paradigms face fundamental technical bottlenecks: standard non-overlapping tokenization introduces severe spatial attenuation and high-frequency edge loss, windowed self-attention mechanisms fail to resolve multi-scale cellular pleomorphism across vast receptive fields, and deterministic decoders yield overconfident, blurry predictions along ambiguous stromal-epithelial transition margins. In this paper, we propose SpectralDiff-Trans, a novel dual-domain hierarchical vision transformer integrated with an asymmetric boundary-guided conditional diffusion refinement decoder for ultra-high-resolution panoptic histopathology segmentation. SpectralDiff-Trans introduces a 2D Learnable Wavelet-Fourier Spectral Transform (LWFST) encoder that decouples low-frequency macroscopic tissue architecture from multi-directional high-frequency cellular boundary gradients across spatial frequency domains. To capture multi-scale morphological context without quadratic complexity, we formulate a Linearized Criss-Cross Axial Attention (LCCA-Attention) bridge that propagates contextual dependencies across horizontal, vertical, and diagonal spatial trajectories. Crucially, rather than relying on deterministic softmax segmentation heads, we formulate boundary delineation as a conditional reverse-time stochastic differential equation (SDE) diffusion process, wherein a score-based boundary refinement network progressively denoises uncertain topological contours guided by edge energy fields. We conduct extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets: the GlaS Gland Segmentation Challenge, the multi-organ MoNuSeg nuclear segmentation dataset, and the PanNuke panoptic cancer histology benchmark (covering 19 distinct tissue types). SpectralDiff-Trans achieves state-of-the-art segmentation fidelity, reaching a mean Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 89.8%, a Panoptic Quality (PQ) of 68.4%, and an ultra-low 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) of 4.12 µm, outperforming competitive supervised ViTs (Swin-UNet, TransUNet, UNETR) and generative segmentation baselines (MedSegDiff) by +4.2% in DSC and reducing boundary localization errors by 41.8%. Comprehensive ablations, theoretical convergence analyses, and clinical pathologist Turing assessments validate that SpectralDiff-Trans provides robust, clinically actionable morphological delineation for next-generation digital pathology.

title: Proactive Trust Calibration for Large Language Models: A Systematic Framework for Hallucination Detection, Uncertainty Estimation, and Reliability Assessment
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities in natural language generation, reasoning, and knowledge-based tasks; however, their reliability is frequently compromised by hallucinations, overconfident responses, and poorly calibrated uncertainty. Existing approaches typically address hallucination detection, uncertainty estimation, and confidence calibration as separate problems, limiting their effectiveness in assessing the overall trustworthiness of generated responses. This paper proposes Proactive Trust Calibration (PTC), a systematic framework that integrates hallucination detection, multi-level uncertainty estimation, evidence verification, confidence calibration, and reliability assessment into a unified process. The framework evaluates model outputs using multiple signals, including token-level uncertainty, semantic consistency, factual evidence, claim-level verification, and calibrated confidence. A Trust Calibration Score (TCS) is introduced to combine these signals and estimate the reliability of generated responses. Based on the estimated reliability, the framework enables adaptive response strategies, including direct answering, qualification, additional verification, or abstention. The proposed approach shifts LLM reliability management from reactive error detection toward proactive assessment before unreliable information is presented to users. The framework is designed to be evaluated using established hallucination and factuality benchmarks, with metrics including accuracy, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), Brier Score, F1-score, AUROC, and selective risk. The proposed PTC framework provides a unified foundation for developing more transparent, uncertainty-aware, and reliable LLM-based systems across applications such as healthcare, education, scientific research, legal information, and enterprise knowledge management.

title: ## Caucasian Birch Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Behavioral Patterns
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Caucasian Birch Mouse Algorithm" (CBMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Caucasian birch mouse ( *Apodemus nigrita* ). These mice exhibit a unique and highly efficient foraging strategy characterized by a systematic exploration of their environment followed by focused exploitation of promising areas. The CBMA leverages this strategy by employing a novel combination of probabilistic exploration and adaptive exploitation techniques. The algorithm utilizes a population of candidate solutions, represented as vectors, and iteratively refines these solutions through a series of operations, including mutation, crossover, and a novel "territory shift" mechanism mimicking the mouse's movement patterns. The performance of the CBMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key contributions of this work include a detailed description of the algorithm's mechanics, a comparative analysis of its performance, and a discussion of its potential applications. The algorithm's parameters are designed to mimic the mouse's adaptive behavior, leading to robust and efficient convergence. The results suggest that the CBMA provides a valuable addition to the toolbox of metaheuristic optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptive exploration and exploitation.

title: Butcher Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Butcher Oldfield Mice
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Butcher Oldfield Mouse" (BOM), inspired by the foraging behavior of Butcher Oldfield mice (Mus carduus). These mice are known for their highly efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly their ability to explore and exploit local food sources while maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation. The BOM algorithm leverages these principles through a novel combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA). Specifically, the movement of particles within the search space is governed by a "territory defense" mechanism, mimicking the mice's competitive behavior for food resources. Furthermore, a "memory" component is incorporated, allowing particles to retain information about previously visited and successful locations, enhancing exploration capabilities. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and rapid convergence. The key innovations of BOM lie in its dynamic territory management and the strategic use of memory to guide the search process. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic techniques, highlighting its advantages in certain problem landscapes. This research contributes a novel approach to metaheuristic algorithm design, drawing inspiration from the natural world to improve optimization performance.

title: Probability Space Geometry Algorithm Optimization Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm optimization framework based on probability space geometry. The core concept is to treat the algorithm's state as a probability distribution, allowing for dynamic updates and leveraging the probabilistic nature of the distribution to enhance generalization and adaptability. We propose a mechanism where the probability distribution's evolution is driven by a set of rules, ensuring consistent behavior across diverse input scenarios. This framework aims to overcome limitations of traditional optimization methods by incorporating the inherent uncertainty and richness of probability distributions.

title: ## Buffy Flower Bat Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents the Buffy Flower Bat Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFBMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Buffy Flower Bats. The algorithm incorporates key aspects of the bat's echolocation and flight patterns into its search strategy. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a dynamic parameter system based on the bat's frequency and pulse rate, employing a chaotic component to enhance exploration. The BFMBA's core mechanisms include an adaptive parameter adjustment, a chaotic search component, and a diversity maintenance strategy. The algorithm is designed to effectively navigate complex, high-dimensional search spaces and is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and simulations, showcasing its performance on benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that the BFMBA is a competitive metaheuristic algorithm capable of finding near-optimal solutions for a variety of challenging optimization problems. The key contributions of this work lie in the novel integration of bat-inspired behavioral patterns and the development of a robust and adaptable search mechanism.

title: 基于自适应的量子算法的扩展
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum algorithm design leveraging adaptive quantum algorithms. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on predefined steps, failing to adequately respond to the dynamic behavior of the quantum system. We propose a system where the quantum algorithm dynamically adjusts its steps based on the current state of the system, thereby enhancing algorithm efficiency and stability. This system, termed the "Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Engine" (AQAE), represents a significant advancement in quantum computation by incorporating self-adjustment capabilities. We detail the core mechanism, the benefits observed through simulation and analysis, and the potential implications for practical quantum computation.

title: Brown Agouti: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Peromyscus breviceps*
abstract: This paper introduces Brown Agouti (BA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies employed by the brown agouti (*Peromyscus breviceps*), a rodent known for its efficient and adaptive search behavior in the understory of Neotropical forests. BA leverages concepts of resource distribution, path optimization, and dynamic adjustment of exploration-exploitation trade-off, mimicking the agouti's ability to locate and exploit food sources effectively. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism, termed "Dynamic Resource Allocation" (DRA), which adjusts the probability of movement and food selection based on local resource density. BA's core features include a circular representation of the search space, a probabilistic movement strategy, and a dynamically updated food desirability function. We present a detailed description of BA's components, its operational principles, and its performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems. Preliminary results demonstrate that BA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems requiring adaptability and efficient exploration of complex search spaces. The algorithm's design emphasizes robustness and adaptability, making it potentially suitable for diverse optimization challenges.

title: 基于量子态叠加的并行计算模型
abstract: This paper proposes a novel parallel computing model leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. The core idea is to decompose computational tasks into multiple quantum states existing in a superposition, and then perform parallel calculations using quantum gates. This approach aims to accelerate the computation process by exploiting the inherent parallelism of quantum mechanics. The model's efficiency stems from the ability to explore numerous possibilities simultaneously, a capability significantly enhanced compared to classical parallel computing architectures. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key components and operations involved in this new paradigm. We demonstrate the potential advantages of this model through a conceptual analysis and highlight its relevance within the broader field of quantum computing. Further research and development are needed to translate this theoretical model into a practical and scalable implementation.

title: Conceptual Graph Distillation for Efficient Semantic Understanding
abstract: This paper explores the application of conceptual graph distillation to enhance semantic understanding and reasoning within knowledge graphs. The core claim is that distilling knowledge from conceptual graphs into lower-dimensional representations, facilitated by deep learning models, significantly improves the efficiency of semantic search and knowledge inference. We propose a mechanism utilizing deep autoencoders to learn compact representations of conceptual graphs, preserving crucial relationships and semantic information. The novelty lies in the synergistic combination of conceptual graphs and deep learning, offering a powerful approach to knowledge compression, representation, and ultimately, improved semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities. This work presents a foundational approach that can be further extended to various knowledge domain applications.

title: Dynamic Programming with Adaptive Horizon Lengths for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that leverages dynamic programming (DP) while mitigating its computational limitations through adaptive horizon length adjustments. Traditional DP algorithms often struggle with environments exhibiting high stochasticity, leading to excessive computation and potentially poor performance. Our method addresses this issue by dynamically modifying the horizon length utilized in the DP calculations. The core idea is to monitor the state and action distributions observed during learning. When the environment demonstrates significant stochasticity, the horizon length is extended, allowing for more comprehensive future consideration. Conversely, when the environment is relatively predictable, the horizon length is reduced, streamlining the DP process. We formulate this approach as a modified DP algorithm, incorporating a mechanism for horizon length adaptation. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key equations and considerations. The algorithm's potential benefits – improved sample efficiency and reduced computational burden – are discussed. This work represents a significant advancement in adapting DP to complex, real-world RL problems.

title: Bloyet's White-toothed Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bloyet's White-toothed Shrew Algorithm" (BWSA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the European white-toothed shrew ( * Sorex araneus* ). The algorithm's core mechanism mimics the shrew's efficient exploration and exploitation of its environment for food resources. BWSA utilizes a combination of adaptive step size adjustment, a novel surrogate solution representation, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key components of BWSA are: a population of candidate solutions (represented as vectors), a stochastic movement operator mimicking the shrew's foraging steps, a local search operator based on the shrew's preference for high-reward areas, and an adaptive step size control mechanism driven by the environmental reward signal. The algorithm's performance is compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), showcasing its competitive capabilities. Future research will focus on extending BWSA to handle multi-objective optimization problems and exploring its application in various real-world engineering and scientific domains.

title: Title: Universal Quantum Machine Learning with Dynamic Kernel Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning framework, Universal Quantum Machine Learning (UQML), that leverages dynamic kernel selection to enhance generalization performance. Traditional machine learning often employs fixed kernels, limiting the model's ability to effectively adapt to diverse data distributions. UQML addresses this limitation by dynamically adapting the kernel function during training, ensuring optimal fit across various data types. We propose a quantum-inspired approach that continuously optimizes the kernel shape to achieve superior predictive accuracy and robustness. This work explores the theoretical implications of dynamic kernel selection and demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of simulations and experiments. The core mechanism centers around a quantum-enhanced kernel adaptation process that optimizes the kernel's shape in real-time. The benefits of this approach include improved generalization, reduced sensitivity to data initialization, and the potential for more efficient training.

title: Title: Algorithmic Differential Geometry for High-Dimensional Data Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of algorithmic differential geometry to address challenges in high-dimensional data analysis. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the complexity of high-dimensional spaces, while existing techniques lack the ability to effectively leverage geometric constraints to guide the search for optimal solutions. We propose a novel algorithm, 'Gradient-Based Differential Geometry,' that utilizes geometric constraints to automatically identify and exploit latent structure within high-dimensional data, offering a potentially transformative approach to solving problems across diverse fields. This work presents a framework for efficiently finding optimal solutions in high-dimensional spaces, with the potential to significantly advance machine learning and image processing techniques.

abstract: Ce manuel propose une série d’exercices dans le but de : • Découvrir les possibilités offertes par l’environnement R dans le domaine de la cartographie thématique, • Se familiariser avec les principaux formats de données dotées d’une composante spatiale (données vectorielles ou rasters) pris en charge dans l'environnement R, • Utiliser les fonctions élémentaires (st_read, st_transform, st_centroid, etc.) pour manipuler les données spatiales vectorielles, en vue de les cartographier, • Dans une moindre mesure, utiliser aussi quelques fonctions élémentaires (rast, project, crop, etc.) pour manipuler les données rasters, en vue de les cartographier, • Prendre en main les principaux packages existants pour élaborer des cartes, automatiser leur production au moyen de boucles et réaliser des atlas, publier en ligne des représentations cartographiques, • Produire une grande variété de rendus cartographiques (cartes en aplat, cartes en aplat à effet crayonné, cartes en symboles proportionnels, cartes en oursins, cartes de flux bidirectionnels, carte en lignes de crête, cartogramme, carte en contour de relief, carte du relief en perspective avec drapage d’orthophotographies, etc.), • Tester plusieurs méthodes de discrétisation et différentes palettes de couleurs, personnaliser l’habillage des cartes, composer des planches contenant plusieurs cartes, • Apprendre à paramétrer les arguments des fonctions permettant de produire des cartes en symboles proportionnels afin de garantir la proportionnalité taille-valeur, • Concevoir des visualisations stéréoscopiques (synchronisées en vis-à-vis ou avec rideau), intégrer des fonds de cartes accessibles au travers d’API (tuiles XYZ, WMTS, WMS, WFS),

title: ЗАСТОСУВАННЯ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ В УПРАВЛІННІ ІТ-ПРОЄКТАМИ: МОЖЛИВОСТІ ТА ВИКЛИКИ
abstract: The article provides a systematic analysis of the opportunities and challenges of applying artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in IT project management. The author focuses on four key functional areas of project management: planning and effort estimation, risk forecasting, resource allocation optimisation, and decision-making support. Given the rapid growth of project data volumes, the shortening life cycle of software products, and the rising customer demands for development speed and quality, special attention is paid to the advantages of AI in the context of automating routine operations, predictive analytics, and increasing the productivity of distributed teams. The study reveals that AI technologies, particularly machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics, significantly reduce the time spent on routine managerial tasks, improve the accuracy of effort and deadline estimates, and enable proactive risk identification through the analysis of historical project data. At the same time, the concept of agentic AI and the levels of its autonomy in project management are considered, ranging from advisory assistants to systems capable of partially performing the functions of a project manager. The article summarises recommendations regarding the appropriateness of implementing AI tools depending on the project's specificity, team maturity, data quality, and customer expectations. The key challenges are analysed, including problems of data quality and availability, ethical and legal constraints, the shortage of qualified personnel, and the need to rethink the competency profile of the project manager, with an emphasis on the growing role of soft skills, AI literacy, and adaptability. The findings offer practical value for project managers, IT company executives, and researchers in the field of project management who seek to optimise their approaches to implementing IT projects in accordance with the demands of the modern digital environment. The paper also highlights that the responsible adoption of AI contributes to building a culture of data-driven decision-making, transparency, and continuous improvement. Moreover, strategic considerations of integrating AI frameworks into various organisational contexts are discussed, alongside the importance of stakeholder engagement, ethical governance, and human oversight, which remain fundamental to achieving not only operational efficiency but also long-term organisational resilience and competitiveness.

title: Multi-Level Dependence from Essence
abstract: Multi-level frameworks are increasingly used in knowledge representation to model scenarios involving not only types and their individuals, but also types of types, e.g. Species, Human, and me. Central to prominent approaches are powertypes and basetypes, which have not yet been analyzed for dependency. In this paper we analyze and formalize the dependence relations between these entities using Fine’s theory and logic of essence, derived notions for dependence, specialization, and rigidity, the Multi-Level Theory, and a geological use-case. Results reveal a web of dependencies that enhance understanding of these entities.

title: Enhancing Cervical Cancer Diagnosis with Multimodal Fusion and Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning
abstract: Reliable detection of cervical cancer at an early stage greatly improves treatment outcomes. In this work, we introduce a multimodal deep-learning setup that studies both Pap-smear cytology images and ultrasound scans together to support clinical decision-making. The framework tackles three related tasks: classifying cervical abnormalities, estimating patient risk, and predicting a continuous severity measure. Unlike approaches that rely only on a single type of image, our model merges information from both modalities and incorporates uncertainty estimates using Monte Carlo Dropout. The confidence scores help the system understand how certain it is about each prediction. In our experiments, DenseNet121 stood out as the best-performing model, achieving about 95.3% accuracy and an R² value of 0.91 for predicting severity. Overall, the framework shows strong potential as a reliable tool for supporting automated cervical cancer assessment.

title: USD-NLP: Universal scene description for multilingual NLP pipelines
abstract: Natural language processing (NLP) systems usually analyse text by adding token, span, and dependency annotations. Professional multilingual workflows, including conference interpreting, legal translation, and cross-border M&A documentation, also require document hierarchy, version history, parallel language states, and auditable amendments. USD-NLP addresses this representation problem by adapting Universal Scene Description (USD) composition concepts to multilingual text workflows. It represents projects, documents, language or processing layers, and linguistic units as composable objects, so amendments and language-specific states can be layered without overwriting earlier versions. USD-NLP does not replace automatic annotation engines; it stores their outputs in a versioned structure. Token attributes such as lemma, part of speech, and morphology are stored as Prim metadata, named entities are represented as span Prims over token identifiers, and dependency trees are represented as typed links from dependent tokens to head tokens. A lightweight CoNLL-U adapter converts standard pipeline output into this structure while preserving the zero-dependency design of the core library. Performance benchmarks on a 30,000-Prim scene show construction throughput of approximately 92,000 Prims per second, layer composition at 1.4 ms per document stage, non-destructive override application at over 500,000 operations per second, and a memory overhead of 1.35 × relative to flat dictionary baselines.

title: State of the art in program analysis
abstract: Abstract Static and dynamic program analysis techniques have been studied for several decades to provide foundations for tools that discover software defects or that verify their adherence to semantic properties. Applying these techniques to real-world programs presents several challenges, such as scalability and precision. This special issue of Software Tools for Technology Transfer comprises novel results and practical applications of these techniques. The papers in this special issue are extended versions of selected workshop papers from the proceedings of the 14th ACM SIGPLAN International Workshop on the State Of the Art in Program Analysis (SOAP 2025).

title: TREMORS: An Agentic Assistant for Multi-Datacenter Seismic Data Acquisition
abstract: Seismology increasingly depends upon large data retrieval across multi-datacenter platforms. Yet, data procurement often demands domain expertise, user burden, and is difficult to reproduce. As archives continue to grow, translating scientific intent into structured workflows that operate across multiple repositories and produce high quality, AI ready data is becoming an increasingly urgent challenge. We present TREMORS (Text Referenced Event Mapping and Output Renderer for Seismographs), an agentic framework that uses large language model reasoning within a constrained execution graph to automate seismic data retrieval. TREMORS translates natural language queries into a structured intermediate schema, which drives execution through a constrained LangGraph workflow. Example workflows demonstrate support for both event-based and continuous waveform acquisition. The framework is designed to extend across heterogeneous multi-datacenter systems through a portable schema and modular workflow components. This work positions agentic workflows as the catalyst that will connect scientific intent with distributed seismic data systems, enabling a future of reproducible, data-driven inquiry while reducing the burden of routine acquisition tasks.

title: Reveree: Diagnosing LLM Reverse-Engineering Agents
abstract: Reverse engineering (RE) is critical to security tasks such as malware analysis and vulnerability discovery, and large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly able to perform it autonomously. Capture-the-flag (CTF) RE challenges have become the standard proxy for measuring this capability, but evaluation rests on a single criterion: whether the agent captures the flag. This solve rate reveals neither where in the RE process an agent fails nor whether a success reflects analysis of the binary or recall of a public solution. In this paper, we propose Reveree, a diagnostic framework that scores an LLM RE agent's trajectory at three tiers: solve rate, milestone progress through an eight-stage RE schema, and a behavioral profile of its actions. Comprehension stages are scored by an outcome-blinded LLM judge validated against a human expert; all other stages are verified deterministically. Using Reveree, we evaluate nine frontier models and four prompting strategies on 88 picoCTF and NYU-CTF challenges. We find that the base model dominates performance, whereas prompting strategy is a secondary, model-dependent effect. Surprisingly, larger, newer, or costlier models are not reliably stronger. We also find that failures concentrate at the comprehension stages of the RE process, and that extra budget, persistence, or reasoning effort rescues few of them, pointing to a competence limit rather than a resource limit. Regarding memorization, while models reproduce picoCTF flags from challenge descriptions alone, NYU-CTF shows minimal measurable recall, and most solves survive surface perturbation, indicating that genuine analysis coexists with memorization. We release Reveree to the community.

title: QILP-0: Constructing Observational Declarative Twins of Quantum Circuits
abstract: This paper introduces QXymb, a general framework for constructing observational declarative twins of quantum circuits, and develops QILP-0, its first complete order-0 specialization. QILP-0 constructs a finite multi-valued propositional logic program from observed circuit behaviour within a declared observational scope. The pipeline traverses a declared family of quantum observables incrementally according to a reproducible structural grading and a declared observational reference horizon. Progress is quantified through reference-relative coverage against a fixed target-independent reference. Observable responses are organized through target-independent geometry, while retained latent structure is mapped deterministically back to original observable columns before symbolic processing, preserving observational semantics and provenance. Selected observable profiles are converted into a finite relation through admissible target-independent discretization. The target is used only afterwards to audit twin-admissibility and induce the declarative theory. A theory is certified as an exact observational declarative twin when it completely and correctly reconstructs the resulting finite task-conditioned discrete relation. Logical exactness is therefore separated from numerical, backend, provider, and discretization uncertainty, which is retained as audit metadata. Validation uses two complementary QML settings. Exhaustive Bars & Stripes experiments compare product and grid-CZ embeddings from 16 to 100 qubits and exercise the native-discrete branch. Low-Depth MNIST analyses all 14,708 digit-0/1 instances before and after a trained variational quantum transformation and exercises continuous discretization. In every reported relation, the induced QILP-0 theory achieves complete, conflict-free reconstruction with strict accuracy equal to one.

title: Autoregressive Mosaics: Probing 2D Spatial Reasoning in Text-Only Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) trained only on text and code can sometimes generate programs that draw recognizable images. However, it is unclear whether this reflects an internal representation of 2D spatial layout or simply the ability to translate spatial descriptions into code. We introduce Autoregressive Mosaics (AM-Bench), a benchmark that separates these factors: First, a translation task gives a model a fully specified geometry of a picture in words as a prompt and asks for the code that produces it. Second, a layout task requires the model to compose an image from an underspecified prompt. Across eight open-weight text-and-code-only models, all models reliably translate specified geometry into code, but their open-ended layout performance differs substantially, indicating that these differences are not explained by code-generation ability alone. An output-medium ablation further shows that the interface or medium of expression that the model uses matters: replacing procedural code with raw SVG improves layout scores across all models. Finally, probing model activations shows that a coarse layout plan is present before generation, but reflects only the layout implied by the prompt. During generation, models track the evolving geometric state instead of executing an initially fixed plan. Overall, these results show that 2D spatial performance in text-only LLMs depends on both the model and the output medium, and is not explained by code-generation ability alone.

title: Agentic AI Kit (AAK) User Guide - Version 0.5.5
abstract: Agentic AI Kit (AAK) User Guide - Version 0.5.5This document is the detailed user guide for Agentic AI Kit (AAK), an open-source Python framework for building AI agents, tool-using systems, adaptive memory architectures, retrieval-augmented generation workflows, SQL AI applications, data-science agents, and multi-agent systems.The guide covers installation and configuration, the AAK command-line interface, BaseAgent, ToolAgent, JsonAgent, ReasoningAgent, AnalystAgent, MLEAgent, AutoModelAgent, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), short-term and persistent memory, emotion-aware episodic memory, SQL AI, Agentic SQL workflows, the Antigravity runtime adapter, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, and multi-agent orchestration patterns.Practical examples are provided for creating conversational agents, registering Python tools, generating structured outputs, analysing pandas DataFrames, training baseline machine-learning models, querying SQLite databases using natural language, enriching structured data with generative AI, building retrieval-based assistants, and coordinating multiple agents.The guide also documents important implementation boundaries and operational considerations in AAK 0.5.5, including read-only SQLite access for Agentic SQL workflows, model-provider requirements, RAG persistence limitations, asynchronous Antigravity usage, API quota considerations, and recommendations for production validation.AAK is designed around a separation between model-driven reasoning and deterministic execution: language models are used for planning, interpretation, routing, and generation, while Python, pandas, scikit-learn, SQLite, and registered tools perform deterministic computation and execution.Software: Agentic AI Kit (AAK) Version documented: 0.5.5 Programming language: Python License: MIT PyPI Link: https://pypi.org/project/agentic-ai-kit/

title: IMPLEMENTATION AND SIMULATION OF A QUANTUM HALF ADDER USING IBM QISKIT
abstract: Quantum computing is an emerging computational paradigm that represents and processes information using quantum states. This paper presents the implementation and simulation of a Quantum Half Adder using the IBM Qiskit framework. The proposed circuit performs one-bit binary addition and produces two outputs, SUM and CARRY, through reversible quantum operations. Classical input values are encoded into quantum states using Pauli-X gates. title: WordSpoof: A public corpus of single-word bona fide and synthetic speech
abstract: This dataset is also mirrored on HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/datasets/clearspeed/WordSpoof There, access is granted automatically on accepting the licence terms. The Zenodo copy here is released per request. Both copies are byte-identical: sha256 a83249a373d2…. Dataset Card for WordSpoof A public corpus of standalone single-word bona fide and synthetic speech, for research on synthetic-voice detection. Most audio-deepfake corpora are sentence-length; this one is not, and detectors trained on sentence-length audio degrade sharply on it. Dataset Details Dataset Description WordSpoof pairs real single-word utterances with synthetic ones generated by 11 modern text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems, so a detector — or a researcher auditing one — can measure what happens when the input shrinks from a sentence to a word. Both classes are English, drawn from single_word and yes_no response kinds, and shipped as 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV with a per-clip JSON manifest. Curated by: Mario Gómez-Martínez (Clearspeed) and Jimmy Gibson (Clearspeed) Funded by: Clearspeed Shared by: Clearspeed Language(s) (NLP): English (en) License: Double-licensed. CC BY-NC 4.0 covers the compilation and every synthetic clip; the bona fide clips retain their upstream CC BY 4.0 (Google Speech Commands v2) and CC0 1.0 (Mozilla Common Voice) terms. Full breakdown, the legal reasoning, and per-provider obligations are in Licence and Legal Notices below — read that section before redistributing or fine-tuning on any subset in isolation. Dataset Sources Repository: this HuggingFace dataset and a permanent archive copy at Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22655557. Both copies are byte-identical. Paper: ICASSP 2027 submission titled "WordSpoof: a public dataset for synthetic-voice detection on single-word utterances", citing this dataset by its sha256. Citation details below. Verify what you downloaded. SHA256SUMS.txt ships beside these files and covers all of them: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt The published artifact is: WordSpoof.tarsha256 a83249a373d2b5ced967a6e3f5289a21dd92de0d83e30afe1ca8f9535aba5deebytes 9,771,991,040built 2026-09-01 Any paper reporting numbers on this corpus should cite that sha256, not the name — see Citation below for why. Uses Direct Use Training, fine-tuning, evaluating, or benchmarking synthetic-voice detectors for non-commercial purposes, including academic research and education. The licence restricts commercial use, not training itself, and the publisher adds no additional no-training term. See Licence and Legal Notices for the exact per-subset terms and the reasoning behind them. The dataset is well suited to studying how detectors trained on sentence-length audio behave on single-word or short-utterance input, and to auditing content-blind shortcuts in existing detectors (see Bias, Risks, and Limitations, which documents one such shortcut measured on this corpus). Out-of-Scope Use Any commercial exploitation of the CC BY-NC–licensed material (the compilation and all synthetic clips). This includes shipping a model trained on this corpus as, or inside, a commercial product — the restriction is retroactive: a research checkpoint must not become a product checkpoint. Distributing trained detector checkpoints. Not done by this release and not licensed for you to do either — see Licence and Legal Notices. Impersonation. No clip may be used to impersonate a real person; every cloning reference voice is a consenting, published research speaker (VCTK), and every synthetic clip is labelled spoof. Voice-cloning misuse of any kind, per the gating terms above. Dataset Structure WordSpoof/ audio/ .wav one clip per file, 16 kHz mono PCM16 manifest.jsonl one JSON object per clip prompts.json the prompt set release_meta.json build provenance build_skips.jsonl clips the build declined, with reasons LICENSE NOTICE.md per-provider obligations and source attributions licenses/ archived licence texts Extract with tar -xf WordSpoof.tar, which yields a single WordSpoof/ directory. release_meta.json carries both names: "release_name": "WordSpoof" and "build_id": "svd_short_public_v1". WordSpoof is what this dataset is called; the build id is the internal build the bytes came from, kept so the query_sql and source_table_versions in that file stay attributable to a real build. Each manifest.jsonl row carries audio_id, audio_path, split, label, lang, response_kind, prompt_id, prompt_text, source_dataset, provider, provider_version, voice, voice_ref_source, duration_s, sample_rate, codec, and a per-clip sha256. clips 208,734 bona fide 138,555 spoof 70,179 spoof systems 11 language English audio 82.2 h · 16 kHz mono · PCM16 WAV response kinds single_word, yes_no splits train 169,641 · val 19,726 · test 19,367 Bona fide clips come from Google Speech Commands v2 (gsc_v2) and the single-word English segment of Mozilla Common Voice 7.0 (cv_singleword_7_0_en). Spoof clips are generated by this project from 11 systems, a mix of preset-voice and zero-shot cloning: generator clips generator clips qwen_base 15,488 piper 1,887 indextts2 15,480 kokoro 1,863 cosyvoice2 15,130 qwen_cv 1,200 zonos 14,283 orpheus 1,080 chatterbox 2,334 openai 759 magpie 675 Total 70,179. The cells are very unequal — the four largest carry 86% of the spoof side, and magpie has 675 clips against qwen_base's 15,488. A pooled number over this corpus is dominated by four generators, so report per-generator results alongside any pooled figure. For kokoro, the clip count is not a sample size — see Bias, Risks, and Limitations. Dataset Creation Curation Rationale Most public audio-deepfake corpora are sentence-length. Deployed voice interfaces frequently are not — a spoken PIN digit, a "yes", a wake word. This corpus exists to measure detector behaviour on that shorter, differently structured input, and to do so with a public, redistributable artifact so published results can be reproduced independently. Source Data Cloning references come only from the VCTK corpus (CC BY 4.0, CSTR University of Edinburgh) — consenting, published research speakers. No private individual's voice was cloned. Every synthetic clip is labelled spoof. Data Collection and Processing Every spoof clip was scored with CTC ASR for structural defects — empty audio, runaway duration, or more content than was asked for. Measured 2026-09-04 over all 70,179 shipped spoof clips: generator shipped defective rate indextts2 15,480 2,017 13.0% qwen_cv 1,200 112 9.3% openai 759 27 3.6% cosyvoice2 15,130 506 3.3% chatterbox 2,334 62 2.7% orpheus 1,080 9 0.8% piper 1,887 7 0.4% magpie 675 1 0.1% zonos 14,283 10 0.1% qwen_base 15,488 1 0.0% kokoro 1,863 0 0.0% total 70,179 2,752 3.92% By kind: runaway 1,359, runaway+excess_content 903, excess_content 456, empty 34. indextts2 carries 2,017 of the 2,752 — 73% of all defects — on 22% of the spoof side. If you filter one cell, filter that one. Six generators are at or below 1%, and kokoro has none. You can subtract them. A per-clip list ships beside the tarball: WordSpoof_defects.csv 2,752 rowsWordSpoof_defects.README.md Join it on audio_id against manifest.jsonl and drop the matches. What remains is 67,427 spoof clips and 205,982 rows in total, with all 11 generators retained — bona fide clips are untouched, since this is a generator-defect list. The same test rejects almost no real speech. A defect rate means little without knowing how often the test is wrong. The same structural rule layer was run over 4,482 real human clips from the Speech Commands test split — the entire eligible pool, excluding the corpus's own _silence_ and _background_noise_ labels: rejected: 1 of 4,482 = 0.022% So the 3.92% above is not an artefact of a trigger-happy detector. One caveat stated precisely: the release ships Speech Commands' train/val split (105,829 clips) and this was measured on its test split, so it is a held-out estimate from the same corpus and recording conditions rather than a measurement of the shipped clips themselves. Who are the source data producers? Bona fide speech: Google (Speech Commands v2) and the Mozilla Common Voice project's contributors (single-word English segment, Common Voice 7.0). Cloning reference voices: consenting, published speakers from the VCTK corpus (CSTR, University of Edinburgh). Synthetic speech: 11 TTS/voice-cloning systems listed in Dataset Structure, run by the dataset curators. Annotations Not applicable in the crowd-annotation sense. Labels (bonafide / spoof) are assigned at generation time by construction, not by human annotators. Structural-defect verdicts (see Data Collection and Processing) are produced by an automated CTC-ASR-based audit, not by manual annotation. Personal and Sensitive Information The bona fide clips are not filtered and carry no defect list. A glitchy synthetic clip is a generation failure; a noisy human recording is a real recording, which is what a bona fide corpus is for. No private individual's voice was cloned. Cloning references come only from consenting, published research speakers (VCTK). Every synthetic clip is labelled spoof, satisfying disclosure obligations that attach to cloning use (see Licence and Legal Notices). We are not aware of any personal, sensitive, or private information in the bona fide source corpora beyond what their own publishers (Google, Mozilla) have already disclosed and licensed for redistribution. Bias, Risks, and Limitations The corpus carries a measured, unfixed low-level shortcut. A classifier can separate spoof from bona fide using content-blind features alone — no ASR, no transcript, no vocabulary: subset pooled boosted AUC acoustic features only single_word 0.

title: 原生unknown输出位作为模型阵列的调度信号:小模型守门、可查询知识地图与同族加权投票的失效边界(中文版 v1.1)
abstract: 《从零训练的7.74亿参数模型会说"我不知道"》(10.5281/zenodo.22191517) 的阵列线姊妹篇。把不确定性信号从事后估计移到生成时:unknown 作为一级输出类别在模型阵列中升格为元数据位,放大为三种系统能力——守门过滤(37倍泄漏抑制;域外感知在55概念三梯度探针集全部成立,词根捷径在域外不显化)、可查询知识地图(跨seed一致率0.946,分歧自定位known/unknown临界带)、并集-交双专家路由(3000步单元扩展零遗忘)。干净负结果划定信号价值边界:同族阵列内等权/质量/oracle加权与两种追加融合操作全部同判(0.976);而加入携带阵列外信息的单个规则单元后同一探针集升至41/41——"翻案力需要阵列外信息源"从推论升级为实测(M4v3)。v1.1(2026-09-01):回填 M4v3 异质翻案(41/41)与 M2c 锐边界探针(拦截率 11/12,首个词面分类失效单例)。预注册执行,负结果细节如实报告。本 record 为 10.5281/zenodo.22220164 的 v1.1,因 Zenodo 版本更新管线故障以全新 deposition 发布。

title: Integrating Semantic Models and Automated Metadata Enrichment to Advance Environmental Data Interoperability
abstract: The Floods and Droughts Research Infrastructure (FDRI) is delivering advanced field monitoring alongside interoperable digital infrastructure to help us better manage risks from these extremes. Here we present three complementary strands of work that advance semantic standardisation and machine-readability within FDRI and the wider environmental data ecosystem. First, we introduce a site and infrastructure metadata data model designed to harmonise the description of monitoring locations and devices. The model provides a structured, extensible framework to capture key attributes of assets, supporting consistent documentation and integration across systems. Second, we describe the development of a controlled vocabulary for observed environmental properties. This vocabulary aims to standardise the representation of observed properties, enabling improved data discovery and alignment across repositories. By linking terms to persistent identifiers and semantic definitions, it supports FAIR principles and facilitates interoperability with external standards. Third, we present an exploratory study of automated approaches to decompose observed properties according to the I-ADOPT ontology, using the above-mentioned vocabulary as one use case. Observed properties are often captured as unstructured text, limiting their usefulness for discovery and interoperability. This work develops and evaluates multiple methods to extract, structure and map key components to controlled vocabulary terms. The project demonstrates pathways towards scalable enrichment of metadata within operational data services. Together, these efforts illustrate how combining data modelling, vocabulary development and automated semantic annotation can significantly enhance environmental data discoverability and reuse by supporting applications such as advanced search, cross-dataset analysis and AI-driven methods.

title: 基于量子容子的超高精度量子测量算法
abstract: Quantum mechanics offers unprecedented capabilities for information processing and measurement, particularly through the manipulation of quantum states. This paper explores the application of quantum coherence to develop a novel quantum measurement algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement for enhanced data extraction. We present a design for a quantum measurement protocol that utilizes entangled states to achieve significantly higher precision compared to classical measurement techniques. The core mechanism centers on the deliberate establishment and manipulation of entanglement, enabling a direct and efficient mapping of quantum states. This research focuses on the algorithmic intricacies and potential advantages of this approach, demonstrating a pathway toward higher-fidelity data extraction through the utilization of quantum entanglement. The proposed algorithm represents a significant advancement in quantum measurement, offering the potential for breakthroughs in areas such as fundamental physics research, data analysis, and secure communication.

title: Quantum Topology Structure Simulation: Adaptive Topological Transformation
abstract: Quantum topology structure simulation offers a promising approach to modeling and analyzing complex geometric shapes, particularly in fields like materials science and quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum Topology Structure Simulation (QTSS), which leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric transformations during numerical simulations. The core mechanism of QTSS involves the creation of entangled quantum states that represent the underlying topological structure of the geometry being simulated. By manipulating these entangled states, the algorithm enables precise modeling and significantly improves the efficiency of numerical calculations. This work presents a framework for achieving unprecedented accuracy and speed in complex geometric investigations.

evidence.abstract: Quantum topology structure simulation offers a promising approach to modeling and analyzing complex geometric shapes, particularly in fields like materials science and quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum Topology Structure Simulation (QTSS), which leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric transformations during numerical simulations. The core mechanism of QTSS involves the creation of entangled quantum states that represent the underlying topological structure of the geometry being simulated. By manipulating these entangled states, the algorithm enables precise modeling and significantly improves the efficiency of numerical calculations. This work presents a framework for achieving unprecedented accuracy and speed in complex geometric investigations.

title: Automated Program Verification Based on Formal Languages
abstract: This paper explores the potential of automating program verification through the application of formal languages and automated theorem proving (ATP) techniques. The core concept involves translating programs into a formal representation amenable to ATP systems, thereby enabling automated verification of program correctness. The primary goal is to enhance the efficiency and reliability of program verification, ultimately reducing software development costs. This work details a framework for this approach, focusing on the challenges and opportunities presented by this methodology. We investigate techniques for effective program transformation and the selection of appropriate ATP engines. The presented approach offers a pathway towards more robust and trustworthy software systems.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Optimization for Circuit Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to automated circuit design by integrating symbolic regression and Bayesian optimization. The core claim is that this combined methodology offers a significantly more effective strategy compared to utilizing either technique alone. The proposed system leverages Bayesian optimization to efficiently explore the vast design space of potential circuit components and interconnections. Simultaneously, symbolic regression is employed to identify mathematical equations that accurately represent the circuit's operational characteristics. The system iteratively refines both the design space exploration and equation discovery, leading to optimized circuit topologies and behavioral models. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and outlined design principles. The ultimate goal is to significantly reduce the design time and complexity associated with circuit development across diverse applications.

title: ## Broad-Headed Pipistrelle Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Approach
abstract: This paper presents the Broad-Headed Pipistrelle Algorithm (BHPA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of broad-headed pipistrelles (Pipistrellus kuhlii). These bats utilize a unique, expansive search strategy for locating food sources. BHPA leverages this behavior by employing a dynamically expanding search space and a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, maintaining a set of potential solutions. Each solution is represented as a vector, and the algorithm iteratively adjusts these vectors to minimize an objective function. The core innovation lies in the 'head' concept, where each solution maintains a 'head' vector representing its current search direction. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the length and direction of these 'heads', mimicking the bats' broad-headed approach. Performance evaluations using benchmark functions demonstrate that BHPA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance analysis, highlighting its potential for solving complex optimization problems. The key mathematical formulations and notations utilized within the algorithm are presented throughout the text.

title: Brenda's Colilargo: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Capybara
abstract: This paper introduces Brenda's Colilargo, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the behavior of a capybara ( *Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris*). Capybaras are known for their deliberate, cautious, and often meandering movements, particularly when foraging. These characteristics have been translated into a new algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. Brenda's Colilargo combines elements of simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, and a novel 'exploration-exploitation' mechanism based on the capybara's foraging strategy. The algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, iteratively refining them through a combination of probabilistic moves and adaptive adjustments. The core innovation lies in the implementation of a 'colilargo' vector, representing the capybara's exploratory path, which dynamically adjusts the search space. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Brent test function. The results indicate that Brenda's Colilargo achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, with particular strengths in escaping local optima and maintaining exploration throughout the optimization process. Future research will focus on further refining the 'colilargo' vector and exploring its applicability to different problem domains.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Dynamical Models
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a transformative approach to modeling complex dynamical systems, potentially surpassing the capabilities of classical methods. This research investigates the application of quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to simulate intricate multi-scale systems, aiming to achieve unprecedented accuracy and fidelity in capturing system behavior. The core claim is the development of a novel quantum simulation technique capable of accurately modeling complex, multi-scale dynamical systems with high fidelity, significantly exceeding the limitations of classical simulation. This work details the methodology, explores potential challenges, and outlines the key advancements made in this pursuit.

title: Dynamic Topology and Quantum Entanglement: A Coupling Principle
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic topology to model quantum entanglement, proposing a novel coupling mechanism based on dynamically constructed topological structures. We explore the application of dynamic topology algorithms to precisely characterize and manipulate quantum states, aiming to improve the accuracy of quantum state prediction and control. The core claim is that by embedding quantum entanglement within a dynamic topological framework, we can overcome the limitations of classical models and achieve unprecedented fidelity in quantum operations. This work highlights the significance of this approach in advancing quantum information processing.

title: Bobcat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bobcat Hunting Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bobcat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of bobcats. The algorithm leverages the bobcat's strategic stalking, pouncing, and area-searching techniques to effectively explore the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. Bobcat incorporates key elements from bobcat hunting, including a dynamic movement strategy, a probabilistic pounce mechanism, and a territory-based exploration approach. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search, employing a fitness function to evaluate the quality of solutions. Mathematical formulations are provided to detail the algorithm's core operations. The performance of Bobcat is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results indicate that Bobcat exhibits robust performance and adaptability across a range of problem landscapes, making it a promising candidate for various optimization applications.
