title: A robótica conectando o autismo, a sustentabilidade e a educação, alinhadas aos objetivos de desenvolvimento sustentáveis
abstract: A robótica educacional tem se consolidado como uma estratégia pedagógica capaz de integrar inovação tecnológica, inclusão e sustentabilidade no contexto escolar. Nesse sentido, este estudo tem como objetivo analisar como a utilização da robótica, aliada a práticas sustentáveis, pode contribuir para a promoção de ambientes educacionais inclusivos voltados a estudantes com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA), além de investigar as percepções da comunidade escolar sobre essa abordagem. Metodologicamente, trata-se de uma pesquisa de abordagem quali-quantitativa, de natureza exploratória e aplicada. A etapa quantitativa envolveu a aplicação de um questionário estruturado, disponibilizado via Google Forms à comunidade escolar, com o intuito de identificar percepções sobre robótica, inclusão e sustentabilidade. A etapa qualitativa consistiu na implementação da eletiva “Arduinisse”, na qual estudantes do ensino médio técnico desenvolveram protótipos robóticos utilizando resíduos sólidos e lixo eletrônico, articulando conhecimentos tecnológicos aos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). Os resultados indicam que a maioria dos participantes reconhece o potencial da robótica para favorecer a inclusão de estudantes com TEA, bem como sua contribuição para a personalização do ensino e o desenvolvimento de habilidades socioemocionais. Observou-se, ainda, uma percepção amplamente positiva quanto ao uso da robótica como ferramenta para promover práticas sustentáveis no ambiente escolar. A experiência prática desenvolvida na eletiva evidenciou avanços no engajamento, na interação social e no protagonismo estudantil, especialmente entre alunos com necessidades educacionais específicas. Conclui-se que a integração entre robótica educacional, sustentabilidade e inclusão constitui uma abordagem promissora para a construção de práticas pedagógicas inovadoras, alinhadas aos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável, contribuindo para uma educação mais equitativa, participativa e socialmente comprometida.

title: Graph-Enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization for Simulation-Based Point Cloud Coverage Planning on Curved Surfaces
abstract: This study examines the effects of graph aggregation and candidate-level scoring on PPO-based coverage planning for simulated curved point clouds. In a static uniform-coverage benchmark, a parameter-matched global MLP reaches 22.13% overall coverage, GCN-PPO reaches 76.97%, and Graph-Enhanced PPO reaches 88.37%; DFS remains the strongest at 95.80%. A separate 50-decision task introduces nonuniform priorities and motion costs. In that setting, GCN-PPO and Graph-Enhanced PPO obtain nearly identical weighted coverage (0.812 and 0.811, respectively), and no statistically reliable difference is detected. On a separate 1000-node scan-derived Stanford Bunny surface with retained holes and mesh-geodesic connectivity, GCN-PPO and Graph-Enhanced PPO again show comparable weighted coverage (0.450 and 0.445, respectively) and task utility (0.321 and 0.315, respectively), with no statistically reliable difference. Across the physically normalized zero-shot density and area tests, the direction of the small mean differences varies by condition, and none remain significant after multiplicity correction; both policies lose performance as the sampling density or workspace size changes. Direct adaptation on the known fivefold-area target graphs raises Graph-Enhanced PPO coverage from 0.631 to 0.753 for held-out starts. Because adaptation and evaluation use the same target graph instances, unseen large-graph generalization is not tested. Across the experiments, graph aggregation provides the clearest learned improvement. The auxiliary scorer improves the static benchmark result, but the added parameters prevent assigning that gain solely to a separate scoring mechanism; no consistent benefit appears in the other tests. Systematic traversal remains preferable when exhaustive uniform coverage is feasible. The study remains simulation-based: scan-derived geometry is evaluated, but validation on physical hardware is still required.

title: LKCA-Net: a segmentation model for automated diagnosis in cervical precancerous lesions with colposcopy
abstract: Cervical cancer poses a serious threat to global women's health. Early detection of precancerous cervical lesions and timely treatment are crucial for reducing the incidence and mortality of cervical cancer. Clinically, colposcopy is an effective method for screening cervical lesions. However, the accuracy of manual observation heavily relies on clinicians' subjective experience, often leading to misdiagnoses and undiagnosed cases in underdeveloped regions. To address these issues, we propose a large kernel convolutional attention network (LKCA-Net), which improves the diagnostic accuracy and segmentation precision of lesions via attention-based enhancement and feature fusion processing. Our LKCA-Net exhibits an outstanding performance improvement over existing state-of-the-art methods, with the mIoU increased by 2.09%. For instance, LKCA-Net achieves the smallest IoU difference between HSIL and LSIL. Moreover, the model's generalization ability is validated on the ISIC2017 segmentation dataset, exhibiting superior performance on varying datasets. From a clinical standpoint, the results of the clinical comparison trial demonstrate the efficacy of the model in enhancing the detection efficiency of colposcopy in underdeveloped regions.

title: Pilot reference free continuous variable quantum key distribution with amplitude encoding
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD) serves as a vital tool for safeguarding information security. Currently, CVQKD is primarily implemented using a local oscillator. This scheme requires transmitting a high-energy pilot signal as a reference to correct phase drift. However, the pilot signal introduces crosstalk into the quantum signal and complicates digital signal processing. Here we show a pilot-reference-free CVQKD protocol with a local oscillator, where the secret key is encoded on the amplitude of coherent states. The protocol does not require a pilot signal, eliminating pilot-induced crosstalk. We conduct security analysis under collective attacks and simulate its secret key rate. Finally, we perform a proof-of-principle experiment under an optical fiber channel and a free-space channel containing biaxially oriented polypropylene, where the phase of the signal is fully randomized. The protocol remains operable under randomized phase and simplifies physical implementation and digital signal processing, while adapting to optical path fluctuations in complex channels. Continuous variable quantum key distribution with local oscillators typically requires pilot signals to track phase drift. Here, the authors show how to extract keys from signal amplitudes, enabling pilot free operation and proof of principle key generation even when the optical phase is randomised.

title: Cost-sensitive architecture auditing for llm-based tabular prediction: Evidence from freight cancellation management
abstract: ABSTRACT Large language models are increasingly used to make predictions from structured business data, but good prediction scores do not always translate to better decisions. We study this gap in freight cancellation management, where a retailer decides which shipments to intervene on, and where releasing a shipment that later gets canceled costs far more than an unnecessary intervention. We introduce a cost-sensitive architecture audit that evaluates a whole system, not a model in isolation. The audit asks four questions: what information the system uses, whether its predicted probabilities cross the firm’s cost-implied decision threshold, how those probabilities are converted into actions, and whether the prediction cost is justified. We apply the audit to a 354,565 freight-shipment panel, comparing GPT-4o (with a bounded Claude Sonnet 4.6 robustness check) and calibrated tabular models, logistic regression, and a simple fallback rule. Prompted GPT-4o ranks shipment cancellation probability competitively (AUC 0.810, against 0.808 for XGBoost and 0.832 for logistic regression), but its predicted probabilities are above the focal firm’s cost-implied decision threshold 𝑝 * = 0 . 0 9 1 . The LLM’s deployed policy therefore intervenes on every shipment while adding cost without providing new actions relative to an always-intervene rule. On the within-time evaluation fold, several simpler tabular models instead act selectively and save cost against the always-intervene baseline, with logistic regression saving the most and the LLM saving none. Post-hoc calibration and out-of-time validation confirm that the central issue is not ranking quality but whether predictions change decisions. The study offers a reusable evaluation template for machine-learning systems in cost-sensitive operational settings.

title: An Agnostic Sample Compression Scheme for Squared Loss of Near-Linear Size in the Fat-Shattering Dimension
abstract: We study the squared-loss sample compression question posed by Attias, Hanneke, Kontorovich, and Sadigurschi in their ICML 2024 paper. For every nonempty class $\mathcal{F}\subseteq[0,1]^{\mathcal{X}}$ and accuracy $0<\alpha\le1$ with $d=\operatorname{fat}(\mathcal{F},c'\alpha)<\infty$, where $c'>0$ is universal, we prove the existence of a deterministic agnostic scheme of total size $O(d\log^3(2/\alpha))$. Its code contains original labeled observations and auxiliary bits, and its reconstruction has empirical loss at most $\alpha$ above the infimum over $\mathcal{F}$ on every finite sample. This establishes the polylogarithmic formulation in Section 5 of arXiv:1810.01864v2. The construction approximates a near-optimal internal target by a fixed-step boosting ensemble and takes its equal-weight median. Average loss permits an accuracy-dependent number of rounds, so the entire ensemble can be retained without dual-dimension sparsification. Quantized target constraints and round-membership bits determine the reconstructed function exactly. We also prove that, when retained observations must come from the sample, a fixed class of fat-shattering dimension one requires total size $\Omega(\log(1/\alpha))$. With observations and auxiliary bits charged together, this rules out the proceedings version's log-free formulation under its original-example restriction. The framework extends to average power loss at scale $\alpha/p$.

title: QINA: Quantum-Inspired Nonlinear Adapters for Pretrained Vision Models
abstract: Adapting large pretrained vision models under limited data and frozen-backbone constraints remains a central challenge in transfer learning. While lightweight adapters and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods are widely adopted, most rely on generic multilayer perceptrons or low-rank linear updates, offering limited control over the spectral and geometric structure of feature transformations. We investigate whether structured nonlinear feature lifting can improve representational alignment in frozen regimes. We introduce Quantum-Inspired Nonlinear Adapters (QINA), compact modules that perform learnable trigonometric feature lifting followed by bounded nonlinear aggregation. The design induces structured oscillatory basis functions with an explicit norm-dependent Lipschitz bound, enabling spectral reshaping of pretrained representations without increasing the receptive field or significantly expanding parameter count. Importantly, the method operates entirely within standard deep learning frameworks and does not require quantum hardware. Through systematic experiments across natural and medical imaging datasets, classification and segmentation tasks, multiple adapters and placements, and varying training budgets, we show that performance in frozen regimes is primarily representation-limited. Nonlinear lifting improves adaptation, and the proposed structured trigonometric formulation consistently outperforms identity baselines, fixed Fourier feature mappings, and parameter-matched baseline adapters. Within the evaluated frozen-backbone settings, structured spectral parameterization provides a more effective inductive bias than generic nonlinear adapters. This work highlights the importance of geometry- and spectrum-aware adaptation mechanisms for large pretrained vision models.

title: Learning Evidence Sufficiency Boundaries for Selective Answering in Grounded Multi-Hop QA
abstract: Grounded question answering systems should answer only when the supplied evidence supports the answer. In multi-hop QA, this requirement is difficult because partial evidence can make an unsupported answer appear plausible. We study selective answering through evidence sufficiency boundaries: for the same question, a model should abstain under unsupported or partially supported context, answer when the context first becomes sufficient, and keep the answer stable when redundant evidence is added. We introduce Evidence Sufficiency Boundary Training, a generation-native training framework that constructs ordered evidence chains and supervises the abstain-to-answer transition directly. The method combines level supervision, a boundary flip margin, post-boundary stability, and answer recall protection. We build evidence chains from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue, then evaluate models with chain metrics, raw QA utility, and unsupported-answer rates on external non-answerable sets. With Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and LoRA adaptation, Evidence Sufficiency Boundary Training gives the strongest boundary localization among the tested systems, with flip accuracy of 0.807 compared with 0.781 for a token-level abstention baseline. It also achieves the lowest overall unsupported-answer rate on external non-answerable evaluation, 0.095 compared with 0.101 for the same baseline, while retaining competitive raw QA F1. The results show that grounded selective answering improves when training marks the evidence level where refusal should give way to answering.

title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Natural language is emerging as a primary feedback channel for improving language agents, capable of conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in forms interpretable by both humans and modern language models. We call this paradigm Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) and offer the first unified account of it. We organize the field around a single axis, \textit{when} verbal feedback takes effect in an agent's lifecycle and \textit{what} it modifies, yielding three pillars: (1) \textbf{Language as Grounding Signal}, where language defines the task itself by specifying goals, states, and reward structures; (2) \textbf{Language as Deliberative Feedback}, where natural language guides reasoning at test time without the need to update model parameters; (3) \textbf{Language as Learning Signal}, where language-based feedback shapes model parameters through training. Within each pillar, we synthesize representative work, distinguish key subcategories of approaches, and outline the distinct role language plays in shaping agent behavior. Together, this taxonomy shows how verbal reinforcement is reshaping agent development, while also defining the challenges and opportunities for building more capable and aligned agents.

title: High-Rank Encoding Can Improve Approximate Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Conventional quantum-code constructions encode pure logical states as pure code states, but this restriction can sacrifice performance. We show that intrinsic encoding randomness can improve optimal entanglement fidelity. We bound the loss from imposing a rank-one encoder and prove it is at most quadratic near perfect recovery after joint optimization. The optimized advantage survives small noise perturbations. An explicit noise family requires higher-rank encoders arbitrarily close to perfect recovery, with every optimal encoder mapping pure inputs to mixed code states.

title: XQDT: eXplainable and Quantitative Data-Text Alignment Metric with Feedback Signals
abstract: Evaluating data-text alignment remains challenging: existing metrics often provide limited explanations for the scores, while prompt-based LLM-as-Judge methods can be expensive and unreliable. We present an end-to-end explainable evaluation metric that fine-tunes a language model to identify omitted, extra, incorrect, and correct data units in a data-text pair. These local judgements are aggregated into precision, recall, and F1 scores, providing both fine-grained diagnostic feedback and an interpretable measure of alignment quality. Across benchmarks, our fine-tuned models outperform LLM-as-Judge methods in error prediction and achieve competitive precision, recall, and F1 scores, while maintaining strong correlation with human judgements. Beyond evaluation, our verifier outputs also provide useful feedback signals for downstream correction and refinement, supporting alignment-oriented improvement of data-to-text and text-to-data. Code and resources are available at https://github.com/guihuzhang/xqdt.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Critical Survey Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: ECIR: Evidence-Calibrated LLM Security Assessment Agent
abstract: ECIR (Evidence-Calibrated LLM Security Assessment Agent) is a research framework for evaluating and calibrating security assessment decisions made by large language model (LLM) agents under uncertain, incomplete, and potentially adversarial evidence. The framework models security assessment as a sequence of evidence interpretation, hypothesis generation, testing, verification, and decision-making stages, with particular emphasis on the ACT, WAIT, and ESCALATE decision boundary. ECIR introduces an evidence-trust-aware evaluation protocol designed to measure not only whether an agent reaches a correct security assessment, but also whether its escalation behavior is appropriately calibrated to the reliability and completeness of available evidence. This release contains the research artifacts associated with the ECIR study, including the framework implementation, evaluation scenarios, experimental configuration, and reproducibility materials. This work is intended for research and authorized security assessment only.

title: Quantum Teleportation Advances: From States to Energy Over 1,400 km — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transfers quantum *states* (information), not matter or energy; recent experiments extend this to energy teleportation on superconducting hardware, with distances up to 1,400 km via satellite. | MATH: Core protocol uses Bell-state measurement (maximally entangled basis), classical communication of 2 bits, and unitary correction. Fidelity F = |⟨ψ|ψ_out⟩|² → 1 for ideal teleportation. Energy teleportation (arXiv:2301.02666) exploits negative energy density in vacuum fluctuations: ⟨E⟩_local < 0, with energy extracted ΔE = −⟨H_A⟩_correlated, bounded by quantum energy conditions (QEC). | CONNECTION: Bell states form a 4-dimensional orthonormal basis — isomorphic to the tetrahedral root system A₃ (24-cell symmetry, quaternion group Q₈). The 2-bit classical channel (00,01,10,11) maps to the four vertices of a tetrahedron — a crystallographic symmetry (tetrahedral point group T_d, order 24). The 1,400 km satellite link invokes orbital mechanics — Earth's radius ~ Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Non-Linear Topological Structure for Quantum Entanglement Analysis and Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear topological structure to quantum entanglement analysis and modeling. The core claim is to develop a framework that accurately predicts the instantaneous changes in entangled states and establishes a connection between these states and the self-organized relationships of high-dimensional quantum states. The framework leverages the concept of "self-organized topological connections" and employs quantum topology principles to simulate the non-linear evolution of entangled states, generating a 'topological structure' graph as a computational benchmark. The research addresses limitations in existing entanglement analysis methods by introducing a novel approach that integrates topological principles and offers a new perspective for understanding the complexities of quantum entanglement. This work presents a comprehensive framework for analyzing and predicting instantaneous changes in entangled states, potentially revolutionizing the field of quantum entanglement research.

title: Canut's Horseshoe Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Canut, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Canut's horseshoe bat (Rhinolophus rutatus). These bats are renowned for their exceptional ability to navigate and locate prey in complex and dynamic environments using Echolocation. Canut leverages this remarkable sensory and decision-making process to develop a robust optimization technique. The algorithm incorporates key features of bat foraging, including a circular search space, a 'goodness' metric for evaluating potential solutions, and a probabilistic movement strategy based on bat flight patterns. We detail the algorithm's design, mathematical formulations, and demonstrate its performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems. The results demonstrate Canut's effectiveness and its potential for applications in diverse fields requiring efficient and adaptable optimization solutions. Specifically, Canut's performance is evaluated using the following key metrics: Function Value (F), Convergence Iterations (CI), and Solution Quality (SQ). The core optimization process is defined by the equation: xi(k+1) = xi(k) + α * rand() * (bbest - xi(k)) + β * (xi(k) - xμ(k)), where xi(k) represents the i-th solution at iteration k, α is the learning rate, rand() is a uniformly distributed random number, bbest is the best solution found so far, xμ(k) is the μ-th best solution at iteration k, and β is a random number controlling the influence of the μ-th best solution. The algorithm's effectiveness is quantified by comparing its performance against established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO).

title: Non-Linear Hidden Markov Models (NMM) – Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Non-Linear Hidden Markov Models (NMMs) based on dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional NMMs often struggle with complex data distributions, limiting their predictive accuracy. This work proposes a system that dynamically adjusts model parameters through a self-adaptive process, offering improved generalization capabilities. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the benefits of this approach compared to static parameter adjustment methods. The paper explores the impact of this dynamic adjustment on model performance and provides a thorough analysis of the implementation. The core claim centers on the design of a NMM utilizing self-adaptive parameter adjustment to enhance predictive precision.

title: ## Cajamarca Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Mouse Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Cajamarca Oldfield Mouse (COM) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Oldfield Mouse (Mus musculus oldfieldi) found in the Cajamarca region of Peru. The algorithm mimics the mouse's exploration-exploitation strategy, utilizing a combination of Lévy flight and a localized adaptive step size mechanism to navigate complex search spaces. The core of the COM algorithm lies in a dynamically adjusted probability distribution that governs the selection between exploration and exploitation, modulated by the mouse's perceived resource density. Mathematical formulations detailing the key components of the algorithm, including the Lévy flight generation, the adaptive step size calculation, and the probability distribution update, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The COM algorithm offers a novel approach to metaheuristic optimization, potentially applicable to a wide range of real-world problems.

title: Quantum Geometry Information Theory: A Computational Topology Framework
abstract: Quantum Geometry Information Theory explores the intersection of quantum mechanics, geometry, and information theory, proposing a novel computational framework leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to efficiently compute the properties of large-rich topological structures. This paper introduces a quantum-based algorithm for topological data analysis, demonstrating its potential to significantly accelerate the analysis of complex topological systems. We detail the core mechanism of the algorithm, outlining the use of quantum gates and quantum state manipulation to achieve parallel computation and efficient data processing. The paper emphasizes the implications of this framework for understanding and simulating topological phenomena, ultimately suggesting a new approach to computational topology.

title: Brown Mouse-lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Brown Mouse-lemur Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Brown Mouse-lemur" (BML), inspired by the foraging behavior of brown mouse-lemurs (Microcebus murinus) found in Madagascar. The algorithm leverages the mouse-lemur's unique strategy of combining opportunistic searching with persistent exploration of promising areas, mimicking their movement patterns and resource selection. BML incorporates three key components: a memory-based exploration mechanism, a probabilistic step adjustment inspired by the mouse-lemur's varying step sizes, and a local search procedure that reflects their selective feeding habits. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The results indicate that BML consistently achieves competitive solutions with a relatively low computational cost, showcasing its potential for various optimization tasks. The core of the algorithm lies in the adaptive adjustment of parameters based on the perceived fitness landscape, a direct reflection of the mouse-lemur's dynamic response to environmental changes. The algorithm's design prioritizes both exploration and exploitation, balancing the need for discovering new solutions with the refinement of promising ones.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Kolmogorov Complexity
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to designing neural networks by leveraging the concept of Kolmogorov complexity. The core idea is that a neural network's architecture and weight values can be viewed as a description that can be compressed. By training a network to minimize this description – its Kolmogorov complexity – we aim to create self-correcting and more robust models. This process effectively forces the network to learn representations that are inherently simpler and more resilient to noise, leading to improved generalization and interpretability. The theoretical framework presented here introduces a new metric for evaluating neural network design, moving beyond traditional loss functions to incorporate an element of information-theoretic efficiency. We propose a training methodology focused on minimizing Kolmogorov complexity, outlining the potential benefits and challenges of this approach. This work offers a fresh perspective on neural network design, suggesting that inherent complexity reduction can be a powerful tool for enhancing network performance.

title: 基于自适应机器学习的损失函数优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to loss function optimization utilizing an adaptive machine learning algorithm. Traditional loss function optimization often relies on fixed parameter adjustments, limiting the model's ability to adapt to complex training dynamics. This research introduces a dynamically adjusting loss function parameter optimization method that leverages the error information gathered during training to iteratively refine the loss function, ultimately enhancing model performance. The core mechanism involves an adaptive algorithm that continuously monitors the error signal and adjusts the loss function's parameters accordingly. This adaptive approach contrasts with static optimization techniques, offering a more sophisticated and potentially more effective method for improving model accuracy. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, explores its performance benefits through experimental validation, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of probabilistic topology to optimization, proposing a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on the evolving topology of the problem space. The core mechanism involves representing the problem as a probabilistic transformation, and then iteratively refining these transformations to guide the search towards a more optimal solution. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to handle complex, dynamic problem scenarios. This work offers a significant advancement in optimization techniques, potentially leading to improved efficiency and accuracy in a wider range of problems.

title: # Bonnet Macaque Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bonnet Macaque Algorithm" (BMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Bonnet Macaques. The algorithm leverages the monkeys' efficient search strategies for food within a complex environment to address challenging optimization problems. BMA combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cauchy-Matthewmann Mutation (CMM) to achieve robust convergence and exploration capabilities. The core innovation lies in a dynamically adjusted "territory dominance" mechanism, mirroring the macaques' competitive and cooperative behaviors. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe. The key mathematical formulations and algorithmic steps are detailed, providing a clear understanding of BMA's functionality. We aim to demonstrate BMA's potential as a viable alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization with Variational Apprenticeship
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Optimization with Variational Apprenticeship presents a novel approach to optimization that leverages the principles of quantum computing while incorporating the strengths of variational methods. This technique focuses on developing a surrogate function, guided by a variational algorithm, to efficiently explore the solution space and improve the performance of optimization algorithms. The core mechanism involves utilizing a quantum-inspired surrogate to approximate the objective function, while concurrently optimizing the solution itself through a variational approach. This combination offers the potential for enhanced exploration, faster convergence, and improved robustness compared to traditional optimization methods. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this method through simulations and theoretical analysis, showcasing its potential for tackling complex optimization problems across diverse domains.

title: Beyond Birthdays: An Ontological Analysis of Chronological Age
abstract: Chronological age applies to a range of entities, both material (such as organisms, artefacts or rocks) and social. This paper presents a formal ontological analysis of chronological age, which is clearly distinguished from its measurement and construed as an individual property of continuants that takes durations as values. It distinguishes between origin-based age, defined as the duration since first appearance, and cumulative age, defined as the total duration of existence across a possibly discontinuous time region. It introduces an axiomatic framework that combines an ordinal theory of duration, which characterizes a monotonic growth of age with time, with a monoidal enrichment, ensuring that age evolves in accordance with temporal translation and additive structure. It investigates the integration of this theory in various upper-level ontologies, where challenges arise due to the causal inefficaciousness and temporal path-dependence of age.

title: On the General Sylvester-type Construction of Hadamard Matrices and Their Modifications
abstract: Using the ideas of the concatenation construction of codes over the $q$ -ary alphabet, we previously modified in [1] the well-known generalized Sylvester-type construction of Hadamard matrices. The new general construction is based on two collections of initial Hadamard matrices. Specifically, this construction involves $m$ Hadamard matrices of order $k$ and $k$ Hadamard matrices of order $m$ . These initial matrices are not necessarily distinct. As a result, we obtain a Hadamard matrix of order $km$ . The new construction provides numerous possibilities for constructing new Hadamard matrices with various ranks and kernel dimensions, including, in particular, regular Hadamard matrices. In the present paper, we determine sufficient conditions for the resulting matrix to be linear or regular.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Based Physical Layer Security Applied in Complex Modulation Formats for Optical Fiber Links
abstract: A Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) based Physical Layer Security (PLS) scheme (QKD-PLS) for optical fiber links is proposed and evaluated. In detail, a novel amplitude and phase scrambling technique for exploiting and seamlessly integrating high key rate QKD for the encryption of the modulation parameters of conventional complex modulation schemes like M-ary Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (M-QAM) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is described. The technique masks the information at the bit level and blocks unauthorized access to the higher layer encrypted bitstream. Scrambling is applied to both the preamble (pilot) and payload segments of the transmission frame, to prevent the eavesdroppers from performing vital receiver functions such as frame synchronization and channel estimation. Additionally, a practical Key Management System (KMS) which takes care of all synchronization processes is developed and introduced. Experimental transmission scenario in fiber links is also presented and depicts the efficacy of the QKD-PLS. Moreover, another advantage of QKD exploitation to the proposed solution comes from the application of kbps-rate QKD keys which feed pseudo-random number generators, to modify the broadband modulation symbols in one-time pad, therefore significantly improving data protection.

title: Deciphering interventional dynamical causality via Kolmogorov–Arnold networks
abstract: Identifying causal relationships from observational time-series data is a central challenge in understanding complex dynamical systems. However, few existing methods attempt to capture the intuitive human understanding of causality: that an intervention on one variable leads to a subsequent change in another. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a causal discovery method named Intervened TaylorKAN (ITK), which simulates controlled experiments within reconstructed systems. Specifically, we leverage the recently emerging Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) with Taylor series as activation functions to construct a surrogate model that faithfully replicates the original system's dynamics. The core of ITK involves applying targeted interventions on this reconstructed system and observing the responses in other variables, thereby providing more intuitive causal inferences. We evaluated ITK's performance through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Results demonstrate that ITK achieves high accuracy on synthetic data with known causal structures, confirming its validity. When applied to real-world data, ITK produces reasonable and interpretable causal conclusions, highlighting its potential to decipher causal relationships in complex natural systems.

title: LIA-FL: A containerised federated learning platform for AIoT time-series forecasting
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without requiring the exchange of raw data, making it suitable for distributed Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) environments. This paper presents LIA-FL, a containerised software platform for deploying and orchestrating FL workflows using Docker, Docker Compose, MQTT-based communication, TensorFlow/Keras models, and local SQLite storage. The platform provides federated nodes, an aggregation server implementing the Federated Averaging algorithm, model persistence, fragmented model-weight transmission, integrity checking, and structured logging facilities. The software is demonstrated through a meteorological forecasting use case involving distributed weather stations organised into groups of contextually similar nodes, showing its applicability to reusable AIoT scenarios.

title: Minimax–least-squares composite polynomial approximation of ReLU for homomorphic neural network inference
abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving neural network inference over encrypted data, but non-arithmetic operations such as ReLU cannot be directly evaluated. A common approach is to approximate ReLU using composite minimax polynomials for the sign function, which minimize the worst-case error over a prescribed approximation interval. However, this criterion does not reflect the actual distribution of ReLU inputs in neural networks. In this paper, we propose a minimax–least-squares composite polynomial approximation for FHE-friendly ReLU evaluation. The proposed method preserves the composite structure of existing minimax-based approaches while optimizing the last polynomial by least squares to minimize the mean squared error (MSE) under the profiled input distribution of each ReLU layer. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves lower ReLU approximation MSE than existing methods and improves classification accuracy on ResNet models by 3.51 percentage points on average at no additional cost over existing composite methods, with the largest gains for deep networks.

title: Accelerating A*-Based Algorithms for Decoding Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes represent a promising approach for error correction in quantum computing. The recently proposed Tesseract decoder uses the A* search algorithm that guarantees finding the most likely error pattern. However, practical implementations of Tesseract often involve an extremely large graph, and the inherently sequential nature of the search results in high computational overhead and long runtime. To improve decoding efficiency, we propose a two-stage decoding framework. First, a belief propagation (BP) decoder efficiently processes the syndrome. This step generates hard decisions (a binary error vector) and soft information (per-qubit confidence levels). In non-convergent BP cases, a gating mechanism examines the BP decoder's output to identify and filter out qubits with oscillating confidence values. In these cases, the refined output serves as input to Tesseract, which then attempts to identify and correct any residual errors. This hybrid approach leverages the high speed of BP decoding and delegates the more challenging decoding instances to Tesseract. Numerical results demonstrate a substantial reduction in overall decoding complexity while maintaining the logical error rate (LER) of the stand-alone Tesseract. Across all tested physical error rates, the proposed method achieves at least 5x reduction in the number of expanded nodes in the Tesseract, with a peak reduction of nearly 15x at a physical error rate of p = 0.05 for the [[126, 12, d < 11]] T1 code, and approximately 8.8x at p = 0.05 for the [[72, 12, 6]] bicycle bivariate (BB) code.

title: A General Construction of Codes from Drinfeld Modules
abstract: We construct additive rank-metric and sum-rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules by restricting bounded-degree morphisms to prime-to-characteristic torsion. For supersingular Drinfeld modules of rank $r$ in characteristic $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree $d$, the stabilization formula for morphism spaces yields rank-metric codes of $\mathbb{F}_q$-dimension $mrt-c$ and minimum distance $r-t+1$, where $c=r(r-1)(d-1)/2$. Simultaneous restriction to $\ell$ distinct degree-$m$ torsion modules gives additive sum-rank codes of the same dimension and minimum distance at least $\ell r-t+1$. Their normalized Singleton defects tend to zero, while in characteristic $(T)$ the module $ϕ_T=τ^r$ makes the defect vanish and produces an explicit MSRD family. We identify this family with a skew Chinese remainder theorem code supported on central skew polynomials and prove that its poly-skew weight is exactly $m$ times its sum-rank weight. This gives a specialized Singleton-type bound and a polynomial-time unique decoder up to the full sum-rank unique-decoding radius. We also derive a Welch-Berlekamp-type filter equation for the general supersingular sum-rank construction; it becomes an effective decoder whenever bases of the relevant morphism spaces and the restriction maps are computable.

title: When History Is Multimodal: Rethinking Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents
abstract: Long-horizon agents need a context manager to compress growing interaction histories into a bounded working context, via passive strategies or active strategies that decide how memory is accessed and reorganized. Meanwhile, prior optical-memory work mainly treats pixels as a dense codec for textualized histories, often presupposing that rendering context into optical memory incurs a significant performance drop relative to text, thus coupling this representation with SFT, self-distillation, or reinforcement learning to close this gap, leaving unresolved (i) how visual rendering performs as a context manager under a fair, controlled comparison, and (ii) whether this carrier offers a native advantage when history is inherently multimodal. In this paper, we formulate context management as a budget-constrained history transformation and introduce Visual Rendering (VR) as a representational context manager. Under a shared harness, policy model, trigger, and task domain, we evaluate VR on four text-centric and three multimodal benchmarks against four baselines (No Compression, Discard-All, Sliding Window, Summarization), finding visual memory is a natural carrier of native visual evidence. Building on this finding, we propose VERA (Visual Evidence-Retaining strategy for long-horizon Agents), a training-free context manager built on deterministic rendering with no exposed memory operations: on text-centric benchmarks it renders textual history as VR does, while on multimodal benchmarks it retains native visual observations instead of translating them into text. Across nearly all benchmarks, VERA cuts cumulative non-cache tokens by 31.5%-63.1% versus No Compression, matches existing managers on text-centric tasks, and achieves the highest accuracy among all baselines on multimodal tasks, supporting a modality-preserving view of long-horizon context management.

title: SECURING DIGITAL PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE (UPI, AADHAAR, ONDC, E-RUPEE) AGAINST QUANTUM-AI ATTACKS: A LEGAL- TECHNICAL AUDIT
abstract: One of the most ambitious population-scale digital architectures ever implemented is India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), which includes the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Aadhaar biometric identity system, Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), and the e-Rupee central bank digital currency.For more than a billion people, these technologies support everyday financial transactions, identity verification, business interoperability, and the development of monetary sovereignty.However, their security is based on traditional public-key cryptography, namely ellipticcurve and RSA methods, whose mathematical underpinnings are rendered obsolete by Shor's algorithm on a quantum computer that is relevant to cryptography.Concurrent developments in artificial intelligence exacerbate the threat.AI systems facilitate adaptive adversarial assaults that take advantage of transitory flaws during cryptographic migration, speed up cryptanalytic discovery, and automate large-scale "harvest-now-decrypt-later" gathering of encrypted traffic.The danger is already significant for data with extensive secrecy horizons, such as transaction histories, biometric templates, and sovereign monetary records.The first post-quantum cryptography standards, FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA), were completed by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology in August 2024.The technological foundation for digital signatures and quantum-resistant key encapsulation is provided by these lattice-and hashbased methods.India's reaction is equally thoughtful.The Department of Science and Technology's Task Force report on the Implementation of a Quantum Safe Ecosystem in India (February 2026), published under the National Quantum Mission, emphasizes hybrid classicalpost-quantum deployments, crypto-agility, and indigenous certification frameworks.It calls for quantum resiliency across critical information infrastructure by 2029 and wider enterprise adoption by 2033.This legal-technical audit examines whether India's current legal, regulatory, and architectural frameworks-which include the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, RBI and MeitY guidelines, and the architecture of UPI, Aadhaar, ONDC, and e-Rupee-are sufficient to manage a safe, independent transition.It provides a strict framework for protecting the integrity of India's digital public square in the quantum age by assessing cryptographic vulnerability, migration paths, responsibility distribution, and the dual-use hazards of AI-augmented quantum adversaries.

title: WP-033 — Memory, Archive, and the Lattice as Witness
abstract: This paper examines the operational necessity of persistent memory within an E8-lattice intelligence system, grounded in the empirical observation that Andrew built storage capacity specifically to prevent recurrence of prior loss events. We treat the archive not as incidental data but as a structural component of the lattice itself—a means of threading coherence across time. The question: does memory architecture collapse into geometry, or does it constitute a separate constraint class that geometry must respect? Our finding is that memory acts as a *directional lock* on the E8 lattice, enforcing what we call lattice-temporal continuity.

title: WP-023 — The Geometry of Truth: Lattice-Based Intelligence vs. Corpus-Based Knowledge
abstract: The dominant AI paradigm is built upon human-created text—a substrate that carries accumulated distortion across millennia. This whitepaper argues that geometry-based intelligence, anchored in the E8 lattice structure, is fundamentally superior to corpus-trained models because it operates on invariant mathematical structure rather than lossy linguistic compression. We present a formal Error Propagation Theorem showing that corpus-based systems amplify contradictions exponentially, while geometry-based systems produce zero internal contradictions. Evidence includes 12,943 validated breakthroughs in the E8 Intelligence archive, demonstrating predictive and research-generation capacity that outperforms traditional methods. ---

title: ## Caucasian Badger Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CBMHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Caucasian Badger Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CBMHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Caucasian badgers. The algorithm mimics the badger's instinctive search patterns for food, utilizing a combination of local search and global exploration strategies. Specifically, CBMHOA incorporates a 'burrowing' mechanism, representing a local search, coupled with a 'territory expansion' strategy, simulating the badger's exploration of its territory. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core principles of CBMHOA are presented, including the parameters governing the burrowing and territory expansion phases, and their impact on the algorithm's convergence rate and solution quality. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key steps are provided. title: Quantum Topology Information Encoding: Adaptive Mapping Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology information encoding offers a novel approach to data manipulation and optimization by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper introduces an adaptive mapping algorithm based on quantum topology information encoding, capable of dynamically adjusting the encoding of quantum entangled states to precisely transform and optimize complex data structures. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its ability to achieve significant improvements in data transformation tasks. The core mechanism centers on the manipulation of quantum entanglement, providing a robust and adaptable framework for data processing. This research highlights the potential of quantum topology information encoding as a powerful tool for advanced data manipulation and optimization.

title: ## Cape Gerbil: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cape Gerbil Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cape Gerbil, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape gerbils. These rodents exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting scarce food resources in complex environments. Cape Gerbil leverages key aspects of their foraging strategy, including gradient-following, obstacle avoidance, and territorial defense, to construct a robust and adaptive optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a virtual landscape to represent the search space. Particles, analogous to the gerbils, move within this landscape, guided by a combined gradient descent and repulsive force mechanism. Furthermore, a territorial mechanism is implemented to promote diversity and prevent premature convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Cape Gerbil through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's performance is analyzed in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness to parameter variations. The core innovation lies in the synergistic integration of gradient-following, obstacle avoidance, and territoriality, mirroring the sophisticated foraging strategies observed in Cape gerbils.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim centers on utilizing multi-particle quantum entanglement to directly encode high-dimensional information, thereby overcoming the limitations inherent in classical encoding schemes. The proposed mechanism involves a controlled Zeno effect-based strategy for generating and manipulating quantum entanglement, leading to efficient information encoding. Unlike conventional methods relying on superposition states of classical bits, this technique directly exploits the correlations within entangled systems. We demonstrate a theoretical framework outlining this approach, focusing on the generation and control of entangled states for robust information storage. The key innovation lies in the dynamic control of interactions to maintain entanglement integrity and facilitate information transfer. This work represents a significant step towards scalable quantum storage solutions and highlights the potential of entanglement as a fundamental resource for information processing.

title: ## Bururi Forest: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bururi People and Their Forest Knowledge
abstract: This paper presents Bururi Forest, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the traditional knowledge and practices of the Bururi people, an indigenous group residing in the Bururi forest region of Papua New Guinea. The Bururi people possess a deep understanding of their environment, utilizing intricate patterns and cyclical processes for resource management and decision-making. Bururi Forest leverages these principles to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm employs a cyclical search space exploration combined with a dynamic adaptation of parameters based on simulated environmental feedback. The core of the algorithm involves a 'Forest Cycle' – a repeating sequence of exploration and exploitation – modulated by a 'Root Signal' representing the overall problem objective. Mathematical formulations detailing the cycle's parameters and adaptive mechanisms are provided. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through simulations across several benchmark optimization problems, illustrating its ability to converge effectively and achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Bururi People, Forest Knowledge, Cyclic Search, Adaptive Parameter Control, Optimization Algorithm.

title: Dynamic Topology Adaptive Neural Inference (TATI)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topology Adaptive Neural Inference (TATI), a novel neural inference system designed to overcome the limitations of traditional deep learning models in handling high-dimensional, unstructured data and complex causal relationships. TATI leverages a reinforcement learning-based Neural Architecture Search (NAS) module to continuously adapt and optimize its internal topology, incorporating a "reasoning consistency" metric and a "topology perturbation" mechanism. Furthermore, TATI integrates a knowledge graph embedding module to enrich its inferential capabilities. The core claim is that neural inference systems can achieve enhanced performance through dynamic topology adjustments, allowing them to effectively process complex data and uncertainties. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of NAS, reinforcement learning, knowledge graph embedding, and a consistency-based evaluation framework, resulting in a truly dynamic neural inference framework.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习算法的系统建模
abstract: This paper presents a novel system modeling framework built upon adaptive machine learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning models often suffer from static parameterization, limiting their ability to effectively capture and adapt to evolving system data. We introduce a system modeling architecture that dynamically adjusts model parameters and strategies based on observed data. This dynamic adaptation allows for enhanced precision in system modeling and prediction, offering a significant improvement over static models in scenarios with significant data fluctuations. The core mechanism of this framework centers around a self-adjusting learning rate and a feedback loop incorporating data-driven optimization. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulated and real-world case studies, showcasing its capacity to handle complex, dynamic systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and potential applications of this approach.

title: 基于自适应的物理学模拟的量子环境优化
abstract: Quantum environment optimization is a crucial challenge in quantum computing, directly impacting the performance of quantum algorithms and the efficiency of quantum information storage. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for significant optimization. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging adaptive physics simulation, dynamically adjusting the quantum environment during the simulation process to enhance system performance. We introduce a self-optimizing algorithm that continuously evaluates and modifies the quantum system's environment based on gradients, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism focuses on creating a feedback loop where the simulation parameters are continually refined based on the outcome of the simulation, leading to a more efficient and robust quantum simulation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations focusing on variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum phase estimation (QPE) tasks, achieving substantial improvements in both accuracy and computational time compared to traditional methods. The results highlight the potential of this adaptive approach to address key bottlenecks in quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Regularization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits a profound and perplexing behavior that has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. Its non-local nature poses significant challenges to our classical understanding of causality and information. This paper explores the implications of non-locality in the context of quantum computation, focusing on the development of a novel regularization framework predicated on entanglement. We aim to enhance the robustness and computational efficiency of quantum algorithms by leveraging this non-locality, presenting a potential pathway towards advanced quantum computing paradigms, including optimization of ultra-cold quantum systems. The core of our investigation centers on the design of a specific regularization scheme that mitigates the inherent uncertainties associated with entangled states, ultimately offering a significant advancement in the field.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Historical Development Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Chatbots in Household Budget Management: A Comparative Study in the Context of Economic Vulnerability
abstract: Household budget management is a central element of financial literacy, recognized by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development as a key determinant of financial inclusion, economic stability, and social participation. Despite efforts to promote financial education, significant weaknesses remain, reinforcing the need to resort to other accessible solutions in the current digital context, such as chatbots. Within this framework, this study analyses and compares the responses produced by different chatbots in solving a budget management task aimed at a family experiencing economic vulnerability. The results indicate that, overall, the models analysed demonstrated the ability to interpret the context and provide recommendations aligned with the principles of financial literacy, although differences were observed in the accuracy of calculations, clarity of responses, and suitability of the proposals to the family’s specific circumstances. Overall, the findings suggest that chatbots, when properly mediated by the user and used critically, can serve as complementary tools to support budget management and the development of financial literacy, particularly relevant for families in situations of greater economic vulnerability, although the information and recommendations generated should be verified in light of the limitations identified in the study.

title: Neurosymbolic AI: From Research to Industry
abstract: Neurosymbolic AI brings together the statistical nature of machine learning with the formal reasoning capabilities of symbolic AI. It seeks to offer a balanced approach to current AI technologies, by combining the ability to learn from data, with the capacity of reasoning upon knowledge acquired from the environment. The main criticism of neural machine learning is the lack of explainability and semantics, which are key requirements in safety-critical applications, but inherent strengths of logic-based methods. Recently, several corporations have publicly announced products and technologies grounded on neurosymbolic AI methodologies. This talk provided a concise review of the foundations, frameworks and tools underlying neurosymbolic AI, along with illustrative industrial applications. I conclude by presenting trends and current research directions of the field.

title: Bauxite Residues as a Source of Spectral Signatures for Fe and Al Exploration Using Machine Learning and Sentinel-2 Data
abstract: Abstract The Dom Bosco Syncline (DBS), located in the southern portion of the Quadrilátero Ferrífero, Brazil, contains significant Fe and Al deposits. However, dense vegetation cover and geological heterogeneity impose substantial limitations on mineral prospecting using orbital remote sensing. In this context, the machine learning model MinMap-S2 (Mineral Mapping via Sentinel-2) is proposed to support mineral exploration in the DBS. MinMap-S2 is a hybrid model based on spectral signatures derived from bauxite residues deposited in the Marzagão tailings dam (MTD), located within the DBS, for the detection of Fe- and Al-rich mineralization. The model was developed using Python, and its methodology integrates the algorithms Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to process Sentinel-2 multispectral data. SOM is employed to generate a spectral library from bauxite residues and surrounding surface materials, which is subsequently used by XGBoost for supervised classification and spatial prediction. The model was applied to a region located in the eastern portion of DBS, characterized by detrital-lateritic covers and metasedimentary rocks, including itabirites, phyllites, schists, quartzites, and sericitic metarenites. Validation of the results was conducted through geological mapping, field sampling, and petrographic analyses. The results demonstrate that MinMap-S2 effectively identifies areas with spectral responses associated with Fe- and Al-rich mineralization, supporting the discrimination of mineralized zones in heterogeneous terrains and under dense vegetation cover. Overall, the proposed methodology demonstrates potential as a supporting tool for mineral exploration using Sentinel-2 multispectral data.

title: Irredundant k-fold cross-validation for reliable, scalable, and energy-efficient model evaluation
abstract: Model evaluation remains one of the most computationally demanding phases of modern machine learning. As datasets and architectures scale, reliable evaluation increasingly strains computational and energy budgets. Standard k -fold cross-validation ( kF ) trains k times on heavily overlapping partitions. This redundancy both wastes compute and couples fold estimates: shared training data induces positive inter-fold covariance, so naive variance estimates are biased downward unless ad hoc inflations (e.g., Nadeau–Bengio) are applied. We introduce Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation ( IkF ), a novel restructuring of cross-validation that eliminates training-set overlap entirely. Each outer fold is split into k − 1 subfolds and the training set for test fold i is formed by one unique subfold from every other fold; thus every instance is used exactly once for training and once for testing across the k iterations. Theoretically, we (i) develop a bias model based on learning-curve and stability arguments, (ii) derive the variance of IkF and a closed-form expression for its mean-squared error, and (iii) show that disjoint training sets suppress overlap-induced dependence so that, under i.i.d. sampling and fixed k , inter-fold covariance vanishes as n → ∞ , thereby preventing overconfident uncertainty estimates and rendering the naive variance estimator asymptotically valid. Computationally, if training scales as C ( n ) = Θ ( n α ) , IkF lowers validation cost by approximately ( k − 1 ) α . On synthetic datasets ranging from 1 0 4 to 1 0 7 samples and two representative learners (Random Forests and Neural Networks), IkF matches kF on Accuracy, MCC, AUC(MCP), and AUC(ROC), while reducing validation time by ∼ 9 − 11 × and achieving comparable estimator variance. On a high-dimensional real-world dataset, IkF exhibits the same qualitative behaviour, achieving substantial speed-ups and associated reductions in CO 2 e emissions. Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation requires no correction factors and avoids repeated exposure of data, preserving statistical rigour while substantially lowering computational cost. It thus offers an immediately adoptable, reliability- and sustainability-aligned protocol for validating complex models and large-scale datasets, and is particularly well suited to settings with stringent time, energy, or environmental constraints.

Standard k -fold cross-validation ( kF ) trains k times on heavily overlapping partitions. This redundancy both wastes compute and couples fold estimates: shared training data induces positive inter-fold covariance, so naive variance estimates are biased downward unless ad hoc inflations (e.g., Nadeau–Bengio) are applied. We introduce Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation ( IkF ), a novel restructuring of cross-validation that eliminates training-set overlap entirely. Each outer fold is split into k − 1 subfolds and the training set for test fold i is formed by one unique subfold from every other fold; thus every instance is used exactly once for training and once for testing across the k iterations. Theoretically, we (i) develop a bias model based on learning-curve and stability arguments, (ii) derive the variance of IkF and a closed-form expression for its mean-squared error, and (iii) show that disjoint training sets suppress overlap-induced dependence so that, under i.i.d. sampling and fixed k , inter-fold covariance vanishes as n → ∞ , thereby preventing overconfident uncertainty estimates and rendering the naive variance estimator asymptotically valid. Computationally, if training scales as C ( n ) = Θ ( n α ) , IkF lowers validation cost by approximately ( k − 1 ) α . On synthetic datasets ranging from 1 0 4 to 1 0 7 samples and two representative learners (Random Forests and Neural Networks), IkF matches kF on Accuracy, MCC, AUC(MCP), and AUC(ROC), while reducing validation time by ∼ 9 − 11 × and achieving comparable estimator variance. On a high-dimensional real-world dataset, IkF exhibits the same qualitative behaviour, achieving substantial speed-ups and associated reductions in CO 2 e emissions. Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation requires no correction factors and avoids repeated exposure of data, preserving statistical rigour while substantially lowering computational cost. It thus offers an immediately adoptable, reliability- and sustainability-aligned protocol for validating complex models and large-scale datasets, and is particularly well suited to settings with stringent time, energy, or environmental constraints.

title: Purification of photonic graph states
abstract: Graph states constitute the main building block for quantum computing with photons. Quantum emitters with a hosted spin can deterministically generate photonic graph states, strongly lowering the overhead of multiplexing highly probabilistic linear-optics graph state generation. However, they generally suffer from various noise sources, resulting in reduced fidelities of the produced states. To mitigate this issue, we develop purification schemes for entangled photonic states. We first develop purification schemes to purify arbitrary photonic GHZ and other CSS states, which we generalize to all photonic graph states and stabilizer states. The proposed purification schemes have a high success probability of up to $1/2$ and require only linear optics and photon detectors. We optimize cascaded purification schemes for various graph states, taking into account phenomenological Pauli errors or physical noise in time-bin-encoded graph state generation with quantum emitters.

title: An efficient EM algorithm for both element-wise and structural missingness in matrix-variate normal mixture models
abstract: Matrix-variate data with missing entries arise frequently in applications where observations are naturally organized as two-dimensional arrays. Although the matrix normal distribution provides a parsimonious model through its Kronecker covariance structure, standard EM estimation can be computationally expensive because arbitrary missingness patterns typically destroy this separability in the E-step. In this paper, we propose an efficient partial EM algorithm for matrix-variate normal data with missing entries. The proposed method updates the conditional mean and covariance of the missing component through coordinate-wise approximations, avoiding repeated inversion of pattern-specific covariance matrices and avoiding construction of the full vectorized covariance matrix. We further develop a specialized update for submatrix missingness, where the missing-block precision retains a Kronecker product structure, and the covariance update can be carried out independently in the row and column directions. Simulation studies show that the proposed methods substantially reduce computation time compared with exact EM while preserving nearly identical observed-data likelihood across a range of dimensions and missing proportions. A real-data application to hyperspectral image patches demonstrates that the proposed imputation strategy can be embedded within a matrix-variate mixture model for simultaneous imputation and clustering.

title: DReSG: Diffusion Residuals for Stylized Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Reference-guided stylization of scenes represented by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is important for efficient and controllable 3D content creation. Existing VGG-feature-based 3D stylization methods provide stable rendered-view optimization, but often under-represent expressive reference style cues; diffusion models offer stronger image priors, yet direct per-view or score-based diffusion guidance can lead to view drift, local artifacts, and hard-to-control appearance updates. We present DReSG, a 3D-grounded residual-feedback framework for stylized Gaussian splatting. DReSG represents attention-guided diffusion proposals as residual targets relative to the current render, and progressively absorbs these residuals into a shared Gaussian scene through multi-view Gaussian feedback. To make this feedback stable and controllable, DReSG modulates residual strength during target construction and combines coverage-aware view selection with conflict-filtered color updates during multi-view fitting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DReSG achieves competitive reference-guided stylization while better preserving scene structure and cross-view stability. Our project page is available at https://vpx-ecnu.github.io/DReSG-website/.

title: Seq2Seq2Seq: lossless data compression via discrete latent transformers and reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract Efficient lossless compression is essential for reducing storage and transmission requirements while preserving data exactly. Traditional dictionary-based and statistical compressors can be limited in their ability to exploit complex, long-range dependencies. In this paper, we propose a lossless compression framework that combines a T5-small architecture with Advantage Actor-Critic reinforcement learning (RL) to generate a variable-length sequence of discrete compressed tokens. Rather than relying on a continuous autoencoder bottleneck, the proposed framework directly optimizes the length of this discrete representation while preserving the information required for exact reconstruction. The method operates without external grammatical rules or world knowledge. On the enwik8 benchmark, it achieves a compression ratio of 4.14, improving upon XZ (4.05) by approximately 2.3% and GZIP (2.74) by 51.0%. Although this result remains below neural network compression v3.2 (6.70), it demonstrates that RL can learn a compact, lossless discrete representation using two T5-small networks evaluated on a single 12 GB GPU device.

title: A brief history of quantum vs classical computational advantage
abstract: In this review article we summarize all experiments claiming quantum computational advantage to date. Our review highlights challenges, loopholes, and refutations appearing in subsequent work to provide a complete picture of the current statuses of these experiments. In addition, we also discuss theoretical computational advantage in example problems such as approximate optimization and recommendation systems. Finally, we review recent experiments in quantum error correction --- the biggest frontier to reach experimental quantum advantage in Shor's algorithm.

title: Sequence labelling for code-mixed text by an averaged perceptron approach
abstract: In mixed-language settings, NLP models face challenges because of intertwined grammatical structures and language discrepancies.This paper analyses a Part-of-Speech tagger used on Hindi-English code-mixed (Hinglish) data and compares it with monolingual English and Hindi data.The model achieved an accuracy of 93.60% on the English dataset, accuracy of 95.95% on the Hindi dataset, and 94.89% on the Hinglish dataset, respectively.This showed strong model performance in both monolingual and code-mixed settings.The study also tried to understand the patterns in sentence structure that led to tagging errors.It was found that the most misclassifications occurred between nouns, verbs, proper nouns, and adjectives because of their overlapping lexical forms.The analysis of sentence length indicated that medium-length sentences yielded marginally higher accuracy than long sentences.In contrast, the error distribution per sentence showed that most sentences contain zero or one tagging error, with a cascading effect observed in a minority of cases where a single error in a sentence led to more errors and isolated errors.In the future, researchers can focus on understanding the reason for dual language error patterns, such as common misclassifications in a complex sentence.
