title: Legal Liability for Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content from an Intellectual Property Perspective in Indonesia
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence now produces economically valuable works on a massive scale, while Indonesian copyright law still recognises human beings as the only possible authors. This study analyses the legal status of artificial intelligence-generated content from an intellectual property perspective and formulates a liability model suited to the Indonesian legal system. This normative legal research applies statutory, conceptual, case, and comparative approaches. Primary legal materials comprise Law Number 28 of 2014 on Copyright, the Indonesian Civil Code, and the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, while secondary materials consist of reputable literature published within the last five years, analysed through content analysis, legal interpretation, and deductive syllogism. The findings show that artificial intelligence can be neither a legal subject nor an author. Copyright protection attaches only insofar as a human creative contribution determines the final form of the work, consistent with the direction and supervision logic of Article 34. Liability for infringement must therefore be transferred to the human or legal entity connected to the system. This study formulates a tiered liability model distributing the burden among model developers, platform providers, and users according to degree of control, creative contribution, knowledge of risk, and discharge of the duty of care.

title: Reproducibility Package for "Schema-Valid JSON Is Not Sufficient for a Safe Cyber-Risk Record: Evidence-Anchored Semantic Validation and Fail-Closed Repair for Schema-Constrained LLM Pipelines"
abstract: This package contains the complete reproducibility materials for a model-independent mutation benchmark of a semantic guardrail for schema-constrained LLM cyber-risk records. It includes the CRSC JSON Schema, deterministic semantic validator, 15 error-code definitions, 144 synthetic core records, 24 adversarial prompt-injection controls, 996 schema-valid semantic fault injections across 14 mutation families, bounded evidence-preserving repair/fail-closed logic, raw and aggregate results, figures, and locked prompts for an optional provider-specific LLM extension. The reported results are mutation-adequacy results for the locked fault taxonomy and are not estimates of arbitrary LLM error rates.

title: Cayman Nesophontes: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Cayman Nesophontes
abstract: This paper introduces Cayman Nesophontes, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to improve the performance of existing optimization techniques. The algorithm draws inspiration from the Cayman Nesophontes, a fascinating reptile known for its unique hunting strategy. Cayman Nesophontes employs a combination of characteristics observed in the animal's behavior, including its opportunistic foraging, strategic positioning, and adaptive response to environmental changes, to create a robust and efficient optimization process. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a new adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a novel "nesting" strategy that simulates the Nesophontes' territorial behavior. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's components, including the initialization phase, velocity update, position update, and convergence criteria. The performance of Cayman Nesophontes is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its ability to achieve superior solutions compared to traditional PSO and other established metaheuristics. The results highlight the potential of biomimicry in the development of effective and adaptable optimization algorithms. The primary objective is to enhance the exploration and exploitation balance within the search process, leading to faster convergence and improved solution quality.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的节点分类
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to node classification utilizing a self-adaptive graph neural network (sGAN). Traditional graph neural networks often require manual design of connection weights, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering performance. We introduce a sGAN that dynamically adjusts connection strengths during training, allowing the network to learn optimal node representations and improve classification accuracy. The core mechanism involves an adaptive training process that iteratively adjusts node weights based on the network's error. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques, offering a robust and automated solution for node classification.

title: Cameroon Horseshoe Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Cameroon Horseshoe Bat Algorithm" (CHBA), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Cameroon horseshoe bat ( *Rhinolophus clivosus*). These bats exhibit remarkable aerial maneuvering and efficient navigation skills, particularly during nocturnal foraging. The CHBA algorithm leverages these observed characteristics to develop a robust optimization strategy. The core of the algorithm incorporates a dynamic movement system mimicking the bat's flight patterns, a memory component representing the bat's learned foraging routes, and a novel convergence mechanism based on the bat's response to environmental cues. The algorithm utilizes a stochastic search process with parameter adaptation, aiming to minimize a given objective function. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform existing metaheuristic techniques in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's design focuses on adaptability, exploration, and exploitation, mirroring the bat's survival strategies. The key mathematical formulation of the CHBA algorithm is presented, including the position update equation, the memory update equation, and the parameter adaptation formula. The simulation results are presented with quantitative analysis to validate the algorithm's performance. The final section discusses the limitations of the current algorithm and suggests potential future research directions.

title: Quantum State Superposition for Parallel Data Processing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum state superposition for parallel data processing, aiming to enhance data processing speeds. The core claim rests on leveraging the inherent parallelism offered by superposition, where data is encoded into a quantum state. This encoded state then undergoes processing by a quantum computer, exploiting its parallel computational capabilities. The proposed mechanism represents a novel approach to data handling, specifically targeting applications demanding high computational throughput. The research investigates the theoretical framework and potential benefits of this paradigm, laying a foundation for future explorations in quantum-enhanced data processing. The primary focus is on conceptualization and outlining the possibilities rather than practical implementation due to the current limitations of quantum computing hardware. ---

title: Cactus Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cactus Mouse Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cactus Mouse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Perognathus longipes*, the cactus mouse. The algorithm leverages the cactus mouse's unique ability to exploit sparse resources and adaptively adjust its search strategy based on environmental feedback. Cactus Mouse combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel "resource awareness" mechanism. Specifically, the algorithm employs a dynamic weight adjustment strategy based on the perceived density of promising solutions, mimicking the cactus mouse's decision to move towards areas with higher resource availability. The performance of Cactus Mouse is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for various complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm revolves around the following key elements: population initialization (s_1, s_2, ..., s_N), position update (s_i = s_i + ω * rand() * (p_best - s_i) + β * (l_best - s_i)), velocity update (v_i = v_i + ω * rand() * (p_best - s_i) + β * (l_best - s_i)), resource density evaluation (r_i = f(s_i)), weight adjustment (α = r_i / Σr_j), and termination criteria (ε).

title: Causal Discovery of Time Series Data using Granger Causality and Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional Granger causality tests when applied to complex time series data. We propose a novel approach combining Granger causality with Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) to enhance causal inference. The core idea is to represent time series dependencies within a DBN, allowing for a more nuanced assessment of causal relationships. The methodology involves constructing a DBN that captures the temporal dynamics between the considered time series. Subsequently, the Granger causality test is performed within this network framework, leveraging the network structure to mitigate potential biases and confounding factors. The resulting model provides a richer understanding of the relationships between time series, offering improved accuracy and robustness compared to standard Granger causality analysis. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline its potential applications in various domains where time series data is prevalent.

title: 基于量子自旋的拓扑信息分析
abstract: Quantum spin provides a unique platform for exploring topological data analysis, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to classical methods. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum spin's inherent properties, specifically its quantum entanglement and superposition, to develop a novel algorithm for uncovering hidden topological structures within data. We propose a quantum-enhanced algorithm that utilizes the principles of quantum mechanics to identify and characterize topological features without the limitations of traditional computational approaches. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of quantum spin states to reveal patterns and relationships within complex datasets, promising a significant advancement in topological data analysis. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential practical applications of this approach, highlighting its distinct advantages and limitations.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for classical computation. Traditional optimization methods often rely on meticulously adjusted parameters, failing to fully leverage the inherent probabilistic nature of entangled states. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Quantum Entanglement Probability Adaptive Algorithm (QEPAA), designed to dynamically adjust quantum parameters based on the probabilistic fluctuations of entangled states. This approach leverages the concept of "纠缠波动" – a probabilistic variable that governs the evolution of entangled states – to achieve significantly improved computational efficiency, particularly in quantum computing and quantum cryptography. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QEPAA through detailed numerical simulations and analyze its impact on key quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around introducing a dynamic weighting system that adapts to the entanglement distribution, leading to optimized results. evidence.abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for classical computation. Traditional optimization methods often rely on meticulously adjusted parameters, failing to fully leverage the inherent probabilistic nature of entangled states. title: Bristle-Spined Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Unique Locomotion of *Tricomys Lawsoni*
abstract: This paper presents Bristle-Spined Rat (BSR), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the distinctive locomotion strategy of *Tricomys Lawsoni*, commonly known as the bristle-spined rat. *Tricomys Lawsoni* exhibits a unique gait characterized by alternating, short steps with periods of stillness, a pattern we term "pulse-step." BSR leverages this pulsing behavior to enhance exploration and exploitation in optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a Pulse Generation Mechanism (PGM), a Step Adjustment Mechanism (SAM), and a Local Search Operator (LSO). The PGM simulates the rat's pulsed movement, introducing randomness while maintaining a degree of stability. SAM dynamically adjusts step lengths based on the objective function value and the gradient information. LSO employs a modified differential evolution strategy to refine solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BSR on a range of benchmark problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and the Powell's Boomeranging function. Results indicate that BSR consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA), showcasing its potential as a robust and efficient optimization tool. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational cost. Future research will explore the algorithm's adaptability to different problem types and its potential integration with machine learning techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Coding Protocol
abstract: Quantum entanglement information encoding protocol presents a novel approach to secure communication utilizing the instantaneous correlations between entangled particles. This paper details the design and implementation of a QKD protocol predicated on this entanglement, emphasizing enhanced security and extended key length compared to existing methods. We introduce a novel key generation algorithm that leverages the instantaneous mutual influence characteristic of entangled states, coupled with a quantum state storage mechanism for improved key retention. The protocol's advantages include reduced operational costs and enhanced security through direct entanglement transfer, offering a significant advancement in secure communication paradigms.

title: 自适应量子纠错协议的概率理论研究
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum information. However, QEC is inherently probabilistic, demanding precise calibration and potentially vulnerable to decoherence. This paper investigates the use of probability theory to analyze and improve the robustness of QEC protocols. We propose a novel "self-adaptive correction" algorithm based on quantum state dynamics, dynamically adjusting error correction strategies based on environmental fluctuations. Our core claim is that by applying probabilistic methods to the QEC process, we can achieve improved reliability and efficiency compared to static QEC approaches. This research explores the fundamental concepts of probability, statistical analysis, and dynamic adaptation within the context of quantum information processing. The core mechanism focuses on developing a quantum state-based feedback loop that optimizes error correction based on environmental changes, offering a more flexible and resilient approach. The study highlights the potential of probability theory to enhance the design and implementation of robust QEC protocols.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Gradient Descent
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Optimization (QIO) aims to accelerate optimization algorithms by mimicking the behavior of quantum systems. This paper explores the application of gradient descent, a fundamental optimization technique, to this framework. We propose a novel gradient update rule inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically focusing on probabilistic updates that mimic the superposition and interference effects observed in quantum systems. The core mechanism involves adapting the standard gradient descent formula to incorporate these probabilistic elements, significantly enhancing convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional gradient descent. This work introduces a new algorithm that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance optimization performance, potentially leading to faster and more reliable solutions for complex problems.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN AUTOMATIC EVALUATION MODEL FOR ASSESSING THE QUALITY OF INDONESIAN DIGITAL TRANSLATION
abstract: This study aims to develop an automatic evaluation model for assessing the quality of Indonesian digital translations and to produce a simple bilingual translation application called Translate You. The research addresses the limitations of existing evaluation metrics, such as BLEU, METEOR, BERTScore, and COMET, which are not fully suitable for Indonesian linguistic characteristics. This study uses a Research and Development (R&D) method combined with a quantitative approach. The data consist of bilingual sentences collected from online articles. Translation outputs are evaluated using an automatic model and a professional translator as the expert validator. The model integrates semantic similarity, fluency, and Indonesian linguistic features. The results show that the developed model produces evaluation scores that are more aligned with expert judgment compared to traditional metrics. The Translate You application also successfully integrates text translation, voice input, and automatic evaluation in a simple system. This research contributes to Translation Quality Assessment (TQA) by providing an Indonesian-specific evaluation model and a practical prototype for translation assessment.

title: A quantum eigensolver framework for assessing solvent effects of an SN2 reaction
abstract: We present a hybrid quantum-classical framework for molecular simulations that combines the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) with projection-based embedding (PBE) and an implicit solvation treatment. Solvent effects are incorporated through the solvation model based on density (SMD), enabling the investigation of chemically relevant processes in condensed phase environments within a quantum computing workflow. The embedding strategy partitions the molecular system into active and environment subsystems, allowing correlated quantum simulations of the chemically important subsystem while retaining an efficient classical description of the surroundings. As a representative application, we compute the potential energy surface of a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction between the chloride ion and chloromethane in multiple solvents, demonstrating that quantum eigensolver methods can be extended beyond gas-phase models to include solvent effects relevant for reaction energetics.

title: Controlador borroso para regulación de temperatura: integración HOME I/O, EcoStruxure y MATLAB
abstract: This paper addresses temperature regulation in buildings through the design and implementation of a Mamdani-type fuzzy controller, aimed at improving energy efficiency and control action smoothness. The novelty of the proposal lies in a co-simulation architecture that integrates three levels: the HOME I/O 3D virtual environment, the MATLAB/Simulink computing engine, and Schneider Electric's EcoStruxure Automation Expert industrial platform. This integration enables closing the control loop using the IEC 61499 standard and the OPC-UA communication protocol. The results demonstrate that, compared to a traditional PI control, the fuzzy solution provides a more resilient dynamic response and a control signal without aggressive peaks, facilitating technology transfer from simulation environments to real industrial controllers.

title: An anomaly identification method for time-series data of fiber-reinforced composite durability testing based on SVM
abstract: Abstract Single-threshold discrimination can only provide rough screening, resulting in low accuracy in anomaly identification for time-series data in fiber-reinforced composite durability testing. Therefore, an anomaly identification method for time-series data of fiber-reinforced composite durability testing based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) is proposed. The study employs wavelet transform denoising, linear interpolation for missing value filling, and time alignment with asynchronous interpolation processing to analyze time-series data from fiber-reinforced composite durability testing. Features are extracted from the time domain, the frequency domain, and the joint time-frequency domain to construct an SVM classifier based on radial basis functions. Optimal parameters are determined through grid search and cross-validation. After training, the classifier classifies samples using decision functions to detect anomalies in fiber-reinforced composite durability test data. Experiments show that the research method maintains high, stable accuracy and recall at different sampling frequencies. Compared with the comparison method, it can more effectively distinguish between normal and abnormal data in the durability test sequence of fiber-reinforced composite materials, and the ROC curve position is better, improving the accuracy of anomaly identification.

title: Mining of risk evolution mechanism and construction of knowledge graph for surface facilities of salt cavern compressed air energy storage
abstract: Driven by global carbon neutrality targets, salt cavern compressed air energy storage (CAES) has emerged as a key technology for low-carbon energy transition. However, the surface facilities of salt cavern CAES systems include compressors, heat exchangers, and other critical components, with multi-dimensional risk coupling among human, equipment, environment, and management factors. Traditional risk analysis methods rely heavily on expert experience, have difficulty in processing massive unstructured operation and maintenance data, and face challenges such as knowledge fragmentation and difficulty in identifying implicit causal chains. To achieve efficient extraction and structured representation of risk evolution knowledge for CAES surface facilities, a CAES-oriented risk evolution graph framework was developed by integrating ontology-guided knowledge extraction with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. First, a risk evolution ontology model comprising seven categories of core entities was built using the METHONTOLOGY approach. Second, the Qwen-8B model was fine-tuned via LoRA, and a multi-stage prompting strategy integrating few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought prompting, and constraint-based prompting was adopted to improve domain-specific entity extraction and causal relationship identification. Finally, entity alignment and deduplication were realized through character-semantic hybrid similarity calculation, and knowledge storage and visualization were implemented in Neo4j. Experimental results show that the proposed CAES-LLM framework demonstrates strong extraction performance, with precision, recall, and F1-score reaching 86.32%, 82.10%, and 84.16%, respectively, significantly outperforming traditional models and vanilla large language models. Case studies further demonstrate that the proposed method identifies 70% more implicit risk nodes than fault tree analysis (FTA), enables the shift from passive repair to active prevention, and supports accurate risk path location and emergency plan matching. The proposed framework provides an effective decision-support tool for safe operation and risk control of salt cavern CAES surface facilities.

title: Deep Learning Models for Mapping Surficial Geology in Selected Physiographic Regions of New York
abstract: ABSTRACT Surficial geologic mapping is required for decisions including infrastructure and water‐resource development and management. Deep learning, a type of machine learning that uses training data to self‐learn and perform tasks, is explored as a tool to help increase efficiency of the labour‐ and time‐intensive mapping process. Deep learning models were trained, and their potential to aid in mapping surficial geology was explored for two physiographic regions in New York: the high‐relief Allegheny Plateau and the low‐relief Erie‐Ontario Lowlands. Key to the development of deep learning models is the availability of highly detailed surficial geologic maps in each of these regions from which the models can learn. Through exploring different groupings of surficial deposits and their corresponding spatial data, deep learning models were iteratively developed to reproduce published mapping for greater than 79% of the training areas, and with similar accuracy in test areas within the same physiographic region. These models were trained using only two inputs: high‐resolution lidar data and previously published surficial geologic maps. This straightforward approach is intended to make the methods and models created easily reproducible using widely accessible datasets. This research describes the strengths and limitations of lidar‐derived surficial geologic models and how broadly grouping surficial types, characteristics of different physiographic regions, and testing models in physiographic regions outside of their training areas affect model creation and performance. In addition, the models created could be used as a tool for mapping surficial geology in similar physiographic regions, in addition to establishing a framework for creating similar models elsewhere.

title: VerTox: Verifiable Reward-Guided Corpus Poisoning Against Neural Ranking Models
abstract: Neural ranking models have become core components of modern information retrieval systems and important building blocks of AI systems such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines. However, their robustness remains insufficiently understood in the presence of large language models (LLMs), which can generate fluent and deceptive content at scale. This work investigates the vulnerability of neural ranking models to corpus poisoning attacks, in which an adversary injects a small number of maliciously crafted documents into the corpus to distort ranking behavior. We propose VerTox, the first framework to formulate corpus poisoning as a verifiable reward-guided reinforcement learning (RLVR) problem. By explicitly coupling ranking distortion with factual corruption through specialized reward shaping, we fine-tune compact LLMs into adversarial generators. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves near-perfect attack success rates, producing adversarial documents that frequently rank higher than target documents across major neural ranking architectures, as well as a proprietary commercial embedding model. The generated adversarial documents are fluent and exhibit low perplexity, making them difficult to detect. Furthermore, by explicitly encouraging factual corruption, our adversarial documents significantly degrade the performance of a downstream RAG application.

title: RATIO: A Benchmark for Retrieval Across Typed Ideation Operations in Scientific Literature
abstract: Retrieved scientific literature can serve as inspiration for both human and AI scientists. Inspiration can take different forms: prior work may directly suggest how to address a problem, or surface directions at different levels of abstraction - zooming out to a more general view or zooming in to a concrete realization. We introduce RATIO (Retrieval Across Typed Ideation Operations), a large-scale benchmark in which relevance is defined by three operations which we name ideation moves: Address retrieves potential approaches for stated problems, Broaden retrieves more general formulations, and Specify retrieves concrete instantiations. RATIO is constructed from millions of full-text scientific papers across CS literature via a general recipe that extends discourse-marker distant supervision - previously used only for classification - to corpus-scale retrieval, combined with extensive LLM and human vetting. Experiments show that operation-specific fine-tuning substantially boosts retrievers but leaves much room for further improvements. RATIO provides a scalable training and evaluation framework for retrieval components that support literature-grounded ideation, opening up new research avenues on scientific inspiration retrieval.

title: P$$^{2}$$CE: Model-Agnostic Plausible Pareto-Optimal Counterfactual Explanations
abstract: Abstract The increasing use of machine learning algorithms in social applications has raised concerns about fairness and transparency, leading to the development of counterfactual explanations. These explanations support individuals to understand and potentially alter unfavorable decisions in areas such as loan applications, job selections, and more, by providing actionable changes to input features that would lead to a desired outcome. Existing methods often struggle to balance feasibility, plausibility, and computational efficiency. To address this, we introduce P $$^{2}$$ CE, an algorithm for generating plausible Pareto-optimal counterfactual explanations, offering users a diverse set of optimal trade-offs between different notions of feasibility. P $$^{2}$$ CE employs an auxiliary isolation forest outlier detector to ensure that explanations are in accordance with the data distribution and leverages SHAP values to obtain optimal results with short computing times, regardless of the underlying model. Our algorithm was empirically evaluated on three datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency compared to related techniques.

title: Summary based retrieval augmented generation(RAG) System with web scraping
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing the factual accuracy andcontextual relevance of large language models by integrating external knowledge sources. This paper proposes aSummary-Based RAG system that incorporates automated web scraping to dynamically collect, process, and utilize upto-date information from online sources[1]. The system first employs web scraping techniques to extract raw textual datafrom relevant web pages in real time. This data is then preprocessed and condensed using advanced summarizationalgorithms to generate concise, information-rich representations.These summaries are stored in a structured retrievalindex, enabling efficient semantic search based on user queries[2]. Upon receiving a query, the system retrieves the mostrelevant summaries and augments the input prompt provided to the generative model. evidence.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing the factual accuracy andcontextual relevance of large language models by integrating external knowledge sources. This paper proposes aSummary-Based RAG system that incorporates automated web scraping to dynamically collect, process, and utilize upto-date information from online sources[1]. The system first employs web scraping techniques to extract raw textual datafrom relevant web pages in real time. This data is then preprocessed and condensed using advanced summarizationalgorithms to generate concise, information-rich representations.These summaries are stored in a structured retrievalindex, enabling efficient semantic search based on user queries[2]. Upon receiving a query, the system retrieves the mostrelevant summaries and augments the input prompt provided to the generative model. By leveraging summarized contentinstead of raw documents, the approach reduces noise, improves retrieval precision, and minimizes token usage, leadingto faster and more cost-effective responses.

title: Supporting Data and Reproducibility Artifacts for "SAIL-LLM"
abstract: This repository contains supporting materials for the study entitled “SAIL-LLM: A Risk-Aware Architecture for Preventing Employee-Driven Data Leakage in Enterprise LLM Deployments.” The study addresses a growing enterprise security risk in which authenticated employees may unintentionally expose confidential or regulated information when submitting prompts, documents, spreadsheets, database fragments, or retrieved enterprise context to Large Language Models. The proposed SAIL-LLM architecture introduces a pre-inference governance layer between the enterprise user interface and the target LLM environment. The architecture combines content classification, role-based authorization, execution-context assessment, explicit risk scoring, policy routing, RAG sanitization, and audit logging. Requests are routed to one of four governance actions: Allow, Restrict, Redirect, or Block, depending on the sensitivity of submitted content, user authorization, execution environment, and detected policy violations. A Streamlit-based proof-of-concept prototype was implemented using a local LLM environment. Before any model call, deterministic detectors inspect enterprise content for personal identifiers, payroll terms, financial indicators, credential-like strings, database-related content, and internal document markers. Restricted content can be sanitized through masking or removal, while confidential authorized requests may be redirected to a secure internal LLM/RAG environment. High-risk or unauthorized content is blocked before inference. The repository is intended to support transparency and reproducibility of the proof-of-concept evaluation. The evaluation uses 24 labeled enterprise scenarios covering finance, human resources, operations, and strategic or technical knowledge-management cases. The benchmark evaluates policy-routing accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro F1-score, false positives, false negatives, sanitization coverage, and pre-inference latency overhead. The prototype achieved 91.7% routing accuracy, 0.93 macro precision, 0.92 macro recall, 0.92 macro F1-score, one false positive, one false negative, 97.1% sanitization coverage for restricted cases, and a median governance-layer overhead of 96 ms, excluding LLM generation. These results indicate that SAIL-LLM can provide measurable pre-inference governance while preserving interactive enterprise use, although the evaluation remains a proof of concept rather than a production-scale validation. Supporting artifacts may include: labeled enterprise governance scenarios; expected and predicted policy actions; risk-scoring rules and thresholds; sanitization examples; evaluation metrics; benchmark outputs; architecture and workflow diagrams; prototype screenshots; and supporting scripts or configuration files used for the proof-of-concept evaluation. The study focuses specifically on unintentional employee-driven leakage by authenticated users performing legitimate work. Deliberate malicious exfiltration, external cyberattacks, and model-training attacks are outside the primary threat model.

title: Superconducting Quantum Computing: Adaptive Quantum State Design
abstract: Superconducting quantum computing offers the potential for unprecedented computational power by leveraging the quantum mechanical properties of superconducting circuits. However, achieving high precision and broad applicability requires sophisticated control over the quantum state. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum state design utilizing adaptive algorithms, aiming to dynamically adjust quantum states to optimize computations and enhance the capabilities of superconducting quantum computers. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in enhancing quantum state fidelity and enabling the implementation of complex quantum algorithms. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent dynamics of the quantum state to guide the optimization process, providing a pathway towards more precise and versatile computations. This work addresses the limitations of traditional quantum computing methods by introducing a dynamic state adjustment mechanism, paving the way for significant advancements in the field.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum topology learning algorithm designed to dynamically adjust topology structures based on input data. Traditional topology learning algorithms often rely on static models, aiming to improve model adaptability. Our approach leverages quantum circuit simulation to dynamically modify the underlying topology, establishing a strong connection between the model and the resulting structure. The algorithm's core mechanism involves iterative quantum circuit simulations, allowing for a continuous refinement of the topology, ultimately leading to more effective system modeling and prediction. We present a rigorous analysis of the algorithm's performance and demonstrate its potential to address challenges in complex system analysis.

title: Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph Reasoning Engine designed to facilitate complex reasoning and knowledge discovery through the interactive integration of diverse knowledge graph modalities. The core claim is that leveraging the interplay between multi-modal knowledge graphs significantly enhances the ability to perform sophisticated reasoning tasks compared to traditional, single-modality approaches. The proposed mechanism centers around constructing a fused knowledge graph encompassing textual, visual, and auditory data, coupled with a graph neural network (GNN)-based reasoning engine. This architecture overcomes the limitations inherent in single-modality knowledge graphs, offering a more comprehensive and nuanced understanding of interconnected information. The engine is designed to dynamically adapt to the relationships between different modalities, improving the accuracy and efficiency of reasoning processes. The paper outlines the architecture, the GNN implementation, and potential applications, illustrating a pathway toward intelligent systems capable of sophisticated knowledge extraction and inference.

title: Bayesian Optimization of Neural Architecture Search with Adaptive Search Space
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a powerful technique for automating the design of neural networks. However, conventional NAS methods frequently face challenges in efficiently exploring the immense architectural search space, leading to substantial computational costs. This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Optimization framework for NAS that incorporates an adaptive search space mechanism. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the search space based on the observed performance of candidate architectures, concentrating computational resources on the most promising regions. We utilize a Gaussian Process (GP) to model the relationship between architectural parameters and the corresponding performance metrics. This GP provides a probabilistic assessment of different architectural choices, guiding the Bayesian Optimization process towards regions with high potential. The adaptive search space management strategy further enhances the efficiency of the search by focusing on relevant architectural variations, ultimately reducing the overall search time and improving the quality of the discovered architectures. This approach demonstrates significant improvements in terms of both exploration efficiency and architectural quality compared to traditional NAS methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement Revisited: A Topological Field Theory Perspective
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, remains a significant challenge in harnessing its potential for computation and communication. Traditional models often rely on classical correlations, limiting their scalability and efficiency. This paper proposes a novel quantum entanglement framework based on topological field theory, aiming to overcome these limitations by leveraging the inherent properties of entanglement itself. We explore the core mechanism of constructing a quantum state through a dynamically evolving topological structure, representing entanglement as a fundamental aspect of spacetime. The proposed model offers a path toward enhanced quantum coherence, robustness, and the ability to explore complex entanglement patterns with improved computational capabilities.

title: ## Budin's Grass Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Budin's Grass Mouse (BGM), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of *Mus budinus*, commonly known as Budin's grass mouse, a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. BGM leverages a combination of adaptive memory, probabilistic search, and a novel "patch" concept to mimic the mouse's exploration and exploitation of resources. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The core mechanism revolves around maintaining a memory of previously visited "patches" (regions of the search space) and dynamically adjusting the probability of visiting these patches based on their historical success. A key innovation is the "patch selection" process, which incorporates a probabilistic component influenced by the patch's recent performance and a global exploration factor. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark test functions, demonstrating its competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic methods. The results indicate that BGM offers a promising approach to optimization, particularly in scenarios where adaptive exploration and memory play a crucial role.

title: ## Black-tailed Tree Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Black-tailed Tree Rat (BTR) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-tailed tree rat (Nesoryzomys rufodorsalis). The algorithm leverages the rat's ability to efficiently explore and exploit a complex environment for food sources, mirroring the exploration-exploitation trade-off crucial for effective optimization. The BTR algorithm incorporates a novel movement strategy based on a weighted random walk, incorporating a 'memory' component derived from past successful foraging locations. This memory component is designed to bias the search towards promising areas, accelerating convergence while maintaining exploration capabilities. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristics such as Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the weight between exploration and exploitation, influenced by the accumulated 'memory' of successful foraging locations. The algorithm's design aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for complex optimization landscapes. The core mathematical components and algorithm description are detailed within this paper.

title: When to Escalate: A Cost-Aware Belief Policy for Conversational Agents Under Hidden Intent
abstract: A conversational agent replying to inbound sales leads must choose an action before it knows the lead’s intent. It can answer, ask a qualifying question, hold, or escalate to a human, but the true buying-readiness and whether a human is actually needed are hidden. The two ways of being wrong are not equally costly. A missed escalation, where a lead who needed a person did not get one, is far more expensive than a needless one, and some wrong answers are not a cost to trade off at all but a line the agent must not cross. We build a small agent that makes this trade-off explicit. It holds a belief over the hidden state, split into readiness (hot, warm, cold) and a separate probability that the case needs a human, and at each message it picks the action with the lowest expected cost under a cost matrix that encodes the asymmetry. Escalation is split into notify, where a human is told while the conversation continues, and pause, where the agent stops, because the two carry different costs. The hardest wrong answers, such as false legal or land claims, are enforced as a hard constraint rather than a priced term. We test on 100 synthetic cases with cached language-model beliefs, comparing the cost-aware policy against the same policy with a uniform cost matrix and against three fixed-action baselines. Two of those baselines give opposite answers, so both are named wherever the cost result appears. Against the uniform-cost version of the same rule — same belief, same feasible set, only the asymmetry removed — the cost-aware policy reaches 1.72 against 2.58 over all 100 cases, a reduction of a third; that gap is what cost-awareness buys, and it is against that baseline and no other. Against always-notify, which escalates every message, there is no cost win: 1.72 against 1.74 over the same 100 cases is a near-tie, a total of 172 against 174, so the cost-aware policy is not the cheaper policy and is not claimed to be. What it buys there is human load rather than cost — over all 100 cases it reaches the same cost while escalating 43 times rather than 100, at an escalation precision of 0.605 against 0.420. The uniform-baseline gap is also not all machinery: that baseline selects the same action as a plain 0.5 threshold on all 100 cases, and reweighting the case set toward the design’s own readiness prior moves the gap from 0.86 to 1.07 rather than closing it, so the direction is robust to reweighting even as the magnitude shifts. Every missed escalation traces to one cause: the belief under-estimated the needs-human probability rather than misreading readiness. Expected calibration error on that marginal is 0.142 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.100, 0.249]), concentrated in the bins adjacent to the escalation threshold rather than the bin containing it; recalibrating that marginal on the same 100 cases is an in-sample ceiling, and the body reports it as one. Held out, the result is different in kind. Re-eliciting bh from the model’s digit logprobs, fitting a map on 50 development cases and scoring the other 50, improves all three calibration measures named in advance — on those 50 test cases expected calibration error falls from 0.1526 to 0.0696, cross-entropy from 0.8546 to 0.8136 bits, and Brier from 0.2063 to 0.1962. Better calibration does not buy a better decision. The fitted map is isotonic, and the lowest block it pools sets a reachable-score floor of 6/23 ≈ 0.2609, above the 3/13 ≈ 0.2308 a belief must fall below for answering to be cheapest, so the threshold sits inside an interval the map cannot emit: on those same 50 cases the policy stops choosing answer at all, escalation precision falls from 0.667 to 0.463, and recall rises from 0.667 to 0.905. The cause is the map’s range rather than the scores it produced, and a calibration-quality gain that the range prevents from becoming a decision gain is the finding. We also report a failure the test set cannot produce by construction, a high-cost message dropped when it arrived batched with a routine one, observed in a live run. Code and data are available.

title: An Integrated Mathematical Model for Detecting Known and Unknown Fraud Patterns with Optimal Resource Allocation in the Nigerian Social Security System
abstract: Social security systems in developing countries face substantial fraud losses threatening system sustainability, yet resource-constrained agencies can investigate only a small fraction of claims. We present a comprehensive mathematical framework integrating Bayesian logistic regression for known fraud patterns, Gaussian mixture model-based anomaly detection for novel schemes, and optimal resource allocation under capacity constraints. Temporal adaptation through exponential smoothing maintains detection performance as fraud patterns evolve quarterly. Our greedy allo- cation policy, derived through marginal benefit analysis, provably minimizes expected cost under investigation capacity constraints. Empirical validation on 10,000 pension claims from Nigerian state bureaus (Lagos, Rivers, Kano) collected over 18 months demonstrates operational effectiveness. The integrated framework achieves area under ROC curve of 0.811 with precision of 84% and recall of 67% on realistic data exhibiting class overlap, label noise (3%), and missing values (5%). Greedy resource allocation detects 7–11 times more fraud than random selection across all capacity levels, translating to estimated annual savings of 165 million ($122,000 USD) for Lagos bureau alone and 2 billion ($1.5 million USD) nationally. Sample complexity analysis reveals that 1,000–2,000 inves- tigated claims suffice for reliable deployment, achievable within 13–18 months for most Nigerian bureaus. Temporal adaptation with exponential smoothing parameter α = 0.70 maintains stable performance despite quarterly fraud pattern evolution, preventing the 13-point AUC degradation observed in static models over 12-month horizons.

title: Exploring Crime Reports from Social Media Through Transformer-Based Text Classification and Geovisualization
abstract: The analysis of criminal acts is of great importance within society, as it enables the identification of high-risk areas with elevated crime rates. This type of knowledge not only provides insightful information about the safety of the environment to the population but can also serve as a strategic instrument for directing essential resources towards areas warranting attention so that the necessary resources can be allocated. This study delves into diverse data sources, encompassing open data and social media networks, to construct an extensive dataset in Spanish. By harnessing the potential of natural language processing (NLP) techniques and geospatial modeling, this dataset facilitates the classification and recognition of criminal reports made through the training of a machine learning model. To visually depict the reported cases, choropleth and heat maps are generated to highlight regions with a high prevalence of crime. Initially, a baseline was determined, where the two main algorithms were Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest. These were trained with different feature representations such as N-grams and embeddings. Notably, SVM employing multilingual Universal Sentence Encoder (M-USE) embedding attains the best outcome of the two algorithms with an F1-score of 0.78. However, this research also employs pre-trained deep learning transformer models, specifically the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) architecture. Using BETO, a Spanish variant of BERT, this method achieves an F1-score of 0.86, significantly surpassing the established baseline and demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced deep learning models in crime classification.

Notably, SVM employing multilingual Universal Sentence Encoder (M-USE) embedding attains the best outcome of the two algorithms with an F1-score of 0.78. However, this research also employs pre-trained deep learning transformer models, specifically the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) architecture. Using BETO, a Spanish variant of BERT, this method achieves an F1-score of 0.86, significantly surpassing the established baseline and demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced deep learning models in crime classification.

title: Isolating Graph Topology from Model Architecture in GNN-Based Fraud Detection: An Empirical Framework
abstract: Graph topology and model architecture are routinely co-designed in GNN-based fraud detection, making it impossible to attribute performance gains to either component. We address this by fixing the training loop, features, and evaluation protocol while independently varying the graph construction strategy and GNN architecture. Three strategies are evaluated: multi-relation temporal, hybrid structural similarity, and intra-group, each evaluated across three GNN architectures (GATv2, GCN, and GraphSAGE). A feature-identical MLP with no graph structure serves as an empirical anchor. On the Sparkov dataset, all three GNN strategies exceed the MLP by 5.0–9.7 F1 points, confirming that topology contributes genuine discriminative value when per-cardholder histories are dense. On the IBM dataset, the intra-group strategy collapses 6.9 F1 points below the MLP, a consequence of near-empty neighbourhoods (mean degree 1.1) following down-sampling, while multi-relation retains ranking advantages in AUC (Area Under the Curve; 0.985) and Average Precision (0.908) despite marginal F1 parity. Across both datasets, multi-relation temporal construction is the highest-performing strategy, achieving F1 0.908 and AUC 0.994 on Sparkov and F1 0.831 on IBM, though this ranking is not entirely architecture-independent: GraphSAGE narrowly inverts the multi-relation/intra-group order on Sparkov. These results suggest that graph construction quality, rather than mere graph presence, matters more for GNN performance than connectivity alone under the conditions evaluated here.

title: The Effect of Increasing the Dataset Size on the Performance of Sentiment Analysis Models for Tokopedia Reviews Using SVM, Naïve Bayes, and Perceptron Based on TF-IDF
abstract: The growth in user reviews on e-commerce platforms generates a large volume of data that has the potential to be utilised in sentiment analysis. This study aims to analyse the impact of increasing data volume on the performance of sentiment analysis models. The data was obtained through web scraping of 4,071 Tokopedia reviews on the Google Play Store. The data was then processed through a pre-processing stage comprising cleaning, normalisation, tokenisation, stopword removal, and stemming. Sentiment labelling was performed using a rating-based method supported by a lexicon, employing three identical machine learning algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multinomial Naïve Bayes, and Perceptron, with TF-IDF feature representation. The results of the study show that Multinomial Naïve Bayes achieved the highest accuracy of 90.35%, followed by SVM at 88.93%, and Perceptron at 85.46%. All models showed an improvement in performance compared to previous research using a smaller dataset. This study demonstrates that the size of the dataset influences the accuracy and stability of sentiment analysis models ABSTRAK (Bahasa Indonesia) Pertumbuhan ulasan pengguna pada platform e-commerce menghasilkan volume data yang besar dan berpotensi dimanfaatkan dalam analisis sentimen. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh penambahan jumlah data terhadap kinerja model analisis sentimen. Data diperoleh melalui web scraping ulasan Tokopedia di Google Play Store sebanyak 4.071 data. Data kemudian diproses melalui tahap pre-processing yang meliputi cleaning, normalisasi, tokenisasi, stopword removal, dan stemming. Pelabelan sentimen dilakukan menggunakan metode rating based dengan dukungan leksikon, dengan menggunakan tiga algoritma pembelajaran mesin yang sama, yaitu Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multinomial Naïve Bayes, dan Perceptron dengan representasi fitur TF-IDF. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Multinomial Naïve Bayes memperoleh akurasi tertinggi sebesar 90.35%, diikuti SVM sebesar 88.93%, dan Perceptron sebesar 85.46%. Seluruh model mengalami peningkatan performa dibandingkan penelitian sebelumnya dengan dataset lebih kecil. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa jumlah dataset berpengaruh terhadap akurasi dan stabilitas model analisis sentimen

title: Privacy-Preserving Natural Language Analytics over Sensitive Tabular Data Using Semantic Grounding and Multi-Stage Privacy Validation
abstract: Natural-language interfaces allow users to query structured datasets without requiring knowledge of database query languages. Existing approaches, however, concentrate on query generation and execution and offer limited protection against semantic ambiguity, unsafe requests, and privacy violations. This paper presents a privacy-preserving framework for natural-language analytics over structured data that combines LLM-based intent extraction with deterministic analytical execution. Semantic grounding and schema validation resolve the request; a two-layer privacy guardrail then validates the request before execution and assesses the returned result for disclosure risk. Because the model produces only a structured analytical plan, no model-generated SQL or executable code reaches the data. The implementation centralizes model settings and disclosure thresholds in configuration and derives schema metadata from the loaded dataset. Evaluation on a 100-query healthcare benchmark produced 95.00% semantic-grounding accuracy and 100.00% final-decision accuracy, with a mean end-to-end runtime of 3.1152 seconds. The framework provides policybased disclosure-risk reduction rather than a formal privacy guarantee.

title: Adaptive filtering and dynamic outlier rejection for laser ranging target distance prediction and densification
abstract: Aiming at the problems of noise interference and data anomalies existing in laser ranging systems in complex environments, this paper proposes a laser ranging target distance prediction and densification algorithm that integrates adaptive filtering and dynamic outlier rejection. By constructing a target motion state model, employing an improved filtering method, and introducing a dynamic threshold adjustment mechanism and a dual anomaly detection strategy, the algorithm achieves high-precision prediction and correction. The convergence of the algorithm is proved theoretically. Experimental results in typical application scenarios show that the prediction error is reduced by 20% on average, the anomaly detection accuracy is improved by 8% on average, and meets the dynamic response requirements.

title: Maximal-velocity deficit under a finite-support constraint in a hard-wall half-line continuous-time quantum walk
abstract: Continuous-time quantum walks on a lattice spread ballistically and converge to a limiting distribution for the rescaled position. On the hard-wall half line the boundary reflects the walker but does not change the bulk dispersion, so the ballistic front remains set by the maximal group velocity. We ask how close one can get to this front when the initial state is constrained to occupy only the first $M$ sites. We show that optimizing the moment-generating function of the limiting-velocity distribution over this finite-support class reduces to the principal eigenvalue of an explicit $M\times M$ Hermitian matrix, which yields the optimal state by direct diagonalization. For large $M$, a near-front scaling limit produces a continuum description that controls the entire peak region. In particular, the maximal mean drift approaches the front with an inverse-square deficit in $M$ and a constant prefactor $π^2/4$. Numerical results verify both the finite-$M$ spectral formulation and the predicted scaling.

title: Hearing the Whispers: Black-Box Membership Inference Attacks on Finetuned TTS Models
abstract: Text-to-Speech (TTS) foundation models are increasingly fine-tuned on private datasets to synthesize highly personalized voices, introducing severe privacy risks by exposing both biometric identities and sensitive speech content. Existing black-box membership inference attacks (MIAs) follow a two-stage pipeline of query generation and representation engineering, both of which face unique challenges when adapted to TTS. For query generation, dual conditioning on synthesis text and reference speech creates a large and underexplored query design space with no established criterion for identifying an effective query. For representation engineering, the multi-level speech characteristics and temporal variability of speech make low-level representations and direct comparisons inadequate for capturing membership signals. To address these challenges, we present the first black-box MIA framework explicitly tailored to TTS models at both the speaker and record levels. For query generation, we characterize the feasible query space and establish two criteria, scorable extent and memorization elicitation, for evaluating five representative queries, identifying recitation as the strongest. For representation engineering, we obtain multi-level speech representations from embedding models and temporally align the generated and target audio for fine-grained comparison. Evaluations across three state-of-the-art TTS models (CosyVoice2, F5-TTS, and XTTS-v2) fine-tuned on two benchmark datasets (VCTK and British Dialect) reveal severe privacy leakage: speaker-level AUC remains above 0.80 and approaches 1.0 in the strongest settings, while record-level AUC ranges from 0.80 to 0.90 and remains effective even in challenging scenarios where both members and non-members are of the same speakers. We further identify speech characteristics associated with disproportionate vulnerability to memorization.

title: Measuring consistency via ensemble margin and local prediction variability: Auditing decision systems in the presence of predictive multiplicity
abstract: The Rashomon effect is a machine learning phenomenon where equally accurate models produce different predictions for the same inputs (predictive multiplicity). Existing work primarily focuses on multiplicity within individual models, but in more complex decision systems, the impact of the Rashomon effect is less well understood. In this work, we study multiplicity from the perspective of auditing incorrect ensemble predictions, where the decision to divert an instance for human review is based on a consistency criterion that combines the ensemble margin with a measure of local prediction variability for each constituent model. With mild assumptions about stability and smoothness, we show that the consistency scores of finite ensembles converge to the corresponding consistency score of the expected model from the Rashomon set as the ensemble size and the number of samples used to measure local prediction variability increase. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed criterion, we evaluate the framework with respect to transformer models applied to natural language understanding tasks and parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models used for tabular data classification tasks. Our experiments show that ensembling models from the Rashomon set substantially reduces the risk of incorrect predictions going unchecked compared with auditing a single model, while incurring only a moderate increase in the number of diversions. Moreover, the auditing behavior of the full Rashomon set can be closely approximated by finite ensembles of relatively modest size, with the risk approaching zero for some datasets. We further demonstrate that the proposed measure exhibits stronger agreement with established predictive multiplicity metrics than existing consistency measures, providing a more reliable way to capture multiplicity in the Rashomon set.

title: Stress Testing Unlearning Algorithms
abstract: Recently, machine unlearning, the removal of specific training data influence from a model, has gained increasing attention. In large language models (LLMs), unlearning is particularly challenging due to the ambiguity of inputs and outputs. Con- sequently, rigorous evaluation is critical for assessing both safety and utility, and for driving progress in unlearning meth- ods. We identify two key shortcomings in existing unlearning benchmarks: (1) they do not actively test whether unlearned information can still be forcibly extracted, and (2) they fail to evaluate performance preservation on boundary questions, be- nign queries that are semantically close to the unlearned con- tent. Here we introduce WMDP++, an extension of WMDP that addresses these gaps by incorporating targeted extrac- tion of unlearned information and systematic evaluation on boundary questions. WMDP++ provides a more stringent and informative benchmark for evaluating unlearning in LLMs.

title: Drone Delivery Packing Problem on a Neutral‐Atom Quantum Computer
abstract: ABSTRACT We address the Drone Delivery Packing Problem (DDPP) via a hybrid quantum‐classical framework in which a neutral‐atom quantum processing unit (QPU) is used in analog mode as an independent‐set sampler, exploiting the Rydberg blockade mechanism. We reformulate DDPP as a graph‐partitioning problem based on the independent sets (ISs) of a scheduling graph encoding delivery incompatibilities. Each partition corresponds to deliveries assigned to a single drone, with the objective of minimizing the total number of partitions. ISs represent time‐feasible schedules, while battery constraints are enforced through a post‐processing routine. The success of the methodology depends on QPU sample‐set size and quality, with optimal schedules recoverable given a sufficiently high sample count. To analyze the effect of the sampling method, we benchmark the emulated quantum IS sampler (QIS) against a classical random‐greedy IS sampler (RG‐IS) within the same pipeline for DDPP, finding overall comparable solution quality. Experiments on Pasqal's Fresnel QPU reproduce the emulator performance on the tested hardware layouts up to 100 atoms, although a non‐negligible additive gap remains at the largest sizes. The results therefore establish the feasibility of integrating current neutral‐atom sampling into a hybrid workflow, rather than a systematic advantage over classical IS sampling.

title: MedSecure AI: Hybrid Deep Learning Models for Secure Fraud Detection over Encrypted Financial Data
abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial transactions has significantly increased the risk of fraudulent activities, whilesimultaneously raising critical concerns regarding data privacy and security. Traditional fraud detection systems relyheavily on access to raw transaction data, which poses serious privacy risks and limits their applicability in sensitivefinancial environments. To address these challenges, this research proposes an AI-powered privacy-preservingframework for fraud detection that operates directly on encrypted transaction data using hybrid deep learning models.The proposed system integrates advanced techniques from Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning with encryptionbasedcomputation to enable secure analysis without exposing sensitive user information. A hybrid model combiningneural networks is employed to capture both temporal and behavioral patterns in transaction data, improving detectionaccuracy for complex and evolving fraud scenarios. The framework leverages privacy-preserving mechanisms such assecure data encoding and encrypted feature processing, ensuring compliance with data protection requirements whilemaintaining analytical performance.

title: Quantum Correlations: From Full Nonlocality to Device-Independent Certification
abstract: Quantum theory admits correlations between distant parties that are stronger than those permitted by classical physics. Such correlations, which are termed nonlocal, have been studied extensively since their discovery by John Bell in 1964. This thesis makes progress on various aspects of quantum nonlocality both from a foundational and practical perspective. We begin by studying a foundational question on the relationship between nonlocality and quantum entanglement. We show that the strongest form of nonlocality, also called pseudo-telepathy or full nonlocality, can be demonstrated by non-maximally entangled states and prove that all pure entangled states can demonstrate full nonlocality in the many-copy scenario. We also provide non-trivial examples of fully nonlocal mixed states. We then turn to the study of another phenomenon in quantum theory which is essential in almost all demonstrations of non-classicality—measurement incompatibility. We generalise the notion of measurement incompatibility and show that our notion has strong operational relevance: it captures the randomness in the outcomes of an untrusted measurement device against a classical adversary. We use our formalism to derive new bounds on the experimental losses and noise that can be tolerated in quantum communication protocols before they become insecure. We then begin a systematic study of routed Bell experiments, a variant of standard Bell experiments that was introduced to demonstrate nonlocality over long distances in the presence of losses and noise. We formalize the notion of genuine long-range quantum correlations in routed Bell experiments and develop numerical and analytical tools to characterize them. We show that routed Bell experiments allow for the demonstration of long-range quantum correlations at arbitrarily large distances using only entangled qubit states. We then prove the security of fully device-independent (DI) quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols based on routed Bell tests and quantify the resulting improvement in key rate and distance compared to standard DI QKD protocols.

title: Detecting Human Gesture Anomalies to Enhance Road Safety of Autonomous Vehicles Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: This research paper uses Machine Learning (ML) models to detect human gesture anomalies to enhance Autonomous Vehicle safety.Specifically, it addresses the following research question: Can ML models trained on normal traffic control gestures reliably detect anomalous gestures and generalize across datasets?We hypothesize that ML models trained on normal traffic control gestures can detect abnormal poses and can transfer this recognition ability across datasets.This study investigates this hypothesis through three experiments: (1) anomaly detection on a Traffic Control Gestures (TCG) dataset using an autoencoder and reconstruction error as the anomaly proxy, (2) supervised classification of known pose categories to test the model's ability to understand semantically meaningful information, and (3) cross-dataset generalization by converting a Chinese Traffic Police (CTP) gestures dataset to the European TCG-compatible pose feature for evaluation and generalization.Statistical analysis of the highest performing autoencoder confirmed a statistically significant separation of the reconstruction errors between the normal and Out-of-Vocabulary (anomalous) frames (Mann-Whitney U=5,938,675,636.5;p<0.001).The MLP model using MeanPose plus standard deviation features achieved 87.1% accuracy and an F1 score of 0.821 for semantic pose information.In the cross-dataset generalization, the model regained anomaly separability between CTP "inactive" or normal, and "active" or active poses used as proxy anomalies (anomalous poses), achieving an ROC-AUC of 0.727.Together, these results suggest that the model demonstrated a clear separability between pose types, an understanding of pose gesture information, and a meaningful cross-dataset adaptation after calibration.

title: From Layperson to Medical Expert: A Corpus-Based Analysis of Linguistic Variation in Audience-Conditioned Biomedical Discourse
abstract: Biomedical text accessibility is often evaluated through readability formulas, although audience adaptation may involve changes across multiple linguistic dimensions. This study analyzed the Persona-Guided Controllable Biomedical Summarization (PERCS) corpus, an expert-curated, GPT-4-assisted resource in which persona-specific drafts were reviewed and revised by physicians. Following corpus-integrity screening, the analytic dataset comprised 1,984 English-language summaries derived from 496 biomedical source abstracts, with matched versions for laypersons, premedical students, non-medical researchers, and medical experts. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for the repeated-source structure and tested categorical audience differences, ordered trends, and nonlinear trajectories[cite: 11]. Twelve theory-driven linguistic features were examined, with Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level used as conventional readability baselines[cite: 11]. All 12 linguistic features showed significant overall audience effects after false-discovery-rate correction[cite: 11]. Information-packaging measures showed the clearest expertise-related progression, whereas several grammatical and cohesive features followed nonlinear or non-monotonic trajectories[cite: 11]. Differences between the premedical and non-medical researcher conditions were consistently smaller than those involving the layperson or medical-expert endpoints[cite: 11]. In a source-separated held-out evaluation, combining readability with the 12 linguistic features increased macro-F1 from 0.610 to 0.677 and reduced multiclass log loss from 0.804 to 0.664 relative to readability alone[cite: 11]. The advantage remained under length-controlled sensitivity analyses[cite: 11]. These findings indicate that audience-conditioned biomedical rewriting in PERCS is distributed across multiple linguistic domains and is uneven rather than reducible to a single readability gradient[cite: 11]. Because PERCS is a controlled, persona-conditioned corpus, the observed linguistic profiles should not be interpreted as evidence of actual reader comprehension or as equivalent to naturally occurring human audience accommodation[cite: 11].
